Just 64 high school football teams remain in the Illinois High School Association playoffs after second-round games Friday and Saturday across the state. In the Peoria area, only three programs remain.
Here is your Journal Star preps experience for the second round of the IHSA playoffs — your one-stop shop as we look around the Peoria-area football landscape each week during the 2024 high school playoffs.
IHSA football playoffs second-round coverage
On to the IHSA football quarterfinals
Three Peoria-area teams will play next weekend in the IHSA football state quarterfinals: Peoria High, Farmington and Princeton. Here is a look at each of the matchups:
Class 5A: Joliet Catholic at Peoria High, 2 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 16
Class 3A: Lombard Montini at Princeton, 1 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 16
Class 2A: Farmington at Dwight/Gardner-South Wilmington, 1 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 16
Eureka trails at halftime
Reigning Class 2A state champion Wilmington leads Eureka 29-0 at halftime of their Class 3A second-round game. The Hornets have struggled to get anything going on offense vs. a defense that has not allowed more than 18 points in a game this season.
Princeton pulls away from Chicago King
The Tigers have jumped to a 34-16 lead over Chicago King in the fourth quarter of a Class 3A game. Princeton is just minutes away from a fifth consecutive trip to the state quarterfinals, where they will host Lombard Montini, a 14-13 winner over defending state champion Byron.
Metamora overwhelmed by Morgan Park
Chicago Morgan Park has scored 28 unanswered points and opened up a 55-21 lead over Metamora headed to the fourth quarter of their Class 5A game at Malone Field. Morgan Park eventually won the game, 55-28.
Farmington defense stands tall in playoff win
No. 2-ranked Farmington moved on to the Class 2A quarterfinals with a 14-10 victory against Taylor Ridge Rockridge.
The Farmers (11-0) remained unbeaten only after the intercepted a pass in the final minute to secure the win. They had taken nearly six minutes off the clock in their final possession — a drive that was extended by a roughing penalty during a kick.
Farmington advances to the state quarterfinals and will travel to face No. 12 seed Dwight/Gardner-South Wilmington (8-3), a 12-6 upset winner over Elmwood/Brimfield.
Elmwood/Brimfield loses playoff game in final seconds
Elmwood/Brimfield was knocked out of the playoffs when Dwight/Gardner-South Wilmington scored in the final seconds to earn a 12-6 win in a Class 2A second-round game.
Dwight's coach Luke Standiford apparently took a delay of game with his team at the 1 to get an extra timeout. The next play, Dwight's QB found a receiver in the endzone for a touchdown with 2.8 second remaining.
Farmington takes a lead in the second half
Farmington puts together a long drive — capped by a short TD run from Lane Wheelwright — and the Farmers lead Taylor Ridge Rockridge 14-10 early in the fourth quarter of a Class 2A second-round game.
Farmington has the ball back after another turnover from Rockridge.
Metamora-Morgan Park updates: Redbirds in a back-and-forth game
Morgan Park and Metamora has scored a combined 35 points in just 12:15 of game time of the Class 5A second-round game — the latest a 47-yard TD run from Jaiduan Cranford, who also scored the Redbirds' first TD, a 55-yard run. Gonna be a lot of points scored today at Malone Field.
Metamora takes the field for playoff game
Metamora football is dressed all in black for its second-round Class 5A game against Chicago Morgan Park. Kickoff is set for 2 p.m., and Dave Eminian is there for the Journal Star.
Elmwood and Dwight tied up at halftime
The Elmwood/Brimfield running offense has been held in check for at least one half. The Trojans (9-1) are in a scoreless tie with Dwight/Gardner-South Wilmington (7-3) in the Class 2A second round. Elmwood last week snapped a five-game playoff losing streak and now are attempting to make their first state quarterfinals since 2004.
IHSA playoff scores: Who is playing Saturday?
There are five Peoria-area football teams scheduled to play second-round games Saturday: Metamora, Elmwood/Brimfield, Eureka, Farmington and Princeton will play for a spot in the state quarterfinals.
You can check out all the second-round scores and schedule here.
IHSA playoff tickets: Where to go to find tickets online
Looking for tickets? The online provider GoFan is selling digital tickets for many of the IHSA second-round games involving Peoria-area teams. You can click this link to see all the IHSA second-round games available via GoFan, which charges $7 for second-round tickets.
Illinois weather radar: IHSA football forecast
On Saturday, the afternoon temps should stay in the 50s, with some precipitation expected across central Illinois.
Notre Dame season ends with loss at Mount Zion
The Notre Dame Irish jumped to an early lead, but host Mount Zion stormed back behind its pair of Division-I receivers and defeated the Irish 43-29 in the Class 4A second round.
The Irish (6-5) season comes to an end one week after a miraculous 59-58 OT victory against Rochester.
Peoria High advances to the Class 5A state quarterfinals
The Lions offense rolled on with a 52-14 road victory against Calumet City Thornton Fractional North on Friday night. Peoria High (9-2) advances to host a quarterfinal next weekend against a state power — either Joliet Catholic or Springfield Sacred Heart-Griffin, who meet 2 p.m. Saturday in Springfield.
Washington season ends with road loss in playoffs
Washington added one final touchdown on a run from Hunter Reed, but the Panthers' season ends with a 42-14 loss to host Oak Lawn Richards in the second round of the Class 6A playoffs.
Todd Stevens ends his first season as Washington's head coach with an 8-3 record and an unbeaten Mid-Illini Conference championship.
Mount Zion takes a late lead vs Notre Dame
With Mount Zion facing fourth down and 15, Illinois football recruit Brayden Trimble grabs a 35-yard TD catch to give the hosts a 36-29 lead over Peoria Notre Dame with about 10 minutes left in the Class 4A second-round game.
Washington gets on the board
Quarterback Tyler Humphrey found tight end Carter Prina for a 6-yard touchdown reception and TD late in the third quarter to get the Panthers on the board. They trail Oak Lawn Richards 28-7 with about 2 minutes to go in the third.
Peoria High opens up lead
The Lions have extended their lead to 34-14 in the third quarter of their second-round game against Calumet City T.F. North. If Peoria High holds on, the Lions will host a quarterfinal next weekend against either Joliet Catholic or Springfield Sacred Heart-Griffin, who meet 2 p.m. Saturday in Springfield.
Washington deficit grows early in the second half
Oak Lawn Richards continues to dominate the Class 6A second-round game vs. Washington. The host Bulldogs scored on their first drive of the second half to open up a 21-0 lead.
Mount Zion storms back vs Notre Dame
Host Mount Zion has scored 15 unanswered points to grab a 22-21 halftime lead over Peoria Notre Dame in their Class 4A second-round game. Winner here gets either Breese Central or Murphysboro in the quarterfinals.
Notre Dame opens up lead at Mount Zion
The Irish have opened up a 21-7 lead on Mount Zion in their Class 4A second-round game. PND is looking to advance to its first state quarterfinal since 2014. The Irish are coming off a huge 59-58 overtime upset of 2023 state champion Rochester last week in the first round.
Peoria High in a shootout against T.F. North
Peoria High has taken its offensive show on the road to Calumet City. The Lions lead T.F. North 22-14 still in the first half of their Class 5A second-round game. Peoria High is trying for its second quarterfinal trip in two seasons and fifth over the last decade.
Illinois coach Bret Bielema at Mount Zion-Notre Dame football playoff game
Illinois football coach Bret Bielema is on the sidelines for Peoria Notre Dame's second-round Class 4A playoff game against Mount Zion on Friday night, according to a post from WCIA reporter Tristan Thomas.
Bielema, whose Illini are off this week, is presumably there to see Mount Zion's JC Anderson, a Class of 2026 tight end target for Illinois. Also on the Mount Zion roster is Illini commit Brayden Trimble.
Washington falls behind early on the road
The Panthers trail Oak Lawn Richards 14-0 early in their Class 6A second-round game with about half the first quarter remaining.
IHSA playoff scores: Who is playing Friday night?
There are three Peoria-area football teams scheduled to play second-round games Friday night: Washington, Peoria High and Peoria Notre Dame, all on the road. Metamora, Elmwood/Brimfield, Eureka, Farmington and Princeton are scheduled to play Saturday.
Illinois high school football schedule today
The IHSA football playoff kick off Friday night across the state. In the Peoria area, three games are on the schedule including Peoria High, Washington and Notre Dame on the road.
IHSA playoff football scores: Peoria-area second round
The scores are coming in, you can find them all right here. Statewide scores are here.
IHSA football first-round playoff coverage
Watch IHSA playoff football games on NFHS Network
You can stream multiple Illinois high school football games at the NFHS Network. The second round of the IHSA playoffs includes 18 matchups of state-ranked teams, led by Seneca vs. Bismarck-Henning-Rossville-Alvin, Byron vs. Lombard Montini, West Chicago Wheaton Academy vs. Burbank St. Laurence, Crystal Lake Prairie Ridge vs. Wheaton St. Francis, Oak Park Fenwick vs. Downers Grove North and Wilmette Loyola vs. Chicago Marist.

title: State medalist and playoff heroes: Vote for Journal Star high school athlete of the week
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Nominees include state medalists, state quarterfinals and more. Vote now for the top high school athlete this week around Peoria, Illinois.
content:
After plenty of solid postseason fall sports performers over the last week, here are the Journal Star high school athlete of the week nominees for Nov. 4-9.
Head to pjstar.com/sports to vote. The poll closes at noon Friday. Information about the nominees is below.
If you have a nominee for the honor, email us at sports@pjstar.com or tag us on Twitter @pjstarsports. Last week, Max Schmidt of the Peoria Notre Dame boy soccer team was named JS athlete of the week.
Breon Green, Peoria High football
Green combined four touchdowns in last Friday's Class 6A second-round road playoff victory. The quarterback threw for 158 yards and three TDs and rushed for another as Peoria High beat Calumet City T.F. North, 52-14. He finished 9-for-13 passing, while carrying it five times for 72 yards. The second-seed Lions (9-2) are hosting No. 6-seed Joliet Catholic (8-3) for a 2 p.m. Saturday kickoff at Peoria Stadium.
Jerett Fauser, Farmington football
Fauser helped give the Farmers a Class 2A second-round road playoff victory. The senior came up with the game-sealing play in the 14-10 win over Taylor Ridge Rockridge last Saturday. His interception against quarterback Cullen Schwigen in the final seconds sent Farmington into the quarterfinals. The top-seeded Farmers (11-0) travel to 12th-seeded Dwight/Gardner-South Wilmington (8-3) at 1 p.m. Saturday.
Khloe Stear, Limestone volleyball
The junior libero played two pretty incredible sectional matches for the Rockets last week. In Thursday's Class 3A sectional title match, Stear went 20 digs and two aces as the Rockets beat Geneseo, 25-23, 19-25, 25-22. That victory put Limestone in the Elite Eight for the first time in seven years. Stear's ability to anchor the back row came with her 12-dig performance in last Tuesday's sectional semifinal win, 25-14, 25-20 over Dixon.
Emerson Eeten, Illini Bluffs volleyball
The freshman outside hitter provided a huge spark at the net for Tigers in last Thursday's Class 1A Williamsfield Sectional final. Eeten posted a match-high 13 kills in beating Henry, 25-19, 25-22. She was instrumental in guiding IB to the Elite Eight for the second time since 2019.
Maxwell Kirby, Peoria Notre Dame boys cross country
Kirby ran his best race of the season at Saturday's Class 2A state meet. The sophomore covered the 3-mile course at Detweiller Park in personal-best 14:47.7 for a fourth-place finish. He improved 16 places from his freshman season, while helping the Irish to a fifth-place finish as a team. Kirby's fourth-place is the third-highest in program history.
Alyssa Higgins, Knoxville girls cross country
The junior turned in the fastest Peoria-area girls time, regardless of class at Saturday's state meet. Higgins took 15th place in the Class 1A race, clocking in at 17:33.7. She joined Breena Shreeves, who took ninth at the 2019 Class 1A state meet, as the Blue Bullets' highest finishers in the last five years.
Ella Peplowski, Metamora girls swimming and diving
Peplowski was a part of three state-qualifying events for the Redbirds at this past Saturday's sectional. She advanced in the 100-yard freestyle, swimming a winning time of 54.12 seconds. The junior was also a part of two winning relays in the 200-yard freestyle relay (1:39.12) and 400-yard freestyle relay (3:41.12). Metamora went on to win the Peoria Notre Dame Sectional with 256 points, beating out runner-up Moline (228 points).

title: College Football Playoff predictions: Projecting who would make 12-team field after Week 11
author: Ehsan Kassim
description: Who could make the College Football Playoff? Here's how the 12-team field would look after Week 11 of the college football season:
content:
Saturday's college football action featured upsets and wins that will shake up the College Football Playoff field ahead of its second rankings release.
Ahead of Tuesday's second Co llege Football Playoff rankings, a pair of top-five ranked teams lost, while a couple of top-10 teams survived close calls. If the US LBM Coaches Poll for Week 12 is an indicator, there could be massive movement in the rankings, impacting the teams' bids for the newly expanded 12-team field.
No. 2 Georgia suffered its second loss of the season at the hands of No. 12 Ole Miss, which had entered the week with two losses. No. 4 Miami was upended by ACC foe Georgia Tech, ending the Hurricanes' bid for a perfect season. In near upsets, No. 9 BYU and No. 10 Indiana each survived one-score matchups.
Alabama, the highest-ranked two-loss team entering Week 11 at No. 11, knocked off No. 13 LSU to hand the Tigers their third loss and eliminate them from contention. Losses by No. 18 Iowa State and No. 22 Pitt also dashed their hopes for a berth.
Here's the latest CFP predictions after Week 11 of the college football season:
College Football Playoff predictions after Week 11
Seedings are based on this week's US LBM Coaches Poll and rules of the College Football Playoff format:
Oregon*
Texas*
BYU*
Miami*
Ohio State
Tennessee
Penn State
Indiana
Notre Dame
Alabama
Georgia
Boise State**
*Receives first-round bye, automatic bid
**Receives automatic bid
Following Georgia's loss, the Bulldogs drop out of the top four and potentially lose a first-round bye. Texas, which lost to Georgia on Oct. 19, is now in the driver's seat to claim the SEC's automatic bid. Despite their win over the Bulldogs, the Rebels are just outside the playoff field due to how the rankings sit.
Oregon remains one of four unbeaten teams, while Miami remains in the top four despite a loss because it is the best team in the ACC. Boise State remains in a good spot to secure the No. 12 seed as the fifth-highest-ranked conference champion.
Ohio State's win over Purdue ensured it remained in the No. 5 position. Despite Alabama's road blowout over LSU, the Crimson Tide only rose one spot in the projections due to its two losses. The Bulldogs fall to No. 11 and still have a great shot at making the field.
Projected CFP bracket after Week 10
Here's what the first-round matchups would be like if the 2024 college football season were to end today:
No. 5 Ohio State vs. No. 12 Boise State
No. 6 Tennessee vs. No. 11 Georgia
No. 7 Penn State vs. No. 10 Alabama
No. 8 Indiana vs. No. 9 Notre Dame
Interestingly, No. 6 Tennessee is scheduled to play No. 11 Georgia in Athens, Georgia, this week, ensuring one of these teams could fall out of the rankings or rise further with a win.
From there, the winner of Ohio State-Boise State would play No. 4 Miami in the quarterfinals, while the winner of Georgia-Tennessee would face No. 3 BYU. No. 2 Texas would play the winner of Penn State-Alabama and No. 1 overall seed Oregon would take on the winner of No. 8 Indiana and No. 9 Notre Dame.
College Football Playoff dates, schedule
The College Football Playoff will kick off with first-round games between Friday, Dec. 20, and Saturday, Dec. 21. This year's national championship is scheduled for Monday, Jan. 20, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta.
Here is a complete list of dates for the College Football Playoff:
First round: Friday, Dec. 20-Saturday, Dec. 21
Quarterfinals: Tuesday, Dec. 31-Wednesday, Jan. 1
Semifinals: Thursday, Jan. 9-Friday, Jan. 10
National Championship: Monday, Jan. 20

The second of the six College Football Playoff rankings will air on ESPN on Tuesday, Nov. 12, at 8:30 p.m. ET. The second rankings will be revealed between college basketball games in the Champions Classic.

title: CFP rankings live updates: How many Big Ten teams made second playoff bracket
author: John Leuzzi
description: The Big Ten landed four teams in the second CFP rankings of the 2024 season. Here's a rundown of who's in, who's out, the full playoff bracket and the top 25 rankings.
content:
The second College Football Playoff rankings of the college football season are in the books.
And the Big Ten conference made quite the statement.
If Tuesday's CFP rankings unveiling would have been the final rankings by the CFP selection committee, the Big Ten would have four of the top five spots in the CFP top 25 and would be hosting three of the four newly added first-round games.

title: These holiday boxes offer a taste of Illinois. See what's inside
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: The Illinois Department of Agriculture is offering shoppers a taste of Illinois this holiday season with a newly-launched gift box.
content:
The Illinois Department of Agriculture is offering for the first time an Illinois Product Holiday Box, an exclusive collection featuring nine curated items from Illinois businesses.
'The Illinois Product Holiday Box is a wonderful way to share a taste of Illinois this season,' IDOA director Jerry Costello II said in a release. 'Our team has made it easy to shop local and support Illinois businesses with this one-size-fits-all gift.'
What's in the Illinois Product Holiday Box?
Each box includes the following local products, including where it is from:
B's Gourmet Nuts – Cashews from Winnetka.
Creekstone Kettle Works – Sea salt caramel popcorn from Raymond.
Fire Department Coffee – Original medium roast ground coffee from Rockford.
Bee-utiful Honey & Candles – Christmas tree beeswax candle from Chicago
Fired Up Jellies and Jams – Strawberry habanero jelly from Carbondale.
Garlic Breath Farms – Garlic Goddess hot sauce from Elburn.
Turasky Meats – BBQ, teriyaki and original snack sticks from Springfield.
Riley's Seasoning – Salt-free all-purpose seasoning from Pike County.
Umland's Crunchy Cheese – Cheddar crunchy cheese from Carlock.
All items are either certified Illinois Products, Illinois Grown, or Homegrown by Heroes products. The Illinois Product logo identifies products that are produced, processed, packaged or headquartered in Illinois. Illinois Grown products contain at least one ingredient grown in Illinois. Homegrown by Heroes logo identifies veteran-produced agricultural products.
Each box also contains two complimentary tickets to the Illinois Product Expo March 1 and 2, 2025, in Springfield.
How to buy an Illinois Product Holiday Box
To purchase the Illinois Product Holiday Box, visit illinoisproductholidaybox.com. Each box can be picked up from the Illinois Department of Agriculture building in Springfield for $50 or shipped anywhere in the U.S. for $70. Shipping will begin the first week of December. To ensure delivery by December 25, orders should be placed no later than December 13.

title: First snow could be headed for central Illinois next week. Here's what the forecast says
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Temperatures will be warm to start the week, but colder weather and snow chances will follow.
content:
Temperatures in central Illinois are expected to drop dramatically beginning Wednesday, Nov. 20, and might be accompanied by snow.
The Weather Channel expects high and low temperatures to drop from a high of 61 and a low of 40 on Tuesday to a high of 43 and a low of 31 on Wednesday, with morning rain showers and a 40% chance of late-night snow on Wednesday, with accumulations of less than one inch.
If that accumulation reaches one-tenth inch, it would precede the historical average of measurable snowfall, which occurs on Nov. 26.
John Bumgardner, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service office in Lincoln, confirmed the snow forecast and added some details about its depth.
"There is roughly a 40% chance of snow mixing in with rain on Wednesday night," he said. "There is a 30 percent chance of accumulation of an inch or more by Thursday afternoon."

title: Mark your calendars: Illinois State Fair announces first two headliners for 2025
author: Tom Ackerman
description: Thinking of heading to the 2025 Illinois State Fair? The first two music headliners have been announced. Here's what you need to know.
content:
Show Caption
We know what you're thinking: didn't the Illinois State Fair just end? Yes, the annual fair ended in August, but it's never too early to start thinking the 2025 Illinois State Fair.
State fair organizers are thinking the same thing, it's why the state fair already announced two headliners for next year's fair.
Here's what you need to know.
Who are the two headliners?
State fair organizers announced country star Megan Moroney and music group Def Leppard will be performing at the 2025 Illinois State Fair.
How much are the tickets?
Tickets for Def Leppard range from $85 to $115, and after the new year will range from $85 to $125.
Tickets for Megan Moroney range from $47 to $122.
Why did they announce the act so early?
The move comes from thinking outside of the box to provide fairgoers a chance to get discounted rates during the holiday season, said Illinois State Fair Manager Rebecca Clark.
Why are these acts appealing to fair organizers?
The fair aims to book acts that appeal to everyone, Clark said.
'Def leopard has a catalog that's spans so many years, and it has so many cross generational appeals,' she said.
On Moroney, organizers shared that the fair has a long tradition of showcasing artists early in their careers. "She has a bright future in Country music," stated Illinois Department of Agriculture Director Jerry Costello II.
When can I get a ticket?
Tickets for both acts will be on sale Saturday morning.
Where can I get a ticket?
Tickets can be purchased at ticketmaster.com.
Lil Wayne, Keith Urban, the Jonas Brothers, Motley Crue, and Jordan Davis headlined, among other big names. Lil Wayne broke the attendance record by selling more than 15,000 tickets.

title: What is the Thanksgiving weather forecast for Illinois? Here's what the experts are saying
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Here is what weather watchers expect for Thanksgiving this year in Illinois and the Midwest.
content:
Like Thanksgiving side dishes, holiday weather outlooks are varied. Here's what some forecasters are predicting for Illinois.
What is the Farmers' Almanac Thanksgiving forecast?
In the Farmers' Almanac 's Great Lakes, Ohio Valley & Midwest zone, which includes the Prairie State, the overall outlook for Thursday, Nov. 28, is "Rain and wet snow Thanksgiving. Colder."
What does the Old Farmer's Almanac predict?
The rival Old Farmer's Almanac divides Illinois into two separate zones. Peoria is roughly on the border of those regions. The Old Farmer expects eastern Illinois to see a mix of sunshine and rain, with varying temperatures. For western Illinois, the almanac predicts sunshine and mild temperatures.
What does the National Weather Service expect?
The National Weather Service office in Lincoln does not yet have an official forecast for Thanksgiving Day.
However, meteorologist Mike Albano said the NWS does have some data that extends out that far. He said temperatures are expected to be seasonable, with highs in the mid- to upper 40s and lows in the mid-30s. Those would be slightly above normal. He said there was about a 30 percent chance of precipitation — "the rain variety." But he added, "There is a non-zero chance of snow — about 10 percent."
What is Peoria's Thanksgiving weather history?
The National Weather Service has tracked Peoria Thanksgiving data since 1883. Some highlights:
Normal high and low temperatures: 47/30
Warmest high: 68 in 1915
Coldest low: minus 1 in 1950
Wettest Thanksgiving: 1.80 inches in 1968
Snowiest Thanksgiving: 4.0 inches in 1893

title: Here are 11 Peoria-area businesses, restaurants offering Thanksgiving food preorders

content:
Thanksgiving Day is just over a week away, falling on Nov. 28. The holiday is about family, friends and, typically, lots of filling food.
Maybe you are hosting a large family gathering or Friendsgiving, and you need a few extra sides and desserts to complete the meal. Or perhaps, you want to take the task of whipping up a homemade meal off your plate entirely. Maybe you just need a single plate for yourself.
Whatever the case, these restaurants and businesses are offering pre-orders ahead of Thanksgiving Day.
Ardor Breads and Provisions
What they offer: Ardor is offering a variety of breads and baked goods this Thanksgiving.
This includes a roasted walnut, raisin and rosemary sourdough for $8, as well as classic sourdough and brioche for $7.50 and $7.75, respectively. Pastries include cookies, croissants, Danishes and more. Three 10-inch pies − which include chocolate custard, cranberry apple and maple pumpkin − are each available for $42.
Customers can also order provisions, such as a hearth roasted chicken salad or smoked salmon spread.

When is pickup? According to Tock, pickup is from 8:30 a.m. until 2 p.m. on Nov. 27.

The individual meal, priced at $18, includes sliced roasted turkey, mixed vegetables, homemade dressing and gravy, whipped potatoes and a slice of apple or pumpkin pie.
The group meal is $60 and features sliced roasted turkey, cranberry sauce, homemade dressing and gravy and rolls. Various extras − each portioned to serve six − range in price from $14 to $18.

title: Here's the latest on a $44 million justice center expansion coming to Pekin
author: Mike Kramer
description: The construction of a $44 million Tazewell County Justice Center annex is progressing. Here's the latest.
content:
A process to design and construct a new annex for the Tazewell County Justice Center in Pekin that began three-and-a-half years ago is progressing toward a foreseeable conclusion, and the project could come in under budget.
'The Board approved spending $44 million for this new facility, said Tazewell County Board chairman David Zimmerman during a presentation at Monday's Pekin City Council meeting. 'Right now, it looks like we're coming in at just over $41 million, so we're excited about that.'
Tazewell County contracted the Palatine, Illinois-based company Wold Architects and Engineers for the design phase. The Peoria-based firm P.J. Hoerr Construction, Inc., is the general contractor for the project. The contractor plans to break ground in March 2025, Zimmerman said, projecting the annex to open no later than the spring 2027.
The new annex will be a 79,000 square-foot, four-level structure. The basement will house the probation offices and will give staff much-needed additional space.
'They're crammed in the spaces they have,' Pekin Mayor Mary Burress said. 'They're very small cubicles, and I'm sure (staff are) thankful every day that this is going to be moving forward.'
What's inside the new courthouse addition?
The facility's first floor will contain two courtrooms and the Circuit Clerk Traffic Division. The second floor will include the Tazewell County State's Attorney's Office and an additional courtroom. The top floor will initially be empty space that could potentially give way to three more courtrooms. The building's exterior design features red brick and white stone, which Zimmerman believes will make it a good fit for downtown Pekin.
'Wold wanted the red brick to fit in with City Hall and the Justice Center,' he said. 'With the white stone that goes up and down, they're trying to match the columns we have at the courthouse.'
Important security features to the new facility will include a holding area for those in custody and a tunnel to transport them from the annex to the Tazewell County Courthouse without transiting public areas.
Currently, people in custody, shackled together and wearing jumpsuits, are transported from the Tazewell County Jail to the Mackenzie Building, then are escorted to the courthouse basement before riding public elevators to the courtroom. Zimmerman said the system not only creates security issues but could prejudice jurors against defendants.
'If one of the jurors is in the elevator," Zimmerman said, "they could look and say 'Hey, look at that guy in the orange jump suit. He must be guilty.' "

title: CFP bracket prediction: Ohio State rises, Tennessee storms in, Alabama bumps out
author: Blake Toppmeyer
description: Ohio State improves seeding as Alabama headlines three teams moving out of this week's CFP bracket prediction with Tennessee and two others joining.
content:
Losses by Alabama and Ole Miss mean SEC could be reduced to three bids, but Tennessee stands to benefit.
Indiana didn't look like a playoff team against Ohio State, but a day of upsets keeps Hoosiers in the CFP field.
ACC positions itself for two bids, with Clemson knocking on the door for a third entry.
The SEC ate itself whole on Saturday, and after three playoff contenders from the nation's most braggadocious conference went down, the ACC benefits. So does Indiana.
The Hoosiers went from in the field to out of the field to back in the field in a matter of hours.
Let's get to my latest College Football Playoff bracket projection.
Reminder: This is not a projection of what I think Tuesday's CFP rankings will look like. Rather, this projects what I think the playoff bracket will look like come selection Sunday on Dec. 8.
Also, remember: Top-four seeds would receive a first-round bye, while teams seeded Nos. 5 through 8 would host first-round playoff games. To earn a top-four seed, a team must win its conference championship.
1. Ohio State (Big Ten)
The Buckeyes are playing their best ball. They destroyed Indiana, showing the chasm between a top-end and bottom-end playoff team. Ohio State can earn a rematch with Oregon in the Big Ten championship game by beating Michigan. Either OSU or Oregon is good enough to win the national championship, but I can't resist the Buckeyes to win the Big Ten, given how strong they looked against Indiana. Last week's projection: No. 5.
2. Georgia (SEC)
Georgia quarterback Carson Beck settled back into form these past two games. If his turnover woes are truly behind him, then the Bulldogs are national championship contenders. Georgia will face either Texas or Texas A&M in the SEC championship game. The Bulldogs already whipped the Longhorns, and the Aggies aren't in Georgia's realm. Last week's projection: No. 9 seed.
3. SMU (ACC)
The Mustangs have won nine in a row after blasting Virginia on Saturday. Credit Rhett Lashlee for triggering a quarterback change in September. A lot of coaches would have stuck with proven veteran Preston Stone, but Lashlee correctly saw more upside in Kevin Jennings, a two-year backup. SMU is playing like the most dangerous team housed outside of the Big Ten or SEC. Last week's projection: Not projected into bracket.
4. Boise State (Group of Five)
Boise State receiving a first-round bye would be the chef's kiss on this zany season. After surviving a scare from Wyoming, the Broncos should head into this weekend ranked ahead of any Big 12 team. Beating Oregon State would help Boise's pitch for a bye. Important to this bracket format, the difference between being ranked as the fourth-best conference champion compared to the fifth-best conference champ could be the difference between being seeded No. 4 or No. 12. Last week's projection: No. 12 seed.
5. Oregon (Big Ten)
Slotting Oregon here comes off as unfair to the undefeated Ducks, but it's a testament to how well the way Ohio State is playing, and the challenge of beating the Buckeyes for a second time, with the rematch coming on a neutral field. Whether No. 1 or No. 5 in the bracket, the Ducks will be on the shortlist of national championship favorites, but missing out on the bye after a dominant regular season would sting. Last week's projection: No. 1 seed.
6. Penn State (at-large)
A home win against Illinois remains Penn State's best victory, but this season is becoming much less about marquee victories than it is avoiding losses. A No. 6 seed would become golden bracket positioning. Penn State could rest up on conference championship weekend, host one of the weakest playoff qualifiers in the first round and likely avoid a Big Ten or SEC team in the quarterfinals. Last week's projection: No. 6 seed.
7. Notre Dame (at-large)
The red-hot Irish must be on upset alert this weekend at Southern California. The Trojans are 2-0 since changing quarterbacks, and they're 4-1 at the Coliseum. USC's only home loss came against Penn State, so if the Irish dominate, they'd even have a case to leapfrog Penn State, as long as the committee continues to forgive Notre Dame for losing to Northern Illinois. Last week's projection: No. 7 seed.
8. Texas (at-large)
Texas enjoyed one of the SEC's most favorable schedules, but now that stiffens. No playoff contender will face a tougher closing stretch than Texas. If the Longhorns beat rival Texas A&M in College Station, they'll then face Georgia for the SEC championship. Few playoff qualifiers will be as complete as Texas is on each side of the ball. Last week's projection: No. 10 seed.
9. Tennessee (at-large)
Courtesy of Alabama and Mississippi losing, the Volunteers went from being the first team out of last week's bracket to nearly being positioned to host a first-round playoff game. Hosting would be quite a prize for the Vols, who play much better at home. A Penn State or Notre Dame loss probably would lift Tennessee into a first-round home game. That's if the Vols beat Vanderbilt, an outcome that shouldn't be assumed. Last week's projection: Not projected into bracket.
10. Miami (at-large)
Miami's loss to Georgia Tech took some steam out of Cam Ward's Heisman Trophy campaign, but he's still playing as well as any quarterback. He gives Miami a chance every time he suits up. Given last weekend's chaos, Miami might enjoy enough wiggle room to qualify for the playoff as the ACC's runner-up, but it can't afford a loss at Syracuse on Saturday. That's no layup. Last week's projection: No. 3 seed.
11. Indiana (at-large)
Indiana didn't resemble a playoff team in a blowout loss to Ohio State, but the implosion of three SEC playoff contenders should allow the Hoosiers to stay in the field. Indiana will have the most favorable matchup of any CFP contender in its regular-season finale, facing 10-loss Purdue. That's a chance for a blowout victory to calm any committee concerns. Last week's projection: No. 11 seed.
12. Brigham Young (Big 12)
BYU has lost two in a row, and it needs either Arizona State or Iowa State to lose to make the Big 12 championship game. So, why roll with the Cougars? Because, of the Big 12's top contenders, BYU enjoys the most winnable game Saturday, a home date with reeling Houston. BYU nearly rallied to beat Arizona State on the road last weekend. The team that showed up in Tempe after halftime is a team that can win the Big 12. Last week's projection: Not projected into bracket.
Dropping out of last week's bracket projection
∎ Alabama
∎ Mississippi
∎ Colorado
Why my latest CFP bracket projection does not include Arizona State
Arizona State must get past rival Arizona, a team that woefully underachieved. Wouldn't it be a fitting end to this anything-goes season the Wildcats to suddenly get right and spoil its rival's playoff bid? I suspect the Big 12 isn't finished dealing surprises.
Why my latest CFP bracket projection does not include Clemson
Beating South Carolina on Saturday would put Clemson in the on-deck circle for a playoff bid, if any chaos ensues elsewhere. In other words, Clemson could be a Tennessee loss to Vanderbilt away from qualifying, or a Miami loss to Syracuse away from getting a crack at the ACC championship.
Would I be surprised to see Clemson in the bracket? No, but, for now, I can't find a spot.

title: As Clemson storms up College Football Playoff rankings, Indiana better watch its back
author: Blake Toppmeyer
description: Clemson doesn't have the strongest case for the College Football Playoff, but it just needs a case better than Indiana's. And it's getting closer.
content:
Show Caption
Clemson doesn't have the strongest case for the College Football Playoff, but it just needs a case better than Indiana's. And it's getting closer.
Debate could boil down to choosing team with better record (Indiana) or team with better top win, if Clemson beats South Carolina.
How close are Indiana and Clemson in committee's eyes? 'Pretty close,' CFP committee chairman says.
Here comes little ol' Clemson.
Two weeks ago, when a reporter asked Dabo Swinney to offer a pitch for his Tigers to make the College Football Playoff, the Clemson coach obliged, but his heart didn't really seem in it.
Swinney offered some meandering rhetoric that amounted to: Why not Clemson?
The answer, at that time, was that Clemson's résumé didn't stack up with a number of at-large contenders ahead of it.
Since then, the SEC cannibalized itself.
Now that the College Football Playoff committee values Clemson ahead of three-loss SEC teams like Alabama and Mississippi, we must ask with a straight face: Why not Clemson?
If Clemson beats No. 15 South Carolina on Saturday, then the committee will be forced to strongly consider the Tigers' credentials.
Clemson ranked No. 12 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings, released Tuesday. More important than the ranking, though, is the reality that Clemson (9-2) sits as the first team out of the playoff field.
That's not a doomsday placement. Last week, Tennessee ranked as the first team out of the field. By Tuesday, the Vols had moved onto the No. 9 seed line.
A lot can happen in a Saturday, and Clemson wouldn't need much help to get into the field.
But, should Clemson need any help at all to enter the field?
What Warde Manuel said about Clemson
Consider the case between No. 10 Indiana, at 10-1, compared to Clemson.
If the Hoosiers beat 1-10 Purdue in their finale and Clemson beats South Carolina, would that be enough to elevate the Tigers into the field, at Indiana's expense?
CFP committee chairman Warde Manuel can't answer that question, because he understandably won't speculate about what a 13-person committee would do in response to games that haven't happened.
What Manuel can do, though, is tell us how close the evaluation currently is between Indiana and Clemson.
So, how close is it?
"Pretty close," Manuel said.
'We think highly of both teams," he continued, "and as you can see, they're very close in the rankings.'
Tigers fans should like that answer.
CFP bracket case between Clemson, Indiana could get interesting
Right now, it's understandable for Indiana to be ahead of Clemson.
While the Hoosiers lack a marquee victory, their only loss came on the road at No. 2 Ohio State.
Clemson lost at home to Louisville. The Cardinals have seven wins but aren't ranked. The Tigers also lost in the season opener against Georgia. Like Indiana, Clemson lacks for a defining victory.
The conversation changes, though, if Clemson beats South Carolina. That would give the Tigers a better win than anything on the Hoosiers' résumé.
True, Clemson would have an extra loss compared to Indiana, but shouldn't the Tigers earn credit for scheduling tough non-conference opponents?
The Tigers have 10 Power Four opponents on their schedule. Indiana has nine, canceled Louisville in favor of Western Illinois, and didn't play a single game against an opponent from the SEC, ACC or Big 12.
Too bad Clemson couldn't cancel Louisville for Western Illinois.
Clemson can't count Louisville as a good loss. It's not. It's a home loss to an unranked foe. And, the Tigers avoided the ACC's top playoff contenders, Miami and SMU.
Clemson is 1-2 against teams that currently boast a winning record. Indiana is 3-1 against teams with winning records but hasn't beaten anyone that's better than 6-5. Neither built an unassailable playoff case, and perhaps the better debate here is whether the committee got it wrong by ranking Clemson ahead of Alabama and Ole Miss, which have an additional loss but better wins.
The committee made its call on that front, and if Clemson beats the Gamecocks, there would be no argument to reverse course and slide it behind Alabama or Ole Miss.
Considering what the committee thinks of three-loss teams – it doesn't like them – Clemson doesn't need an ironclad playoff case. It just needs one that's better than Indiana's, and it's getting closer.
If Indiana had scheduled Georgia for its season opener, like Clemson did, and Clemson scheduled Florida International, like Indiana did, I suspect we wouldn't be having this conversation, because the Tigers would be ranked ahead of the Hoosiers.
How much would the committee value an 11-win team from the Big Ten, compared to a 10-win ACC team that played 10 Power Four opponents, including two ranked SEC teams?
Again, don't expect Manuel to project on hypotheticals.
"We don't project, but winning always helps," Manuel said.
And winning against a quality opponent like South Carolina should help Clemson more than beating clueless Purdue would aid Indiana.

title: UCLA takes top spot in latest USA TODAY Big Ten women's basketball power rankings
author: Dargan Southard
description: The Bruins' big win over South Carolina, coupled with USC's loss to Notre Dame, creates a change up top.
content:
Show Caption
A slew of interesting results in big ranked matchups and Thanksgiving tournaments have caused some shakeup in the USA TODAY Sports Network's third Big Ten women's basketball power rankings.
Many teams are finally getting tested in the non-conference, with many passing but a few flopping. We're starting to get a loosely established heiarchy with Big Ten play right around the corner.
With that, here are the latest power rankings.
1. UCLA (7-0)
Previously: No. 2
What to know: The Bruins' impressive home win over South Carolina vaults them to the top spot. UCLA followed that up with wins over UT Martin and Fresno State in the Rainbow Wahine Showdown.
2. USC (6-1)
Previously: No. 1
What to know: The home loss to Notre Dame knocked USC off the Big Ten pedestal, but JuJu Watkins and the Trojans have responded since with neutral-site wins over Seton Hall and Saint Louis.
3. Maryland (7-0)
Previously: No. 3
What to know: Maryland keeps right on rolling with wins over St. Francis and George Mason since the last rankings.
4. Ohio State (7-0)
Previously: No. 4
What to know: Few issues so far for Ohio State, which landed wins over Bowling Green, Old Dominion and Utah State over the last week.
5. Iowa (8-0)
Previously: No. 5
What to know: Jan Jensen's first season couldn't have gotten off to a better start. Since the last rankings, Iowa has added wins over Washington State, Rhode Island and BYU. The last two came without starting point guard Lucy Olsen.
6. Michigan State (8-0)
Previously: No. 9
What to know: Another riser this week after Michigan State toppled California and Vanderbilt at the Acrisure Holiday Invitational.
7. Illinois (6-1)
Previously: No. 8
What to know: The Fighting Illini suffered loss number one in a neutral-site stumble against top-15 foe Kentucky. Before that, Illinois added wins over Oregon State and Maryland Eastern Shore.
8. Nebraska (6-1)
Previously: No. 6
What to know: Creighton stuck Nebraska with its first loss in a big rivalry showing. Since then, the Cornhuskers knocked off Kansas City to move to 6-1.
9. Minnesota (9-0)
Previously: No. 10
What to know: The schedule hasn't been super tough, but Minnesota keeps cruising right through it with most recent wins over Montana, Houston and Louisiana.
10. Oregon (6-2)
Previously: No. 7
What to know: Oregon took a tumble this week with a rough showing at the Hawaii North Shore Showcase, which included losses to Georgia Tech and South Dakota State.
11. Michigan (7-1)
Previously: No. 12
What to know: Recent wins over Long Beach State, Belmont and Virginia Tech have the Wolverines rolling through their non-conference schedule after the opening-night loss to South Carolina.
12. Penn State (8-0)
Previously: No. 13
What to know: Recent wins over Marshall, Georgia and Drexel have Penn State right on track with just a few non-conference games remaining.
13. Indiana (4-3)
Previously: No. 11
What to know: The Hoosiers picked up a nice win over Baylor to start the Bad Boy Mowers Women's Battle 4 Atlantis, only to cough up that momentum with an ugly 30-point loss to North Carolina.
14. Wisconsin (7-2)
Previously: No. 14
What to know: Wins over Providence and VCU came after a stumble against San Diego State on Thanksgiving.
15. Washington (7-2)
Previously: No. 15
What to know: The Huskies hung tough with LSU before falling by one point. Washington then rebounded with a cruise-control victory over Southern.
16. Purdue (4-3)
Previously: No. 16
What to know: A rough showing at the Fort Myers Tip-Off saw Purdue stumble against Middle Tennessee State and South Carolina.
17. Rutgers (5-3)
Previously: No. 17
What to know: Rutgers beat Georgia Southern last time out, but all that did was end a three-game losing streak that included home losses to Princeton and Marquette.
18. Northwestern (2-3)
Previously: No. 18
What to know: The Wildcats are still trying to find footing after a 1-1 week saw Northwestern lose to Harvard and bear Loyola (Chicago).

title: The state's top playoff performers in Illinois state championship games
author: Dave Eminian
description: Here are the players with the best performances in the championship games of the IHSA high school football playoffs in Normal.
content:
The Journal Star each week spotlights the top-performing teams and players from weekend playoff games. This week, we take a look around the state with the top performers from the eight Illinois state championship games.
Players from state champions Belleville Althoff, Lombard Montini, Chicago DePaul College Prep and Palos Heights Chicago Christian lead our list of top performers so far in the championships of the IHSA football postseason in Normal, Illinois. This list will be updated all weekend.
IHSA football championship game coverage
Dierre Hill, Belleville Althoff
The 6-foot, 190-pound all-state running back dominated in the first half, rolling up more than 300 yards and four touchdowns before halftime on the way to a 57-14 victory in the Class 1A championship game vs Lena-Winslow. Hill, a University of Oregon commit, finished with 523 total yards and seven TDs. This season, he ended with 2,957 total yards and 49 touchdowns.
Kenny Jager, Palos Heights Chicago Christian
The 5-foot-7, 180-pound all-state running back controlled the ground game for Chicago Christian, rushing for 223 yards and a TD touchdowns on 38 attempts in a 47-7 victory over Maroa-Forsyth in the Class 2A championship game. The senior finished the season with 2,025 rushing yards and 28 TDs.
Nick Martinez, Chicago DePaul College Prep
The 5-foot-11, 175-pound running back led DePaul's run game with 100 yards and three TDs on 19 carries, helping the Rams to a decisive 40-6 Class 4A championship win over Mount Zion. QB Juju Rodriguez added 47 rush yards and a score, while also throwing for 68 yards and a TD. Nicholas Hathcoat added 91 rushing yards and a TD. Martinez finished the season with 1,262 rushing yards and 13 TDs.
CJ Harkins, Lombard Montini
The 6-foot-2, 180-pound junior caught two long TD passes in the first half as Montini won the Class 3A championship, 49-8, against Monticello. Israel Abrams (10-for-16, 225 yards) found Harkins for TDs of 53 and 70 yards in the first half, while adding another 63 yards and a TD on the ground.
Jeremiah Peterson, Lombard Montini
The 5-foot-11, 220-pound senior accounted for 183 total yards and two TDs on 14 touches to help Montini defeat Monticello, 49-8, in the Class 3A final. Peterson ran for 134 yards and a TD on 13 carries and added a 49-yard TD reception. Peterson ends the season with 995 rushing yards and 13 TDs.
Alec Schlichting, Lena-Winslow
The Panthers running back finished with 117 yards and a TD on 22 carries, but Lena-Winslow lost its second successive Class 1A championship game, 57-14, to Belleville Althoff. The 5-foot-9, 145-pound back finishes the season with 1,972 yards and 27 TDs rushing. Backfield mate Aiden Wild added 94 yards and a TD; he finishes with 1,393 and 22 TDs.

title: State records more: IHSA crowns first of its eight football state champions
author: Dave Eminian
description: Highlights, recap from the 2024 IHSA football state championship games in Normal.
content:
The Illinois High School Association football state championships continue Saturday at Hancock Stadium in Normal.
On Friday, four private schools dominated their championship games winning by a combined average of 48-7.
Here is a game-by-game look at each championship game. We will update this story throughout the weekend.
IHSA football championship game coverage
Class 4A: Chicago DePaul College Prep 40, Mount Zion 6
NORMAL — DePaul College Prep made a Cinderella run through the Class 4A postseason, capping its run to Normal with a 40-6 victory against Mount Zion and its pair of Division-I recruits.
DePaul (11-3) won the school its first title since precursor Gordon Tech won a title in 1980. The Rams did it with a run game and defense, rolling up 245 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 35 carries. They also had two sacks, an interception and nearly blocked a punt.
Nick Martinez led DePaul's run game with 100 yards and three TDs on 19 carries. QB Juju Rodriguez added 47 rush yards and a score, while also throwing for 68 yards and a TD. Nicholas Hathcoat added 91 rushing yards and a TD.
Illini commit Brayden Trimble had 40 yards on 12 touches, including a nice catch on a 4-yard TD reception late in the game. Tight end JC Anderson, who dozens of offers, finished with one catch for 11 yards.
Mount Zion (10-4) was making its first state championship game appearance.
Class 3A: Lombard Montini 49, Monticello 8
NORMAL — Montini controlled from the start to win its seventh football state championship.
Senior running back Jeremiah Peterson accounted for 183 yards and two TDs on 14 touches, while junior receiver CJ Harkins (123 yards) caught two long touchdowns from Israel Abrams, who finished 10-for-16 for 225 yards and three TDs.
Montini (12-2) led 21-0 after one quarter and 35-0 at halftime, adding a title in its fourth class. It won 4A in 2004, 5A in 2009, '10, '11 and '12 and the 6A crown in 2015.
Carter Forman had nine receptions for 110 yards and the lone TD for Monticello (11-3), which was back in the finals for the first time since its 3A title in 2018.
Monticello QB Ike Young, an Illinois baseball recruit, was held to 92 passing yards and 2 rushing yards on nine carries in the first half. He came in as a 3,000-yard passers and 1,000-yard rusher.
Class 2A: Chicago Christian 47, Maroa-Forsyth 0
NORMAL — Palos Heights Chicago Christian won the school its first boys state championship, shutting down state power Maroa-Forsyth.
Chicago Christian (13-1) controlled the game from the start, holding Maroa to 72 yards and three first downs.
Kenny Jager led the way for Chicago Christian, rushing for 223 yards and a TD. Quarterback Christian Flutman added 86 rushing yards and three scores. He also was 12-for-16 passing for 132 yards, including a 59-yard TD to Niko Griggs and a 30-yard TD to Jared Hall.
Maroa (12-2) earned its ninth runner-up finish to go with titles in 2006 and 2012.
Class 1A: Belleville Althoff 57, Lena-Winslow 14
NORMAL — Belleville Althoff won its first state championship in more than three decades, easing past Lena-Winslow behind its massive offensive line and impressive run game.
All-state running back Dierre Hill ran for record 438 yards and six touchdowns on 32 carries for the Crusaders (14-0), who controlled much of the game on a cold and snowy morning. He added an 80-yard touchdown reception. His rushing total is a Class 1A championship game record and his 46 points are an all-class record.
The Althoff offensive line of Cam Golden, Broc Rodgers, Logan Davis, Jordan Wright and Patton Leib averages nearly 6-foot-4, 300 pounds. Althoff ran for 492 yards overall, including 230 in the first half.
This is the second consecutive runner-up finish for L-W (13-1) after winning four championships in five seasons under coach Ric Arand. Alec Schlichting led Lena with 129 yards rushing.

title: Tazewell County's board has a new look. Meet the new chairperson and members here
author: Mike Kramer
description: The new chairman presided over his first Tazewell County Board meeting Monday, and five new members were sworn in.
content:
New Tazewell County Board chairman Brett Grimm presided over his first meeting Monday with a newly reorganized County Board.
Grimm replaces former chairman Dave Zimmerman, who announced his retirement last month. Grimm was elected to the position last month after his opponent, former County Board member Roy Paget, withdrew from the race.
Grimm served as a Tazewell County Board member for 10 years before being elected Tazewell County auditor in 2020. He will remain in his role as auditor until the end of the year.
What Brett Grimm had to say about his role on the board
Grimm said in his work as a contractor, he is accustomed to working from blueprints and has been working with Tazewell County administrator Mike Deluhery to develop a blueprint for Tazewell County government.
'We are going to have an outside firm come in and help us with a strategic plan for the next two to five years so that things that were done by the previous board are not lost or ignored,' Grimm added. 'This is not a time when we're going to necessarily change everything or wash it away.
"I'd like to work together with everyone to try to make this happen. They're going to start in January talking to board members and elected officials about how we can make some progress and put this together so we can all get behind it and move forward.'
Other Tazewell County board members sworn in
Five new Tazewell County Board members took their oaths of office Monday: Ralph Deene Milam and Joe Woodrow (District One), Cathryn Stump and Eric Stahl (District Two) and Eric Schmidgall (District Three).
Five other representatives renewed their oaths, including: Jay Hall (District One), Jonathan Hopkins (District Two) and Bill Atkins, Michael Harris, and Tammy Rich-Stimson (District Three).

title: Chemical plant given approval to build facility along Illinois River in Peoria
author: JJ Bullock
description: The company will move its operations from Nebraska to Illinois after debate over environmental concerns.
content:
Show Caption
A chemical plant that Peoria officials say will bring practices that are "sensitive" to environmental concerns will be allowed to build a new facility along the Illinois River.
The Peoria City Council voted 9-1 to allow Viridis Chemical to move its operations from Columbus, Nebraska, to Peoria and construct a new facility behind the existing BioUrja ethanol facility off Southwest Washington Street.
City councilmember Kiran Velpula stood alone in voting no on the proposal, saying he was not convinced that the Viridis plant would be completely safe to have so close to the river and said Peoria still had a lot of unanswered questions about the company.
Velpula questioned the solvency of the chemical Viridis would be producing and raised concerns over what would happen if it spilled into the river.
Eric Lawrence, the plant manager for Viridis, said the ethyl acetate produced by the facility has a solvency of 30%. Velpula, who has a PhD and studies cancer biology and pharmacology for the University of Illinois College of Medicine in Peoria, pointed out that 30% solvency is "still dangerous."
The rest of the council, however, approved the new facility after months of negotiations between BioUrja, Viridis, environmental groups and South Peoria neighborhood groups that culminated into a deal that some felt would be a "win-win" for all involved.
City attorney Patrick Hayes told the council that the technology Viridis uses has an "industry leading" and "environmentally sensitive" process for producing ethyl acetate, a chemical often found in products like nail polish remover. Hayes also noted that the company won an award in October that recognized its environmental practices.
Hayes said the new facility would build business and jobs in Peoria. He called the proposal a "tremendous opportunity" for Peoria.
Peoria has been discussing and debating the merits of the new plant for months, dating back to December 2023 when a new tax-increment financing district was created that opened the door for expansions by BioUrja.
Environmental groups and activists from South Peoria sprang into action, demanding a seat at the table in any negotiations or plans that would allow for a potential polluter to expand or build in the newly created TIF. The groups' original key concern was the potential for a CO2 pipeline to be built at the facility.
The approved deal includes provisions that say BioUrja and Viridis have to stay compliant with federal environmental laws and must annually submit a report to Peoria updating them on their compliance with Environmental Protection Agency rules.
Virids will also have to annually document and publish its greenhouse gas emissions to the city of Peoria unless it does not produce the minimum amount of greenhouse gases the EPA requires for mandatory reporting.
Viridis also agreed to prioritize hiring residents of South Peoria to work in its facility.
Activists went before the council on Tuesday night and commended the city for bringing all parties to the table and working toward a deal.
Tim Berstchy, an attorney who has been working with the activists, said the deal was a "win-win" and Peoria achieved "some level of protections for the community," adding that "the city really stepped up here."

title: Double-doubles and perfect weeks: Vote for Journal Star athlete of the week for Dec. 9-14
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Nominees from Washington, Canton and Morton lead a ballot filled with winter performances. Vote for high school athlete of the week.
content:
After plenty of solid winter sports performers over the last week, here are the Journal Star high school athlete of the week nominees for Dec. 9-14.
Head to pjstar.com/sports to vote. The poll closes at noon Friday. Information about the nominees is below.
If you have a nominee for the honor, email us at sports@pjstar.com or tag us on Twitter @pjstarsports. Last week, Toby Cooper of the Illini Bluffs boys basketball team was named JS athlete of the week.
Gavin Walder, Peoria Christian boys basketball
Walder guided PCS to a pair of victories last week. He scored 25 points and grabbed six rebounds as the Chargers beat Clinton, 63-59 on Saturday. In Friday's 73-32 win over Bloomington Cornerstone Christian, he scored 14 points and grabbed four rebounds. Peoria Christian is 7-3 with two games scheduled this week.
Brady Ward, Illinois Valley Central boys basketball
Ward put together a trio of solid outings at last week's Colmone Classic in Spring Valley. His week began last Monday with 21 points and nine rebounds in a 56-52 loss to Kewanee. On Thursday, the 6-foot-8 junior posted a double-double (12 points, 12 rebounds and two blocks) in beating Putnam County, 55-31. Ward wrapped up the week on Saturday with 14 points, 10 rebounds and four blocks in a 66-55 win against St. Bede.
Cole Dubois, East Peoria boys basketball
Dubois put together two complete games last Friday and Saturday. The 5-foot-11 sophomore guard scored 30 points in a 63-48 win over Mid-Illini Conference foe Canton on Friday. On Saturday, Dubois put up 19 points and three assists, but EP fell to Lincoln, 54-48.
Josie Hughes, Havana girls basketball
Hughes came up big in a tough loss on Saturday at the Abingdon-Avon Shootout. The senior guard dropped 25 points only to see Sherrard win 49-47. Hughes, however, scored 13 points in helping the Ducks to a 56-29 win last Thursday over Lewistown.
Ella Demler, Canton girls basketball
Demler stuffed the stat sheet for the Little Giants during an undefeated week. She concluded the trio of victories with 17 points, 10 assists, seven rebounds, four steals and two blocks to knock Abingdon-Avon from the undefeated ranks with a 57-41 win on Thursday. Last Tuesday, the senior went for 10 points, four rebounds, four assists and three steals in beating East Peoria, 56-44. Her week began last Monday with 13 points off 9-for-10 free throws in a 56-44 victory against Metamora.
Abby VanMeenen, Morton girls basketball - Class 3A/4A
VanMeenen was instrumental in helping Morton go 2-0 last week. Her 14-point effort was a game-high as the Potters beat Metamora, 39-33 at the Illinois Wesleyan Shirk Center on Friday. VanMeenen then scored 10 points as Morton beat Mt. Sterling Brown County, 53-37 at the Abingdon Shootout on Saturday.
Wyatt Medlin, Washington boys wrestling
Medlin won the 157-pound title at the Washington Holiday Invitational on Saturday. The junior improved his record to 17-2 by knocking off Chicago Mount Carmel junior Liam Kelly, 4-2 in the title. Medlin went 3-0 in his pool, getting two pins and a tech fall on his way to the championship match.
Kelly Ladd, Macomb girls wrestling
Ladd took home the 140-pound championship at Friday's "The Munch" Pontiac Invitational. She made a run through the 14-wrestler bracket with three pins. The senior recorded a fall in 4:45 to beat Urbana sophomore Rickasia Ivy in the title bout. Ladd advanced to the championship by pinning Canton sophomore Kennedy Smith in 3:13 during the semifinal matchup.
Drake Shepherdson, Washington coop boys swimming and diving
Shepherdson won two events in helping Washington win the Peoria Notre Dame Invite on Saturday. The Morton sophomore was the individual winner in the 100-yard butterfly (54.93 seconds) and 100-yard breaststroke (1:03.21). He was also part of the second-place 200-yard freestyle relay (1:32.86) with Aiden Crull, Robert Spurgeon and Hudson Essig. Shepherdson also on the third-place 200-yard medley relay (1:42.64), teaming with Spurgeon, Landon Boerke and Keagan Boerke.

title: Comedy icon Chevy Chase dines at longtime Peoria steakhouse during visit
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: The "Christmas Vacation" and "Caddyshack" star joined his family for a meal at the Peoria business.
content:
As the Griswold family gathered around the table to enjoy Christmas dinner, they served up one of the many iconic moments laced together throughout ' National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation ' – from mentions of Grace's passing 30 years ago and a patriotic take on the Christmas blessing to the surprise of an overdone turkey.
Comedy icon Chevy Chase – who starred as Clark Griswold – hopefully enjoyed a meal with fewer mishaps when he and his family visited Jim's Steakhouse in Downtown Peoria this past weekend.
Waitress Gayla Ray said Chase and his family arrived at around 6:30 p.m. on Saturday, Dec. 14. The well-known comedic actor was in town for a 35 th anniversary screening of 'National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation,' which was to be followed by a live conversation with Chase.
'I was just super excited to meet him, you know, and I was just really obviously honored to be able to wait on him and his family," Ray said.
Need a break? Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
Chase, also known for movies such as "Three Amigos," "Caddyshack" and "Fletch," had a medium filet mignon with a side of broccoli and baked potatoes, according to Ray.
Manager Kristin Comfort said Chase visited with his wife and kids. Ray said everyone at the table was nice and down to earth, and described Chase as a 'normal, regular, family-type of guy.'
'I did hear him say something to them about that he was just glad that they all could be there for dinner…' Ray said. 'I just tried to give him that time, that space, to eat and enjoy, you know, time with his family.'
Ever the comedian, though, Ray said his family laughed and joked together as they dined next to the fireplace. Comfort said he joked around a bit with staff, as well.
'We put a picture on the table for him to sign for us to put on the wall,' Comfort said. 'And I did hear that he cracked a joke to make sure to hang it in the ladies room.'
Though Comfort was not at the restaurant during Chase's visit, she said her family was 'thrilled to have him.'
'We grew up watching all the National Lampoon's, and he's really just an icon,' Comfort said. 'So, he's really I think one of the favorites that we've had.'
And his visit evidently left an impression. When Ray returned home after her shift, she settled in to watch 'National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation' with her daughter.
Comfort described the movie as a seasonal classic and said it is her favorite film starring Chase.
'I think it's just one of those Christmas movies that people watch every single year at this time, and you just never get sick of it,' she said.

title: Chicago Cubs finally end Sammy Sosa exile after legend's apology letter
author: Bob Nightengale
description: Sammy Sosa will finally be welcomed back into the Cubs family after two decades of estrangement.
content:
The 20 years of estrangement between the Chicago Cubs and Sammy Sosa was wrong.
It was petty, malicious and really made no sense.
Under chairman Tom Ricketts, the Cubs refused to permit Sosa, the greatest home run hitter in franchise history, back into the club's good graces unless he apologized for steroid use.
The Cubs were the only organization in Major League Baseball who took such a stance.
Players linked to PED use have long been punished by the BaseballHall of Fame voters. There has never been a player who publicly tested positive or admitted to steroid use who has been elected into the Hall of Fame.
While they may have been shunned by the Hall of Fame, those players still have been widely celebrated and honored by their former teams.
The San Francisco Giants have opened their arms to Barry Bonds, baseball's all-time home run king, where he remains a hero despite the involvement with BALCO and his personal trainer going to prison for refusing to testify against him. He's in the Giants' Hall of Fame.
The St. Louis Cardinals worship Mark McGwire, who was in the famous 1998 home run chase with Sosa. He admitted to PED use after retirement and is in the Cardinals' Hall of Fame.
Roger Clemens, who was accused of steroid use by his former trainer, remains welcome and widely accepted in the Yankees, Red Sox and Astros organizations.
Andy Pettitte, who acknowledged using human growth hormone after his name appeared in the Mitchell Report, is revered by the New York Yankees.
There are hundreds of players who used steroids over the years and still have fabulous relationships with their former teams.
But until Thursday, the Cubs refused to even extend an offer to Sosa to throw out a ceremonial first pitch or be a guest singer for the seventh-inning stretch, let alone retire his number or permit him in club Hall of Fame.
Now, after Sosa issued a formal apology in a letter to Cubs' fans on Thursday, Ricketts responded by inviting him to their annual Cubs' convention for the first time since he left the organization after 2004.
Sosa, who testified in front of Congress in 2005 that he never used performance-enhancing drugs, made sure not to commit perjury in his apology, but strongly alluded to past transgressions at a time when PED use was rampant throughout baseball.
'There were times I did whatever I could to recover from injuries in an effort to keep my strength up to perform over 162 games," Sosa said in his letter. 'I never broke any laws, bit in hindsight, I made mistakes and I apologize."
Sosa, who hit 60 or more homers three times with the Cubs, and hit 545 of his career 609 homers in his 13 years with the Cubs, was a seven-time Al-Star, 1998 MVP and Roberto Clemente award winner. He hit .310 and averaged 61 homers, 149 RBI with a 1.058 OPS from 1998-2001. Yet, he never received more than 18.5% of the votes in his 10 years of eligibility on the Hall of Fame ballot.
"I understand why some players in my era don't always get the recognition that our stats deserve," Sosa said in his statement."
Now, 20 years later, Sosa at least is being recognized by the Cubs for his greatness, helping fill Wrigley Field and generating millions of dollars to the Cubs during their lovable losing years, helping end an eight-year postseason drought in 1998, and coming within one game of reaching the 2003 World Series.
"We can't change the past, but the future is bright," Sosa said. 'In my heart, I have always been a Cub and I can't wait to see Cubs fans again."
Sosa, who accepted an invitation in September and attended the Club 400 event – a non-profit charity designed for Cubs fans in need – said at the time that he badly wanted to be reunited with the Cubs. Club 400 founder Stewart McVicar vowed to help facilitate a reconciliation.
'That was our main goal," McVicar said, 'for Sammy to be invited back to the 2025 convention, We were offering a free vessel for him to use to get the word out. The Cubs fans still love him.
'I couldn't be happier."
Yes, indeed, Christmas came early.
Now, Sosa has the opportunity to be celebrated and worshipped once again in front of thousands of Cubs fans at their Jan. 17-19 convention.
'We appreciate Sammy releasing his statement and for reaching out," Ricketts said in a statement. 'No one played harder or wanted to win more. Nobody's perfect but we never doubted his passion for the game and the Cubs. It is an understatement to say that Sammy is a fan favorite.
'We plan on inviting him to the 2025 Cubs Convention and, while it is short notice, we hope that he can attend. We are all ready to move forward together."
Sosa, according to one of his close friends, is making plans to be there and hopes to savor every moment.
Forget the Cubs' active player roster, Sosa will be the star attraction, and a reminder to Ricketts and everyone else in the organization of his immense popularity.
He's back.
And this time, for good.

The Rams once again find themselves in the 16-team field of the 93rd annual holiday tournament. Manual, the No. 1-ranked Class 2A team, did not receive a top-four seed. But an opening round win over Plainfield North gets Manual a meeting with top-seeded Chicago Simeon. These two programs have combined for 37 title game appearances and 26 state championships (Simeon 16 and Manual 10). Rams coach Marvin Jordan will his team ready to compete led by a hopefully healthy Bradley recruit Dietrich Richardson along with Joshua Humbles, Tony Bradford and Terrence Paige.
3. Two great tournaments at Princeville
Princeville hosts two tournaments and have competitive teams in both fields. The 96th annual boys tournament is highlighted by top-seeded Brimfield, No. 2 Princeville, third-seeded Peoria Heights and No. 4 Elmwood. The Princes are the reigning champs, while Brimfield was the consolation third-place finisher. This is the second year that Princeville will have an eight-team bracketed event as part of the 13th annual Lee Westerman girls tourney. Elmwood (8-4) is the reigning champion, but Tremont (10-2) will be out to avenge an 11-point loss to the Trojans last month.
4. Manual Holiday Tournament has wide open field
Last year, top-ranked Lincoln, which went on to win the Class 3A state title, met up with second-ranked Peoria High in the title game. It was a matchup between future Illinois Ms. Basketball Kloe Froebe and current Iowa Hawkeye Aaliyah Guyton. But this season, there is no clear-cut favorite in the field. Great individual players have the potential to help their team win this year's tournament. Limestone has Hannah West. Kylie Moeller is the star of East Peoria. Londyn Sommerville should be the catalyst for Richwoods. And Manual has been a roll thanks to the play of Breyasia Grayson and Nyanna Payton. Pekin will use Zoe Kormah. This should make for a great tournament.
5. Pekin Insurance Holiday Tournament gets deeper
This is a loaded tournament highlighted by three of the top four finishers from last season's Class 3A state finals. Top-seed Chicago Mt. Carmel was the state runner-up, while third-place Richwoods and fourth-place Mt. Zion have a potential rematch brewing in the quarterfinals. The Knights have rejoined the tournament after playing in New Jersey last season. Other local teams include Washington, Peoria Notre Dame, Morton and the hosts. This will also be the third year a 35-second shot clock will be utilized.
6. Metamora boys, Peoria Notre Dame and Dunlap girls hit the road
Last season, Metamora made history at the Jack Tosh Holiday Classic and will return this year for the 50th annual event. The Redbirds became the first team ever outside of the Chicagoland area to participate in the 32-team tournament. Metamora then went on to win five games in five days to claim the title. Now, first-year coach Justin Dehm heads to Elmhurst York High School with a pair of Division-I talents in Matthew Zobrist (Bradley) and Jonah Funk (South Dakota) looking to become the first back-to-back champion since Hoffman Estates Conant (2016, 2017). As for PND and Dunlap, these two girls programs head to Rockford Boylan for the 2024 edition of the Reindeer Games Tournament. A meeting between these two teams would be a great matchup of talent between PND's Lexi Baer, Julia Mingus and Emy Wardle and the Dunlap freshman trio of Keniya Todd, Keyaira Haywood and Amiyah Gulley.

title: Which historic teams are headed into the Greater Peoria Sports Hall of Fame?
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Peoria High boys basketball, Richwoods girls basketball and Eureka cross country teams are the latest inductees into the GPSHOF.
content:
Peoria high school basketball made a name for itself in the 1990s, but the talent kept flowing well into the new century.
Some of the city's top high school basketball teams from that era have been voted into the Greater Peoria Sports Hall of Fame in the Class of 2024, along with another championship-level high school cross country program.
Peoria High's state champions from 2003 and 2004 and the champion Richwoods girls basketball team from 2005 will be joined by the Eureka boys cross country teams from 1998-2004 as the newest team inductees to the GPSHOF.
These teams are only part of the GPSHOF's newest class, set to be inducted during the March 29, 2025, ceremony at the Peoria Civic Center. Individuals being inducted will be announced next month, along with the top Tri-County athletes and coaches for 2024.
Here is a quick look at the teams being inducted:
2003 and 2004 Peoria High boys basketball
One of the best high school teams to ever play in Peoria, the Lions won back-to-back IHSA Class AA championships behind all-American and future NBA champion Shaun Livingston. Peoria High went a combined 62-3 in two seasons with largely the same team under HOF coach Chuck Buescher, spending time among the national ranks during its second title run. The teams included all-staters Brandon Lee (Northwestern) and Danny Ruffin (Bradley), along with other starters like all-tourney pick guard Jacob Motteler, big man DeAndre Miranda and wing Dustin Warfield.
2005 Richwoods girls basketball
Coach John Gross and the Knights won the IHSA Class AA state title — the first downstate state champ since Manual won in 1986. Richwoods finished 38-0 a state record single-season win total tied by Lincoln during its 2024 state championship run. The Knights defeated Bartlett in the championship game in Normal behind first-team all-state sophomore sensation Biannca Ward, the Journal Star Player of the Year. Other starters included all-stater Megan McGann, Hanna Reising, Stephanie Cole and Kylee Grant.
1998-2004 Eureka boys cross country
Coach Brett Charlton and the Woodford County school cemented itself as a cross country power, winning five Class A state championships in seven seasons, including four in a row from 1998-2001 and another in 2003. Eureka finished second in '02 and '04. Dustin Franckey won an individual state title in 1999, a year in which the nationally ranked Hornets put four runners in the top nine at state. Eureka had another seven all-state runners during that era, four who went top 25 three times during their careers: Jon Houseworth (1999, 2000, 2001), Daniel Martin (1999, 2000, 2001), Sean Houseworth (2002, 2003, 2004) and Johnny Reel (2002, 2003, 2004) Ryan Chapman (1998, 1999) and Alex Gerber (2003, 2004) were two-time all-staters, while Trent Leman was all-state in 1999.
Greater Peoria Sports Hall of Fame ceremony
When:
Where: Peoria Civic Center
Details: Cocktails at 5 p.m. and dinner at 6 p.m., followed by the induction ceremony. Ticket prices and information will be released early in 2025.
Class of 2024 inductees: Teams being inducted include the 2003 and 2004 Peoria High boys basketball teams, the 2005 Richwoods girls basketball team, and Eureka boys cross country teams from 1998 to 2004. Individual inductees and annual award winners will be announced later.

title: Illinois football brings in another transfer to bolster defensive front
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: The versatile Florida State lineman is the third defender and fifth player overall brought from the portal so far by the Illini.
content:
Illinois football has added another player for its revamped defensive front.
The 6-foot-4, 280-pound former Florida State defensive lineman Tomiwa Durojaiye will transfer to the Fighting Illini, according to On3's Pete Nakos.
This will be the fourth school for Durojaiye, who will have two seasons of eligibility remaining. He spent one season at FSU after stops at West Virginia (2023) and Kentucky (2022).
Durojaiye played four games for the Seminoles with three tackles, one for loss, and a sack. The Philadelphia native is the fifth player to be added to the Illini from the portal so far this offseason.
