title: Four classes, one weekend: IHSA will align baseball, softball state finals schedules
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: The four-class baseball and softball state finals will take place on the same weekend starting in 2026, the IHSA voted during its January board meeting.
content:
The Illinois High School Association will adopt a single-weekend format for its baseball and softball state finals starting in 2026, the board of directors approved on Wednesday.
Currently in both sports, the finals in Class 1A and 2A are held the weekend prior to Class 3A and 4A. Starting next season, the IHSA will consolidate its spring bat-and-ball sports finals to the same weekend, like Illinois has done for basketball and soccer.
'The move to a single-weekend state final format in basketball and soccer has been very well received overall," IHSA executive director Craig Anderson said in a release, "which led our baseball and softball advisory committees to seek out a similar format. I believe this has the potential to create an exciting culminating weekend for both sports.'
Midseason power rankings: The 12 best high school basketball teams around Peoria
Richwoods baseball coach Patrick Hogan, for one, is onboard with the change.
"I'm definitely in favor of one weekend," he said. "I think it is something that kind of brings everyone together in the baseball community for one weekend. ... It's just kind of exciting where the postseason starts the same time for everybody."
Dozer Park, which is home to the Class 1A/2A baseball state finals, is in the final year of its contract. The contract for the Class 3A/4A site — Slammers Stadium in Joliet — doesn't expire until after the 2026 state finals.
Anderson said the IHSA is "open to multiple options in 2027 and beyond." He says it could be a situation where multiple venues within the same city host the four-class tournaments or the IHSA continues to contest different classes at two sites on the same weekend.
As for softball, Anderson said the IHSA has no intention of leaving its current state finals site — Louisville Slugger Sports Complex in Peoria. The contract expires after this season, but Anderson says the IHSA has a "fantastic partnership" with the venue and expects the state finals to stay.
"We believe there is mutual interest from Louisville Slugger," Anderson said, "and the many community partners that help put on the event and expect to be able to work together to make this official very soon.'
East Peoria coach Denee Menzione applauds the move for the sake of continuing to give more exposure to softball.
"I think it's awesome," the 14-year coach said, "that we're going to get a ton of fans in one weekend. ... I think people are going to see all levels of softball at one time. Be there in one place, so I love the idea of one weekend all together.
"I think it (pairs) well with the other sports that are doing this because everybody can go (to the state finals) and watching everybody."
One drawback, however, is shorting the seasons by a week. Both state finals in 2026 will be held on what previously was the Class 1A/2A state finals weekend, eliminating that extra week of the regular season for the large-school teams. This leaves a small window to reschedule any rainouts, especially for conference games.
"Now, we're going to be forcing to get more games in," Menzione said, "in a shortened amount of time. ... Personally, I wish they would have stayed at the 3A/4A weekend, a little bit better weather. But in the general idea of one weekend, everybody all at once, I mean, I know I'll be a fan there watching everybody."
This fall the IHSA board of directors will gather more information on writing a by-law to align the season length of both sports.

title: This new girls basketball shootout is a nod to the past and a look to the future
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Pekin's coach and AD put a new spin on an old event with its 12-school MLK Day girls basketball shootout. Here's how it came together.
content:
A new spin on an old event has arrived on the Peoria-area high school basketball scene.
Pekin is hosting the inaugural Mid-Illini vs. Big 12 Classic on Monday, featuring a dozen girls basketball programs from the two local conferences all playing with a 35-second shot clock. Dawdy Hawkins Gym will be bustling with hoops for nearly 10 hours on Martin Luther King Jr. Day thanks to an idea from Pekin athletics director Cole Stoner and head girls basketball coach Brett McGinnis.
The Pekin graduates were teammates 20 years ago when the Dragons were still a member of the now-defunct Mid-State 6 Conference. They played in the 14th Annual River City Shootout, a Mid-State 6/Mid-Illini Challenge at Carver Arena during the 2005-06 season. They wanted to format the Mid-Illini vs. Big 12 Classic in a similar fashion.
'Kind of drafting off that experience,' Stoner said, 'we thought this would may be a really fun way to bring a lot of teams to our gym, to experience the shot clock, to promote girls basketball … We host so many events here at Pekin High School in every sport and in every area, but one area where didn't host anything was a girls basketball event.'
Stoner says he originally wanted to host rematches of all four girls state championship games from 2024, but he couldn't work out all the logistics. Mid-Illini teams will be the home teams for the event, while many of the matchups were determined by a random draw.
How teams will manage the shot clock
Managing a shot clock throws in an interesting wrinkle into a team's gameplan.
Richwoods has spent the last few practices tweaking the tempo of their offense. The Knights, who face Canton in the 2 p.m. game, haven't played with a shot clock at all this season.
'We've just been working on just game situations,' Richwoods coach Shamar Hill said, 'and getting into our offensive sets quicker. … We've just been preparing by cleaning up some of our offensive sets and just trying to get quick hitters.
'I haven't played with a shot clock since I played college basketball.'
Hill says his players have shown no signs of apprehension about the shot clock.
'We're excited,' the second-year coach said. 'I mean, we get to play faster. That's what I love.'
Dunlap is another team that hasn't experienced a shot clock yet. However, coach Becky Fulkerson isn't too entirely worried about it. Her team faces Normal Community in the 12:30 p.m. contest.
'As a coaching staff, we've talked about it,' she said. 'I mean we're excited to try it. Obviously, it's coming down the pike here soon (shot clock implementation is expected by the 2026-27 season) and we're going to have to play with it all the time.
'It'll be fun for the girls. I don't think there's going to be too big of an issue with it, just because I know that there sometimes some possessions that I don't even know if we have (the ball) for 10 seconds.'
Providing shot clock data to the IHSA
The Illinois High School Association is looking for more data on the girls game utilizing the shot clock, according to Stoner. Previously, shot clocks could only be used in tournaments during the past two years, but a new IHSA edict for this season allows for shot clock use in the regular season if both teams agree to it.
This gives Stoner the perfect opportunity to help the state's prep governing body.
'I'm not sure if other teams have played a lot with the shot clock this year or not,' he said, 'but I think it's more excitement than anything.'
Metamora and Morton weren't a part of this year's shootout. Look for those two remaining Mid-Illini schools to get involved down the road. Also absent are Big 12 schools Peoria Notre Dame and Manual.
'We haven't gotten past this year yet,' Stoner said when asked about the shootout for 2026 and beyond. 'We just kind of want to see how things go and monitor it.
'Will it look the same in future years? I'm not sure. I want to kind of see how this first year goes but we're just really, really excited to bring a lot of really good basketball teams for one day.'
Adam Duvall is a Journal Star sports reporter. Email him at aduvall@pjstar.com. Follow him on Twitter @AdamDuvall.

title: Unlikely friends: MSU superfan invites Mr. Blue Hands to join her for Illinois game at Breslin
author: Nick King
description: After meeting Mr. Blue Hands recently, MSU superfan Janet Alleman invited him to join her for a game at Breslin.
content:
An unexpected display of sportsmanship and camaraderie is taking place in Breslin Center's section 109 just above the two team benches as Michigan State men's basketball faces off against a tough Illinois squad on Sunday.
Spartans superfan Janet Alleman, a retired MSU professor infamous for her dancing often seen on the Jumbotron during home basketball games, is sitting next to Ceasar Perez, aka Mr. Blue Hands, a Fighting Illini superfan with his head covered in orange and blue body paint and his hands sporting oversized blue fists.
Perez, a former Marine and Illinois graduate from Champaign, has been cheering for the Fighting Illini for 20 years.
Their allegiances to their teams are well-documented. Their proximity to each other in the Breslin Center stands is no accident.
Alleman invited Mr. Blue Hands into the belly of the green and white beast.
"Janet is great! It's so cool to see a game here in East Lansing. I'm loving the arena," said Perez as he entered a Breslin Center bathroom to put the finishing touches on his makeup before the game.
"I'm glad we're playing Michigan State earlier in the year because the later the year, the better Izzo has the team prepared," Perez added.
Alleman said she recently met Perez at an event where the two hit it off because they share the same passion of cheering for their teams.
When Alleman learned Perez had never been to the Breslin Center, she invited him to join her for Sunday's game. She's also hoping Mr. Blue Hands' presence agitates the Spartan faithful.
"My motivation is to rile up our crowd," she said.
Alleman feels some good-natured pressure bringing an enemy into her cheering section.
"He's very boisterous," she said. "He's very animated and loud. He's muscular. He wouldn't be afraid of the devil. I just have to out do him. I don't have any tricks up my sleeves. Maybe bring some props?"

title: Who are the best College Football Playoff champions? We ranked them from No. 1 to No. 11
author: Paul Myerberg
description: Since the start of the College Football Playoff in 2014, there have been 11 national champions. Which were the best? We ranked them all.
content:
Ohio State's 34-23 win against Notre Dame in the College Football Playoff championship game will earn the Buckeyes a spot in history as the first champion in the 12-team playoff format. Ohio State was also the first winner of the four-team playoff tournament, so this is becoming a bit of a trend.
But where do the Buckeyes rank among the national champions of the playoff era?
Regular-season losses to Oregon and rival Michigan dent theirds case for coming in atop the list of 11 teams, though the Buckeyes did achieve something no one in Bowl Subdivision history had never done: win four postseason games. That gives them a unique argument for being compared to the best of the best since the playoff debuted in 2014.
The résumé still doesn't stack up with teams such as 2020 Alabama and 2019 LSU, which lead the way in our rankings of playoff champs:
1. 2020 Alabama (13-0)
Led by an unstoppable offense starring Heisman Trophy winner DeVonta Smith, the 2020 Crimson Tide have an argument for being counted among the top teams in modern FBS history. Against the backdrop of the COVID pandemic, Alabama went unbeaten in games against 11 SEC teams, Notre Dame and Ohio State, scoring at least 31 points in every game, at least 41 points in every game but two and winning every game by at least 15 points. This was a dominant group and the most impressive team of the Nick Saban era.
2. 2019 LSU (15-0)
This offense will live in FBS history. Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, Justin Jefferson and others formed one of the most intimidating and explosive groups to ever grace the Power Four. Burrow threw for 5,671 yards and 60 touchdowns and won the Heisman. LSU beat seven ranked teams, including Alabama and Georgia, but the Tigers didn't really take off until getting past Auburn on Oct. 26. From there, though, this team was an all-timer.
3. 2022 Georgia (15-0)
Very close behind this top two are the 2022 Bulldogs, the second of back-to-back championships and the program's first team since 1980 to run the table. Another dominant defense was joined by an improved offense that ranked fourth nationally in yards per play. Georgia beat five teams ranked in the top 15 and put a ribbon an unforgettable year with a 58-point destruction of TCU to become the first repeat champs of the playoff era.
4. 2018 Clemson (15-0)
Until LSU matched or even exceeded the feat a year later, the 2018 Tigers put together the most dominant two-game run of the four-team playoff era, beating Notre Dame 30-3 and Alabama 44-16. Freshman quarterback Trevor Lawrence put himself on the map with an epic game against the Crimson Tide, throwing for 347 yards and three touchdowns. The Christian Wilkins-led defensive line is one of the most memorable in history. Overall, Clemson beat 12 bowl teams but didn't have to deal with the same strength of schedule as the other undefeated teams on this list.
5. 2024 Ohio State (14-2)
Beating Tennessee, Oregon, Texas and Notre Dame should be recognized as the ultimate postseason achievement. Before this season, teams had to win two games for the national title; Ohio State won two, and then two more. When on their game, the Buckeyes were the best team in the Bowl Subdivision and an unstoppable offensive force. But the loss to Michigan is a big part of OSU's story and impossible to ignore. To be the first playoff champ with more than one loss is also something to keep in mind. But the overall road through the playoff puts OSU in elite company.
6. 2021 Georgia (14-1)
The Bulldogs did have the one blemish against Alabama in the SEC championship game but avenged that loss by topping the Tide 33-18 in the playoff title game. More so than the 2022 squad, which had a bit more balance, the Bulldogs were defined by a suffocating defense. Georgia allowed 10.2 points per game to lead the FBS and gave up just 16 touchdowns all season. The offense, however, didn't have the explosiveness it did with former quarterback Stetson Bennett's improvement the following season.
7. 2023 Michigan (15-0)
A relatively weak regular-season schedule that featured just two legitimate contenders (Penn State and Ohio State) and many of the worst offenses in college football docks Michigan a bit, though there's no doubt the Wolverines were a deserving national champion and one of the best teams in program's proud history. The offense never received much credit but married physicality with extremely strong play from quarterback J.J. McCarthy. Defensively, Michigan took care of business in Big Ten play and proved itself by rallying past Alabama and shutting down Washington in the title game.
8. 2016 Clemson (14-1)
Clemson faced a run of solid-to-very-good teams, with 13 of 15 opponents advancing to the postseason. The Tigers played single-possession games against Auburn, Troy, Louisville, North Carolina State, Florida State and Virginia Tech while losing to Pittsburgh, so it wasn't always pretty. But the Tigers are boosted by winning a classic championship game against Alabama with a memorable last-second touchdown.
9. 2015 Alabama (14-1)
The 2015 Tide finished by beating teams then-ranked No. 1 (Clemson), No. 2 (LSU) and No. 3 (Michigan State), and there's something to be said for that. But Alabama also lost to Mississippi in September and weren't always consistent on offense, ending the year 49th nationally in yards per play and 46th in yards per carry. But this group stepped up when it mattered to beat Clemson 45-40 in the title game.
10. 2014 Ohio State (14-1)
The Buckeyes rocketed into the top four of the final playoff rankings by demolishing Wisconsin in the Big Ten championship and then beat Alabama and Oregon. Ohio State gets credit for winning it all despite losing two starting quarterbacks (Braxton Miller and J.T. Barrett) and prevailing in the final three games behind third-stringer Cardale Jones. But the Buckeyes lost to Virginia Tech in non-conference play, needed double overtime to top Penn State and weren't always reliable on defense.
11. 2017 Alabama (13-1)
The 2017 team comes in last as the only champion of the four-team playoff era to not even win its own division. Despite dropping the Iron Bowl and the SEC West to rival Auburn, the Tide reached the playoff as the No. 4 seed, beat Clemson in the semifinals and then topped Georgia 26-23 in overtime after making a halftime quarterback change from Jalen Hurts to Tua Tagovailoa that ended with a walk-off touchdown pass in overtime.

title: 'The turning point': Fans, media, players react to Chicago Bears' hiring of new head coach
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Everyone is on board with the Chicago Bears hiring former Detroit OC Ben Johnson. Well, except for Lions fans. Here's how social media saw the move.
content:
The Chicago Bears got their coach — and the fans are excited.
One of the NFL's most iconic franchises hired Detroit Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson as its newest head aoch on Monday, according to multiple media reports.
Johnson was the top choice for Chicago, which interviewed a varied list of 17 candidates. The Bears had competition from the Las Vegas Raiders and Jacksonville Jaguars — but likely moved to the top because of the promise of rookie QB Caleb Williams.
We took a spin around social media to gauge reactions from fans, players and media. Everybody likes the hire. (Well, except for some Lions supporters)
Bears fans like the move
Twitter user @TheBennettK echoed the sentiment of many Bears fans, who were excited about the prospect of Johnson's creative playcalling. He and coach Dan Campbell helped turn around the Lions offense in three seasons, making them one of the NFL's best with 33.2 points per game (1st), 409.5 yards per game (2nd), 6.2 yards per play (3rd), 263.2 passing yards per game (2nd) and 146.4 rushing yards per game (6th).
"Bears beat the Packers AND hire Ben Johnson?" TheBennettK wrote, "This is the best month of Bears football in years."
Another Chicago Bears fans, @ChicagoAdamC on X.com, got a double dose of good news Monday since he is also a fan of Notre Dame football, playing in the College Football Playoff championship game.
"It'll be a banner day for me, and nothing but good vibes for an entire off-season of Notre Dame and Chicago Bears football," he wrote. "Not something I've ever experienced!"
Bears players like the move
Bears safety Jaquan Brisker called the hire a "turning point," while former Bears linebacker Lance Briggs simply posted"I likey @ChicagoBears."
"This is the turning point. New times!," Brisker wrote. "Let's get it .. #DaBears"
Former Bears running back Jarrett Payton — also the son of Chicago great Walter Payton — loves the Johnson hire, also pointing out the team could bring in another big name to coach the defense.
"I love the Ben Johnson hire, and if he brings Dennis Allen with him, that would be great too," wrote Payton, a sports reporter for WGN. "Allen is a guy who can hold down the defense. Now, it's time to start investing in both the offensive and defensive lines."
Bears media likes the hire
Jacob Infante, who covers the Bears for Windy City Gridiron and Pro Football Network, called Johnson the "best hire since Kyle Shanahan" and a "slam-dunk hire." He also credited the Bears in their swift movement.
NFL writer Dan Pompei of The Athletic, formerly of the Chicago Tribune, says Johnson is a measured coach who will bring hubris and a numbers-based approach to Chicago.
"What can the Bears expect from Ben Johnson?," Pompei asked, "Some things that stand out from my time around him and the Lions: He's low on ego but big on analytics. He thinks creatively and will emphasize the run game and protections. Johnson will have a vision for what he wants to do with Caleb."
Former NFL quarterback Chase Daniel, now with FS1's The Facility and The Athletic, called Johnson's the biggest hire in the team's history.
Lions fans don't like the move
As expected, multiple fans of the Detroit Lions didn't hesitate sharing their displeasure with Johnson's departure.
The X.com account @TheSimpsonsNFL, which posts screenshots from the long-running animated series that correspond to NFL news, posted the following for the Johnson hire:
Another Lions supporter @DetSparty_ on X.com thinks Johnson will struggle in Chicago without the talent afforded him in Detroit, posting of GIF of former Lions coach Matt Patricia and the comment: "Ben Johnson without a generational backfield the best OL in the league a top 5 TE and two top 20 WRs."
He also said Chicago will be "greatest hate watch of all time."
Levi Bright posted @JASF_Detroit on X.com that he's "been over Ben Johnson a little while, but to mentally check out before our huge playoff game then immediately leave for a divisional rival is in such poor taste I'm fighting the urge to say some irresponsible things."

title: College Football Playoff picks, predictions: Does Ohio State or Notre Dame take home title?
author: USA TODAY
description: It's down to this. Notre Dame and Ohio State meet in the College Football Playoff championship game. Who will prevail? Our experts make their picks.
content:
Editor's note: Follow Ohio State vs. Notre Dame live updates from the CFP national championship game.
The longest College Football Playoff season in history is down to one game. Notre Dame and Ohio State are the two teams left standing after three rounds and will face off in Atlanta to decide the national champion for the 2024 season.
It's a surprising matchup given the Fighting Irish entered as the No. 7 seed and the Buckeyes were seeded eighth. But after each convincingly won first-round matchups at home, they then defeated the champions of the SEC and Big Ten, respectively, to make the semifinals. From there, Notre Dame scored a late defeat of Georgia in the Orange Bowl, and Ohio State knocked off Texas in the Cotton Bowl to get to the final game.
While these are two of the biggest programs in college football, both will be looking to end long title droughts. The Fighting Irish last won a national championship in the 1988 season. The Buckeyes haven't captured the crown since winning the first College Football Playoff in 2012.
It shapes up to be a contrast of styles. Ohio State has a flashy, high-scoring offense, while Notre Dame's strength lies with its elite defense. The quarterbacks - Will Howard of the Buckeyes and Riley Leonard of the Fighting Irish - are in their first year at the program and will be hoping to end their college careers with a title. So who prevails? Our experts weigh in.
Scooby Axson
At the beginning of the season, Ohio State was the pick here to win the national championship. So now that they have made the title game, there is no reason to deviate from that prediction and jump on another bandwagon. And because games aren't played on paper, expect the Buckeyes to struggle to run the ball but to test Notre Dame through the air, as that's where they are most vulnerable, and to make enough plays with their skilled receiving corps to bring a championship to Columbus. Ohio State 27, Notre Dame 21.
Jordan Mendoza
The matchup to watch will be the Notre Dame secondary against the Jeremiah Smith. Will the man defense work to limit the superstar freshman and company, or will the Buckeyes make them pay? Two great defenses should make this a low-scoring affair - as long as Notre Dame doesn't break apart. The Fighting Irish aren't able to sustain it, and Ohio State is the national champion, ensuring the safety of Ryan Day's job. Ohio State 23, Notre Dame 16.
Paul Myerberg
Ohio State has plenty of room for error thanks to a more explosive offense and the recent play of its defense. Notre Dame can't afford turnovers and has to establish things up front to avoid a quarterback-driven game that would favor the Buckeyes. But the Fighting Irish are very capable of controlling the tempo and forcing Ohio State into more uncomfortable territory. A low-scoring game favors a team that honed its mental edge in tense and hard-fought playoff wins against Georgia and Penn State. Notre Dame 24, Ohio State 20.
Erick Smith
Notre Dame has one of the elite defenses in the county and the secondary to slow down the Ohio State offense. The question is how long the Fighting Irish can continue to get stops without their offense providing support. Maybe a half? So while the focus is on the high-flying Buckeyes, the story of the game will be told by how well quarterback Riley Leonard and Notre Dame can possess the ball and put points on the board. If successful, this game goes four quarters and has a dramatic finish. If not, it'll be party time in Columbus. Ohio State 30, Notre Dame 16.
Eddie Timanus
Both defenses are tough enough to keep big plays to a minimum. But the biggest difference between the teams is the fact that Ohio State has more weapons, namely the running back tandem of Treveyon Henderson and Quinshon Judkins and a wide receiver group led by freshman Jeremiah Smith. Eventually one of them will break through for a game-changing score. A late turnover will seal it for the Buckeyes once again. Ohio State 27, Notre Dame 17.
Dan Wolken
Even though Notre Dame is capable of making this a game into the fourth quarter, I believe the Texas win was the Buckeyes' crucible moment on the way to a championship romp. They passed the Longhorns ' test, and now they get an Irish team that has been physically beaten up by the grind of the playoff and doesn't have enough offensive talent to penetrate a very good Ohio State defense. This is competitive for an half but becomes a runaway in the third quarter. Ohio State 33, Notre Dame 10.

title: Ohio State finishes the final college football rankings at No. 1 in the US LBM Coaches Poll
author: Eddie Timanus
description: Ohio State was crowned national champions after winning the College Football Playoff and the Buckeyes lead the final US LBM Coaches Poll.
content:
The College Football Playoff championship game left no doubt who would be ranked at No. 1 with the season now concluded. But to put a final bow on the 2024 campaign, the US LBM Coaches Poll panel weighed in one more time to rank the rest of the playoff and bowl participants.
National champ Ohio State, of course, is the unanimous top-ranked finisher claiming all 53 first-place votes. Runner-up Notre Dame finishes at No. 2, picking up all but one of the No. 2 votes.
Texas at No. 3 heads the non-finalists. Oregon, ranked first heading into the playoff, will finish fourth just four poll points ahead of No. 5 Penn State. Georgia finishes sixth, followed by Big 12 champ Arizona State at No. 7. Tennessee, Boise State and Indiana round out the top 10 with ACC finalists Clemson and SMU bringing up the rear in the playoff field in a tie for 11th.
Mississippi at No. 13 is the highest ranked finisher among the non-playoff invitees, followed by No. 14 Brigham Young and No. 15 Iowa State. Illinois checks in at No. 16 ahead of Alabama, which has its lowest final ranking at No. 17 since the 2007 season – Nick Saban's first in Tuscaloosa - and it's first finish outside the top 10 since 2010. Miami (Fla.), South Carolina and Missouri close out the top 20.
No. 21 Army ends the season ranked for the first time since 2019, and No. 22 Syracuse has its first Top 25 finish since 2018. No. 23 Memphis and No. 24 UNLV retain their poll spots after bowl victories, and Colorado hangs on to finish at No. 25 after dropping its bowl game.

title: Ohio State star sends a message for downtrodden SEC after College Football Playoff title
author: Blake Toppmeyer
description: Where, oh where, did you go, SEC football? An Ohio State star sent a message to the rival conference after national championship.
content:
Show Caption
Where, oh where, did you go, SEC football? An Ohio State star sent a message to the rival conference after national championship: 'We beat SEC teams.'
Buckeyes celebrate in Mercedes-Benz Stadium, which often hosts key games involving SEC teams.
Big Ten produces back-to-back national champions, pausing the SEC's reign of college football.
ATLANTA – The SEC played hooky from the national championship game for a second consecutive season, but the nation's most braggadocious conference showed up Monday night in spirit – or in, stripes, rather.
The SEC supplied the officiating crew for the title tilt between Ohio State and Notre Dame, and when the public address announcer introduced the referee and stated his conference affiliation before the pregame coin toss, a chorus of boos greeted the referee inside Mercedes-Benz Stadium, rather than the familiar refrain of 'S-E-C! S-E-C!' that's most often heard in this venue that hosts the SEC championship game.
In the SEC's absence, Ohio State scored a second national championship in a row for the Big Ten with a 34-23 coronation.
Kings of the North, and humblers of the South.
'Everyone says we can't beat SEC teams. We beat SEC teams,' Buckeyes safety Lathan Ransom said.
SEC watching from home 'Priceless' in eyes of Ohio State fan
Buckeyes and Irish fans felt delight in ascending to this stage, but also pleasure in who wasn't here – a representative from the almighty conference that produced 13 national champions during the 17-year span from the 2006-22 seasons. Five SEC programs produced at least one national title during that run of unchecked power.
A photo of a Buckeyes fan began circulating online Monday that showed the man with a red and white wig on his head and a sign noting that his tickets and hotel cost $9,000 but that the SEC watching from home was 'PRICELESS.'
The SEC's stranglehold loosened last season, when Michigan beat Washington in the national championship game after surviving Alabama in the Rose Bowl.
But, SEC loyalists could point to Georgia's snub from the four-team playoff and speculate as to how the Bulldogs would have fared against Michigan.
No need to speculate this season. The SEC was as down as it's been in some time. Notre Dame humbled Georgia, the SEC's champion, in a College Football Playoff quarterfinal.
Ohio State shattered Tennessee in the first round, before turning back SEC runner-up Texas in the semifinals. Including the regular season, the Buckeyes amassed victories against six teams that qualified for the playoff.
The SEC limped away with a 1-3 record in CFP games and a 7-7 postseason mark overall. Not as embarrassing as the ACC's postseason vamoose, but, still, feeble stuff by the SEC's standards.
Even in its absence Monday, the SEC lingered on the brain. Without prompting, Ransom brought up the Big Ten's rival conference during his postgame interview session, and he also steadfastly defended Ryan Day, who went from embattled Buckeyes coach to vindicated conquerer at warp speed.
'We beat undefeated teams. We beat Texas,' Ransom said. 'Anyone want to come for Coach Day's head? Y'all can't.'
The SEC would appreciate Ransom's bravado, if not his sentiment.
Big Ten's elite surpassed the SEC
For a nuanced take in this Big Ten vs. SEC debate, let's consider the opinion of Ohio State safety Caleb Downs, who starred last season for Alabama, giving him perspective on both leagues.
So, how do the conferences compare?
Well, for starters, Downs said Big Ten offenses deploy formations using two tight ends more frequently. Also, aside from Ohio State's games against Oregon, he didn't encounter tempo offenses as often this season.
'In the SEC, there's a lot more tempo,' Downs said.
Fair insight, indeed, but that's a little technical.
Brass tacks, which conference is stronger?
'For a lot of the games, the level of talent is very comparable,' Downs said. 'At the end of the day, they're both elite conferences.'
The Big Ten offered more crème de la crème this season, though, and the Buckeyes smoked celebratory cigars to begin their reign in the building where so many meaningful SEC games are played, while a bitter cold descended upon the South.

title: Emmy-winning stand-up is coming to a Peoria comedy club. Here's how to get limited tickets
author: Mike Kramer
description: Comedian Louis CK will perform two shows at Peoria's Jukebox Comedy Club in April.
content:
Before he became famous, comedian, actor and filmmaker Louis C.K. performed at Peoria's Jukebox Comedy Club.
Now, C.K. is scheduled to return to Peoria on April 5-6, 2025, as part of a tour to thank some of the clubs to book him before he began piling up his accolades. Doors will open at 7 p.m. for both shows.
'I brought him to the Jukebox originally in February 2005,' Jukebox owner Dan Conlin wrote in a Facebook post this week. 'He was 'known' then, but within two years was internationally famous.'
Conlin said tickets will go on sale 10 a.m. Sunday. He also plans to offer 50 tickets for early purchase for each show, available Friday and Saturday night for those who attend live shows at the club.
"There are only 200 seats (for) each show,' Conlin added. 'Both shows will sell out.'
C.K. has won three Peabody Awards, six Prime Time Emmy Awards, and a Screen Actors Guild Award. In 2015, Rolling Stone magazine placed his stand-up special 'Shameless' third in its list of 25 best stand-up specials and movies of all-time. The magazine also ranked C.K. fourth on its 2017 list of the 50 best stand-up comics of all time.
Jukebox Comedy Club is located at 3527 W. Farmington Road in Peoria. For more information, visit jukeboxcomedy.com.

title: Report card time. College football season grades for all 134 teams. Who got an A?
author: Paul Myerberg
description: With the college football season complete, it's time to evaluate the performance of schools in the Bowl Subdivision. Our letter grades for each team.
content:
The year is done. All assignments have been completed, for better or worse. Sorry, but there is no opportunity for extra credit.
Now that the dust has cleared on Ohio State's national championship, it's time to hand out report cards in the form of season grades for every team in the Bowl Subdivision. An annual tradition, the grades consider overall performance compared to preseason expectations, with added weight given to how a team performs in key games against rivals and other high-profile opponents.
Remember that grades are given on a scale relative to these expectations. That helps explain the difference between Marshall and Mississippi, for example.
While both teams went 10-3, the Thundering Herd earn an A grade for winning the Sun Belt, the program's first conference championship since 2014. The Rebels drew a B+ for bad losses to Kentucky and Florida that cost them a College Football Playoff berth.
Similarly, Vanderbilt gets an A- for going 7-6 while the same record earned a dismal C- for Southern California.
Four teams drew the elite A+ grade, led by Indiana. The Hoosiers had the most successful regular season in program history under new coach Curt Cignetti. Four teams landed on a D-, including Arizona and Purdue. And three teams were handed the dreaded F, led by Florida State.
Ohio State earned an A, not an A+, despite Monday night's victory over Notre Dame. That's because of the Buckeyes' regular-season loss against Michigan, which drops them a peg despite the most remarkable postseason run in FBS history.
As with every great professor or talent evaluator — say, like a member of the playoff selection committee — the grades ignore the names and focuses only on results. That's led to some poor report cards for some of the biggest programs in the country.
Dinged by losses to the Commodores and Oklahoma, Alabama gets a C after going 9-4 under first-year coach Kalen DeBoer. Michigan's 8-5 gets a C+, lifted by wins against Ohio State and the Crimson Tide to end the year. Oklahoma is given a C+ after landing with a thud as new members of the SEC.

title: Positivity, planning and growth: What we learned from Pekin's state of the city address
author: Mike Kramer
description: With a busy bicentennial year behind them, Pekin looked back on its accomplishments of the past, but also focused on the future.
content:
Pekin celebrated its bicentennial year in 2024 and looked to 2025 on Tuesday with a State of the City address from Mayor Mary Burress. The event highlighted the city's recent achievements and looked to its future.
'The challenges for our city in 2025, I believe, are still going to be to support and to grow development,' Burress said. 'We cannot make the city grow without a positive attitude. When we have a positive attitude, it's contagious and passes on to everyone.'
Here is what we learned from the State of the City address hosted at the Pekin Public Library by the Pekin Area Chamber of Commerce:
'Believe in Pekin': Looking to the city's recent past
Burress said Pekin had fallen behind on audits of financial records and operations, but now is caught up through 2023. Getting the city's finances in order is important, she said, because it allows Pekin to apply for state grants and federal funding.
The city's bicentennial year also saw a number of infrastructure improvements, Burress said. Rehabilitation of Court Street from Veterans Drive to Stadium Drive is complete, along with repairs to Derby Street between 8th and 14th streets. Pekin purchased 1,000 acres of land to build a roadway that will connect Veteran's Drive with I-474.
Burress highlighted examples of economic development, listing 20 Pekin businesses that either opened or made improvements in 2024. 'Each and every one of these businesses have believed in Pekin and have helped Pekin grow,' she said.
'Making the city grow': Looking to Pekin's future
Burress wants Pekin's future to be a clean one, because beautifying a community begins with tidying it up. She said the city will continue to enforce property maintenance codes. Pekin has also entered into a contract with McDaniels Marketing to promote the city to other communities.
'That is key to making the city grow,' Burress said. 'Market, market, market.'
Bicentennial events last year included a Historic Adventure Quest, performances by the Pekin Civic Chorus and the Pekin Municipal Band, a Downtown Street Fair, and a Pekin Park District Bicentennial Porch Party. Regular annual events like the Pekin Marigold Festival and Christmas on Court also introduced a bicentennial theme into the festivities.
U.S. representative helps celebrate Pekin
U.S. Rep. Darrin LaHood, R-Ill., was on hand Tuesday to present Burress with a congressional bicentennial resolution. He also helped celebrate distinguished Pekin natives such as U.S. Sen. Everett Dirksen, U.S. Assistant Secretary of Defense for International Security Affairs John T. McNaughton and astronaut Scott Altman.
'Pekin is a place where neighbors look out for each other,' LaHood said. "They support local businesses and embrace the community spirit here. Behind every business, street, and school, there's a story of people who worked diligently to contribute to the growth of the city.'

title: Illinois lawmakers file bill to repeal 'Trust Act,' require police to work with ICE
author: Tom Ackerman
description: Illinois Republicans announced they would again try to repeal a law that limits law enforcement's participation in federal immigration enforcement.
content:
Illinois Senate Republicans Tuesday announced they would again try to repeal a law that limits state and local law enforcement's participation in federal immigration enforcement.
Sponsors seek to reverse aspects of the 2017 law that prohibits law enforcement from participating, supporting or assisting the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Illinois law enforcement can currently only work with ICE if presented with a federal criminal warrant or otherwise required by federal law.
Senate Bill 1313 would rather require state law enforcement agencies to cooperate with ICE, 'ensuring undocumented immigrants charged with or convicted of a felony are identified, reported, and deported,' according to a news release.
The bill is sponsored by State Sen. Neil Anderson (R-Andalusia) and was filed Tuesday morning. Additional legislation, sponsored by State Senators Terri Bryant (R-Murphysboro) and Andrew Chesney (R-Freeport), seeks to repeal the Illinois TRUST Act in its entirety.
Multiple bills aiming to repeal the Act were filed in the last two-year General Assembly session that ended earlier this month.
HB4187 was filed in October of 2023 with around 35 sponsors and was referred to the Rules Committee. It would need to be reintroduced in the current session for it to still be considered.
Already in this session, multiple repeal bills for the Act have been filed that have been referred to the Rules Committee.

title: Student teacher arrested in Washington after 'inappropriate' shooting comment on social media
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: School officials said the student teacher would not be returning to Washington District 50.
content:
A reference to shooting a student during a class Wednesday led to the arrest of a student teacher with District 50 in Washington, according to an email obtained by the Journal Star.
Local law enforcement told the school district about the incident involving a female student teacher who was in an online chat with friends on social media, according to the email sent to parents by District 50. Sitting in the back of the classroom, she had her laptop open when a student decided to close it, causing her to be disconnected from the chat.
She addressed the matter with the student, then reopened the computer and continued with her chat. She sent messages to her friends explaining what had happened before asking if she should "shoot" the student.
"The use of that obviously inappropriate language on the social media site triggered a report to law enforcement who subsequently interviewed the student teacher," the email sent to parents stated. "Law enforcement officers quickly determined that the student teacher made the statement out of exasperation concerning the student conduct but did not have any actual intent to shoot anyone or otherwise cause harm."
The teacher, whose name was not released, was arrested on disorderly conduct charges. The specific school where the incident took place has not been released.
The district said it was confident that there was no threat to student safety and no other student or staff member was aware of the conversation. However, it said the student teacher would not be returning to District 50 to complete her assignment.
"This incident serves as a reminder for all persons in the school community that neither violence nor the use of threatening language will be tolerated in our schools," the statement said.

title: Amid social media rumor, Pekin police clarify mission of raid in neighborhood
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Social media claims had circulated that ICE was conducting a raid in Pekin, Illinois.
content:
The Pekin Police Department said Thursday that a narcotics raid at a home in south Pekin was being falsely framed as an immigration raid on social media.
Police said that the raid in question, which took place Wednesday in the 1000 block of Charles Street, was actually the execution of a high-risk narcotics search warrant in collaboration with the Central Illinois Emergency Response Team. The department said that it requested the operation and that it had no connection to Immigration and Customs Enforcement, which had been conducting raids in the Chicago area on the first full weekend of Donald Trump's second presidency.
The department said that its use of armed vehicles and blocking of streets was standard procedure when it came to drug operations.
ICE's raids did not impact Peoria, but they did lead to the arrests of at least 100 people in Chicago, according to local officials, with over 4,500 arrested nationwide as of Thursday, according to the department.

title: Where is the Senior Bowl played? Location, date, time, TV info to watch NFL draft showcase
author: John Leuzzi
description: Where is the Reese's Senior Bowl played? Here's what to know about the annual college football all-star game and NFL draft showcase:
content:
Every year, the sports calendar includes a handful of cities across the United States that are well-associated and identified by sporting events.
There's the NFL combine in Indianapolis, the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, California and the Masters Tournament in Augusta, Georgia.
That list also includes Mobile, Alabama and the Reese's Senior Bowl.
On Saturday, college football's most prestigious showcase is renewed when the National Team takes on the American Team in the 2025 Reese's Senior Bowl at 1:30 p.m. CT at the University of South Alabama's Hancock Whitney Stadium.
The Senior Bowl, which began in Jacksonville, Florida in 1950, marks the start of the NFL draft process for many of the top available NFL prospects. In last year's NFL draft, 110 future picks (43% percent of the entire draft) participated in the 2024 Reese's Senior Bowl.
Headlining the quarterbacks in the Reese's Senior Bowl this year are Alabama's Jalen Milroe and Ohio State's Will Howard. Ole Miss ' Jaxson Dart and Oregon's Dillon Gabriel are also competing in Alabama.
Here's what you need to know about the 2025 Reese's Senior Bowl:
Where is the Reese's Senior Bowl?
Location: Hancock Whitney Stadium (Mobile, Ala.)
The Reese's Senior Bowl will be played at the University of South Alabama's Hancock Whitney Stadium in Mobile, Alabama.
The 2025 Reese's Senior Bowl will be the 76th year time that college football's preeminent all-star game will be held in Mobile. It has been held at Hancock Whitney Stadium since 2021, per its website. It was previously held at Ladd-Peebles Stadium from 1951-2020.
What channel is the Senior Bowl on?
The Reese's Senior Bowl will be broadcast nationally on the NFL Network. Streaming options for the college football all-star game include Fubo, which carries the NFL Network and offers a free trial to new subscribers, and the NFL app.
Senior Bowl start time
Date: Saturday, Feb. 1
Time: 1:30 p.m. CT
The Reese's Senior Bowl will kick off at 1:30 p.m. CT on Saturday, Feb. 1 from the University of South Alabama's Hancock Whitney Stadium in Mobile, Alabama.

title: Former UCLA offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy eyes a return to the NFL
author: Jake Hamilton
description: Following a brief stint as offensive coordinator with the Bruins, Bieniemy is in talks with NFL teams about a new position.
content:
Since the end of the 2024 college football season, the UCLA Bruins have made significant changes to their coaching staff as they try to keep pace in the Big Ten.
UCLA's most notable move to their staff was their decision to cut bait with offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy. In one season with the Bruins, Bieniemy struggled to generate a balanced offense and contributed to some of UCLA's pitfalls in 2024.
But over a month after Bieniemy and the Bruins parted ways in December of 2024, the Bruins' former offensive coordinator is garnering attention in the NFL.
In a post on X from Fox Sports NFL Insider Jordan Schultz, Bieniemy was a leading candidate in the New England Patriots offensive coordinator search and has "spoken with multiple NFL teams."
Though there is no word on which teams have expressed interest in the former college and NFL coordinator, as coaching staffs across the league begin to fill out, Bieniemy should be considered a serious candidate for offensive coordinator openings.

title: Ohio State's Ryan Day 'third base' narrative, CFP expansion lead college football mailbag
author: Blake Toppmeyer
description: The narrative that Ryan Day's career began on third base discounts his achievements. He got Ohio State to home plate. Day deserves his flowers.
content:
The narrative that Ryan Day's career began on third base discounts his achievements. Anyway, he got Ohio State to home plate. Day deserves his flowers.
Deep Notre Dame quarterback competition headlined by CJ Carr and Steve Angeli among top offseason topics.
Brian Kelly headed to hot seat at LSU? Maybe pump the brakes on that thought.
The narrative that Ryan Day's career began on third base discounts his achievements as an offensive coordinator and quarterback developer before he succeeded Urban Meyer as Ohio State's coach. Day earned Chip Kelly's respect while starring for him as New Hampshire's record-breaking quarterback, then caught Meyer's eye as a Florida graduate assistant. Within a coaching industry where nepo babies are unmissable, Day didn't gain that shortcut.
But, even to the extent that " third base" narrative rings true by Day landing Ohio State as his first head coaching job, Day deserves praise for assembling an uber-talented team and bringing the Buckeyes across home plate for their first national championship in more than a decade.
Day's coaching performance remains a water-cooler topic as the offseason uncorks, as does runner-up Notre Dame's outlook and the College Football Playoff format.
Let's answer some reader mail addressing these topics:
Does Ryan Day get too much credit at Ohio State?
Gene writes: I think that Coach Day is given too much credit, except for raising money and recruiting. Having the best talent that money can buy, … he should win it all. … Doing the expected is reason for appreciation but not high praise.
My response: College football championships are won foremost through stockpiling talent and getting the stars to play together as a unit. Nick Saban had a mind for the game, sure, but he became the GOAT because nobody consistently attracted and united more talent than Saban's Alabama. Then, Kirby Smart replicated Saban's success as a recruiter, motivator and developer.
As the saying goes, Jimmys and Joes matter more than X's and O's.
Day proved himself an ace recruiter, before and after NIL, and energizing NIL fundraising now is part of a coach's duties. His persistent ability to magnetize talent made winning a national championship a matter of when, not if.
Day hired excellent coordinators and let them do what they do best while he effectively served as CEO. He kept the Buckeyes focused and motivated after another soul-sucking loss to Michigan. Yes, Day built an enviable amount of talent, but others (see: Alabama, Georgia) achieved less this season with talented rosters.
Day burnished his quarterback development résumé, too, while transfer Will Howard flourished in the postseason.
Discounting Day's coaching abilities because he's a skilled recruiter and he galvanizines NIL is like saying your mechanic gets too much credit, because all he does is fix your car. That's the job.
Recruiting, fundraising, leadership and motivation are college football's coaching pillars. Day became the coach Ohio State needed, because he assembled and inspired an unmatchable roster, much as Smart and Saban did during their national championship seasons.
Should the College Football Playoff get smaller?
Tim writes: I read your column about the CFP. I believe 12 teams are too many. The games proved that to be the case. … Pick the eight best teams and seed them.
My response: The playoff will not shrink in size. Not happening. If anything, it might grow to 14 teams in 2026.
Even if we could wave a wand and shrink the playoff, I wouldn't want to. I like that this playoff earmarks byes for the top conference champions. Byes would go away in a three-round, eight-team playoff.
With an 11-game playoff, you're naturally going to have some lopsided outcomes. That's not new, though. The four-team playoff regularly featured blowouts. The NFL's wildcard round featured several blowouts, too, but I don't detect a clamoring to shrink the NFL playoff.
Fortunately, the CFP games improved as the rounds progressed, peaking with two excellent semifinals.
The first-round format heightens the chance for blowouts because the better-seeded team hosts. That's one argument for keeping quarterfinal games at neutral sites. Playing at bowl sites removes score-tilting home-field advantage.
Let's leave room for a larger sample size before making sweeping rebukes of this format. Just because the No. 8 vs. No. 9 game became a blowout this season, doesn't mean that will repeat.
Is it Steve Angeli or CJ Carr for Notre Dame?
Guy writes: I think you are grossly underestimating the abilities of Steve Angeli, (a contender for Notre Dame's starting quarterback vacancy). We have not seen CJ Carr in game action. … As in the Penn State game, Angeli has shown himself to be a more than adequate alternative.
My response: The Irish require a standout quarterback, not a 'more than adequate' quarterback, to become national champions. More wide receiver starpower would help, too. It's a pitch-and-catch game, as much as block-and-tackle. Virginia transfer Malachi Fields boosts the receiving corps, but that leaves the matter of replacing starting quarterback Riley Leonard.
Angeli probably would offer Notre Dame a respectable floor. The Irish would do well to retain him, but if the Irish are serious about pursuing a national championship in 2025, then a healthy Carr is the choice. He earned rave reviews after signing as a blue-chip recruit. His September elbow injury ended the chance of seeing his abilities this season. Never mind the floor. A healthy, effective Carr offers Notre Dame the highest ceiling.
Ohio State had too much talent for Notre Dame
James writes: You are right on!!! Glad someone said it: Ohio State was superior to Notre Dame with the skill-position guys. Are the Irish just recruiting star rankings?
My response: It's not a matter of Notre Dame being too focused on star ratings. To the contrary, the Irish would benefit from signing a five-star receiver.
Ohio State's top three receivers, Jeremiah Smith, Emeka Egbuka and Carnell Tate, were five-star recruits, as rated by 247Sports. Smith rated as the nation's No. 1 overall recruit in the 2024 class.
Michael Floyd, who signed with the Irish in 2008, remains the last receiver with a 247Sports Composite five-star rating to sign with Notre Dame. Floyd became a first-round NFL Draft pick after a stellar Notre Dame career.
What's the difference between a four-star and five-star wide receiver? I don't mean to oversimplify it, but consider Notre Dame's Jaden Greathouse compared to Ohio State's Smith. Greathouse was a four-star, and Smith a five-star. See the difference? Greathouse is good. Smith is sensational.
Brian Kelly is College Football Playoff or bust at LSU
Tim writes: Full disclosure, SEC homer and LSU fan. If Brian Kelly doesn't have us in CFP next year, look for his buyout!
My response: Kelly crushed the hot-stove league. LSU plundered an impressive bounty of portal prizes – both in quantity and quality – to accompany a top-10 recruiting class. Add it up, it's the best player acquisition haul all of Kelly's tenure.
Kelly's been good, not great, for LSU, totaling 29 wins in three seasons. It's fair for LSU fans to enter next season with a playoff-or-bust mentality, particularly considering Garrett Nussmeier returns as the SEC's most proven quarterback. Kelly's quest will hinge on retooling the offensive line and finally engineering improvement on defense for a unit mired in a yearslong slump.

title: 20 rebounds and school records: Vote for Journal Star athlete of the week Jan. 27-Feb. 1
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Nominees from Morton, Brimfield, Metamora and more. Vote among nine high school athletes this week in our online poll at pjstar.com
content:
After plenty of solid winter sports performers over the last week, here are the Journal Star high school athlete of the week nominees for Jan. 27-Feb. 1.
Head to pjstar.com/sports to vote. The poll closes at noon Friday. Information about the nominees is below.
If you have a nominee for the honor, email us at sports@pjstar.com or tag us on Twitter @pjstarsports. Last week, Maddy Stephens of the Illini Bluffs girls basketball team was named JS athlete of the week.
Brady Johnson, Brimfield boys basketball - Class 1A
The senior helped Brimfield extend its win streak to four thanks to a pair of victories last week. Johnson helped avenge an earlier-season loss to Illini Bluffs last Tuesday. He scored 24 points to go with five rebounds and three assists to beat IB, 58-52. In Friday's 58-42 win against West Prairie, Johnson went for 17 points, five rebounds and three assists.
Boston Smith, Farmington boys basketball - Class 2A
Smith continues his high-scoring output with three solid games last week. His week began last Monday with 20 points, nine rebounds and two assists in a 50-41 loss to Aledo Mercer County. He then scored 24 points last Tuesday in a 61-24 win against Lewistown. The junior wrapped up his week on Saturday, putting up 25 points with six rebounds and two steals in a 46-44 loss to Kewanee.
Quinton Kitt, East Peoria boys basketball - Class 3A/4A
Kitt posted an impressive stat line in a revenge win over Dunlap. On Friday, the sophomore scored 32 points and grabbed 20 rebounds to beat Dunlap, 71-65. He was a part of a 21-for-24 effort from the free-throw in the fourth quarter. Kitt put up 29 points last Tuesday as EP lost to Canton, 64-62. Kitt finished his week on Saturday with nine points as Alton defeated the Raiders, 54-25.
Bri Harms, Roanoke-Benson girls basketball - Class 1A
Harms came off an injury last week and helped R-B make school history. She scored 17 points as the Rockets beat Henry, 46-35 last Monday, giving R-B its first 20-win season in program history. The junior point guard continued her offensive tear on Thursday, putting up 27 points in a 47-37 win over Seneca. Harms ended her week with a 30-point effort on Saturday as R-B rallied from a halftime deficit to grab a 61-52 win over Fieldcrest.
Macy Gochanour, Fieldcrest girls basketball - Class 2A
Gochanour turned out three 20-point games last week. Last Monday, the junior scored 26 points in taking down Lexington, 59-47. Despite two losses later in the week, Gochanour went for 29 points as El Paso-Gridley beat Fieldcrest, 68-52. She then scored 21 points on Saturday as Roanoke-Benson came from behind for a 61-52 victory over the Knights.
Paige Selke, Morton girls basketball - Class 3A/4A
The sophomore has been instrumental in helping Morton run its win streak to nine in a row. Her 23 points on Saturday lifted the Potters to a 61-49 win over Limestone. She scored 13 of those points in the second quarter. This came after Selke scored 14 points on Friday night to beat Pekin, 57-34. Her week started with seven points as Morton knocked off Normal West, 48-27, last Tuesday.
Bowden Delaney, Tremont boys wrestling
The senior cruised through the 165-pound bracket at the Heart of Illinois Conference Tournament on Saturday at Deer Creek-Mackinaw. Delaney (42-2) recorded three pins en route to the HOI championship. He pinned El Paso-Gridley sophomore Braden Gibson in 1:59. That was the third of three pins Delaney had in under two minutes. Those trio of pins helped put Delaney as third all-time in IHSA history with 129 career pins.

The senior was dominant in her run to a 130-pound regional championship at Jacksonville on Saturday. Smith (37-3) capped her day with a 1:28 pin over Erie junior Michelle Naftzger in the title match. In the semifinals, Smith posted a 1:04 win over Galesburg junior Dai Driana. Smith's victory helped the Little Giants (137.5 points) finish second to regional team winner Geneseo (183 points).

title: Metamora man dies after falling through ice while fishing on lake, coroner says
author: Zach Roth
description: Two men were pulled from the icy waters and taken to hospitals, according to the McLean County Sheriff's Office.
content:
Show Caption
A Metamora man died Sunday after he drowned in a lake in McLean County while ice fishing.
Jared M. Ward, 49, died at 8:18 p.m. Sunday at OSF HealthCare St. Joseph Medical Center in Bloomington after he and another man fell into icy waters at Evergreen Lake north of Hudson while ice fishing earlier that day. According to McLean County Coroner Kathleen Yoder, Ward died from drowning due to cold exposure.
The McLean County Sheriff's Office said that at 4:32 p.m., they responded to the 18000 block of Recreation Area Drive along the shores of Evergreen Lake in response to two men who fell into the lake. Fire departments from Hudson, El Paso, Towanda and Normal responded to the scene and were able to pull both men from the water.
Ward was transported to St. Joseph, while the other man was sent to Carle BroMenn Medical Center in Normal. Ward died after being transported to the hospital.
Yoder said that toxicology results remain pending. The coroner and the sheriff's office are continuing to investigate what led to Ward's death.

description: Here's an updated look at where Big Ten basketball teams sit in the latest USA TODAY Sports Coaches poll and AP Top 25 rankings:
content:
Over the past several months, a handful of contenders have emerged as the Big Ten's best hopes for its first men's basketball national championship team since 2000.
The program that won that now-25-year-old title, Michigan State, is one of them, with a surprising 18-3 record. Purdue isn't quite where it was last season with Zach Edey, but it's not terribly far off with Braden Smith leading the way. Wisconsin, with a potent and shockingly fast-paced offense, is excelling. Newcomers Oregon and UCLA have turned heads. Few teams in the country are playing better than Maryland right now. And Michigan, behind a pair of versatile 7-footers, has impressed in its first season under Dusty May.
The past week included some notable results that shape both the conference and national landscape. Tom Izzo's Spartans saw their 13-game win streak come to an end in a loss at USC. Maryland knocked off Wisconsin 76-58. UCLA blew out Oregon 78-52. Purdue held off archrival Indiana 81-76.
With those games in hand, here are the latest updates of where Big Ten teams stand in the USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll and AP Top 25:

title: Illinois football lands its highest ranked high school recruit under Bret Bielema
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: The Ohio high schooler is a 4-star defensive back ranked in the top 50 nationwide in the Class of 2026.
content:
Illinois football continues its productive recruiting offseason.
The Illini landed the highest-ranked prep recruit of the Bret Bielema era over the weekend when four-star defensive back Victor Singleton announced his commitment.
The 6-foot, 160-pounder from Toledo (Ohio) Central Catholic is the No. 46 overall prospect in the Class of 2026, according to 247Sports, and No. 3 at his position. He chose Illinois over Ohio State, Texas A&M, Michigan, Penn State, Oregon, Ole Miss, Tennessee and a dozen-plus others.
Singleton said his pursuit by Illinois defensive backs coach Corey Parker was a primary driver of his commitment. Parker came to Illinois two years ago from Toledo, the first school to offer Singleton.
"(He has) been sticking with me and keeping the process going and recruiting me, so I just felt like I needed to come and visit him," Singleton told Illini Inquirer. "He was my first offer, and he's stuck with me ever since. So I show him some love, and I really like him."
Singleton is the seventh commit in the Class of 2026. He joins to in-state recruits in Jacob Alexander of Frankfort Lincoln-Way East and receiver Davon Grant of DeKalb. The Illini also have received commitments from offensive lineman Landen Van Seggern of Nebraska and three Florida players in quarterback Michael Clayton and receiver Kenyon Alston of Orlando and linebacker Kingston Shaw of Apopka.
The Illinois recruiting class is No. 17 overall in the nation, according to 247Sports. The Illini are coming off a 10-win season and a victory in the Citrus Bowl. They return 18 of 22 starters for the 2025 season.

title: Iconic thrift store to close one of its central Illinois locations
author: Mike Kramer
description: With the opening of a large store in Galesburg, Goodwill of Central Illinois has decided to close a neighboring location next month.
content:
Goodwill announced Thursday it will close its location in Kewanee on March 8.
The non-profit organization Goodwill of Central Illinois announced all Kewanee store employees will be eligible for rehire at another location. These employees will also qualify for unemployment benefits. All of Goodwill's free employment, youth and veterans services will still be available to area residents.
Goodwill in December opened a larger store in Galesburg, located about 40 miles southwest. It is three times the size of its previous store.
Tazewell County food inspections: Onions on the floor and menu advisories
Goodwill chief executive officer Don Johnson said "sustainability must always be our first consideration."
"To maintain that ability, we must be as strategic as possible," Johnson said. "With the opening of our new, larger Galesburg store, we are strengthening our sustainability and thus our ability to serve even more individuals. With this in mind, the decision has been made to close our store in Kewanee.'
Goodwill of Central Illinois has 11 locations, including two in Peoria and locations in Washington, East Peoria and Pekin. For more information visit www.goodwillpeo.org.

title: Our Super Bowl Sunday picks: Who wins NFL championship of Chiefs vs Eagles?
author: Adam Duvall
description: Our picks for Super Bowl 59: Odds, predictions, how to watch Philadelphia Eagles vs Kansas City Chiefs game on Feb. 9, 2025.
content:
The Philadelphia Eagles and Kansas City Chiefs play on Super Bowl Sunday at 5:30 p.m. CT Feb. 9 at Caesars Superdome in New Orleans.
The NFL championship game is the culmination of the 2024 season and the final game of the NFL playoff schedule.
Which team will win the Super Bowl? Here are the picks from the Journal Star sports staff, why they will win and who will win MVP of the big game.
Illinois to the Super Bowl: Eagles, Chiefs players with ties to the state
Wes Huett: Eagles 27, Chiefs 21
Why Philadelphia? Two words: Saquon Barkley. The NFL is a quarterback's world, but Barkley is the exceptions that proves the rule. He will help Philly control the clock, Jalen Hurts will make just enough plays and the 'Birds defense will be just disruptive enough to Patrick Mahomes to allow Philly to escape with its second Super Bowl title in the last decade.
Super Bowl MVP: Saquon Barkley.
Expert Super Bowl picks: Unique betting insights only at USA TODAY.
Adam Duvall: Chiefs 27, Eagles 21
Why Kansas City? Patrick Mahomes and KC make NFL history with the league's first three-peat. The dynamic QB seals his place on the pantheon of the all-time greats with this victory. Eagles RB Saquon Barkley will run through the Chiefs defense, but Mahomes again will be too much in clutch time.
Super Bowl MVP: Xavier Worthy
Did we get it right? Our predictions before the 2025 NFL playoffs
Dave Eminian: Chiefs 31, Eagles 24
Why Kansas City? Everyone is tired of Taylor and Travis and the Mahomes Rules and all those story lines. I want the Eagles to win. I want Saquon Barkley to run for a ring. It's better for the NFL. But a ground game against a quick-strike pass offense scares me, and I think Mahomes is a generational guy who still has another ring left in him. If the Eagles get behind, they have Jalen Hurts leading a comeback. If the Chiefs get behind, they have Mahomes.
