description: Longtime NFL player and coach Dick Manual Jauron died Saturday. Here is the story of his birth in Peoria and how a local school became his namesake.
content:
Dick Jauron made his name in football. That story includes a hall of fame career as a Yale running back, nearly a decade as an NFL defensive back, and three decades as a respected pro coach. He died of cancer on Saturday at the age 74.
As for how Richard Manual Jauron was given part of his actual name? That story is one steeped in football lore dating back to 1950 when his father, Bob, coached high school football in Peoria, Illinois.
As the story goes, Bob's Manual Rams were on their way to a second consecutive perfect season — the best any Illinois high school team could hope for in the years before the state playoffs.
"A potent Kewanee team stood in the way of this objective," Journal Star columnist Phil Theobald wrote on Nov. 19, 1973. "Jauron said, in so many impassioned words, 'If we beat Kewanee I'll name my son after the school.'
"They did. The coach kept his promise."
Richard Manual Jauron was born Oct. 7, 1950 — one day after that fateful road game.
"My wife didn't like it, but that's the way it went," Bob Jauron once told the Chicago Tribune. "She said it was a good thing we didn't lose, or his middle name would be 'Kewanee.'"
The Jaurons time in Peoria was brief. Bob, a World War II veteran, was a New Hampshire native who played at Boston College. He coached Manual for three years, going 47-3 from 1949-51. He then bounced around various levels of football until retiring in 1972. He and his wife, Kay, told the Tribune they moved 22 times in the course of Bob's coaching career.
Dick, of course, followed. He attended grade school in Indiana and was a high school all-American in Massachusetts before becoming a record-setting running back at Yale and earning a spot in the College Football Hall of Fame.
Dick was drafted by the Detroit Lions in 1973, spent five years in Detroit and three with the Cincinnati Bengals. He retired in 1980 with 25 career interceptions and one Pro Bowl appearance.
Dick began his pro coaching career in 1985 as a spent 10 years as a head coach, most notably with the Chicago Bears from 1999 to 2003. In 2001, his Bears won the NFC Central with a 13-3 record and Jauron won the NFL Coach of the Year.
The notoriously taciturn Dick Jauron didn't talk much about Peoria in various interviews over the years. Not that he would remember since he moved away at such a young age. Back in 1973, the Journal Star's Theobald cornered Jauron that day and simply asked: "Why is your middle name Manual, Dick?"
"You know why my middle name is Manual,' Jauron replied, "chagrined that anyone at Soldier Field would have reason to ask why his middle name is Manual," wrote Theobald.
And with that, Theobald wrote, the television people "dragged Dick Manual Jauron away."

title: Illinois congressman questions purpose of Musk group's access to NOAA systems
author: Zach Roth
description: Before entering politics, 17th District Rep. Eric Sorensen was a TV meteorologist for various stations.
content:
An Illinois congressman – and former TV meteorologist – is looking for answers from the Trump administration after reports that a group associated with Elon Musk had gained access to IT systems at the headquarters for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.
Rep. Eric Sorensen, who represents the 17th Congressional District containing much of Peoria, sent a letter, along with North Carolina congresswoman Deborah Ross, to President Donald Trump on Monday asking him to clarify the purpose of allowing members of Musk's Department of Government Efficiency access to NOAA's systems.
In addition, both want further clarification as to whether DOGE was able to access sensitive data, if Trump wants to alter NOAA's mission, restrict public access to NOAA data and if there are any safeguards preventing Musk in particular from abusing his access to the data.
The letter says that Musk's varied business interests – including aerospace, telecommunications and artificial intelligence through companies like Tesla, X (Twitter) and Starlink – provide him with conflicts of interest that may impact the integrity of the agency's operations, which include weather forecasting through the National Weather Service.
The pair extolled the virtues of NWS and its mission, saying that the work done by their forecasters provides life-saving information and helps farmers, fisherman and other "hardworking Americans" protect their livelihoods. They also noted that NWS helps ensure the safety of the nation's airspace, saying that any threat to NOAA and NWS would "pose a great danger" to the United States.
The pair had been acting on reports published last week that DOGE members had gained access to NOAA and had gained access to the agency's computer systems, which contained confidential information only available to department staffers. The Musk-backed group had entered several other government agencies, such as the Treasury Department, where they reportedly gained access to payment systems that contained personal data for millions of American citizens, according to the New York Times.
Sorensen was a meteorologist for over 20 years before entering the political sphere. A native of Rockford, he had served as a meteorologist for one of the city's major TV stations – the NBC-affiliate WREX from 2003-2014 – before heading to the Quad Cities and ABC-affiliated WQED from 2014-2021. First elected in 2022 in the 17th District, Sorensen is currently in his second term in office.
Sorensen and Ross ask that the Trump administration provide answers to their inquiry by Feb. 21.

title: What's the best restaurant in the Midwest? See USA TODAY's 2025 Restaurants of the Year
author: Howell
description: These 11 restaurants are part of the USA TODAY Restaurants of the Year 2025.
content:
Food writers across the USA TODAY Network selected their favorite spots
These restaurants are part of the USA TODAY Restaurants of the Year 2025 list
They range from white tablecloth, James Beard-nominated spots to roadside burger stands
The Midwest may be known for its comfort foods and classic supper clubs, but our USA TODAY Restaurants of the Year list proves the region's dining scene is far more than just meat and potatoes.
Chosen by our team of food writers who live and work in the communities they cover, this carefully curated list highlights dining spots ranging from an upscale, wine-focused New American gem to a beloved Serbian family-run institution.
Spanning Iowa, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, South Dakota, and Wisconsin, these standout restaurants showcase the best of Midwestern dining, offering diverse cuisines and culinary philosophies. Whether it's a chef-owner infusing bold international flavors into Midwestern classics or a small-town eatery serving unforgettable farm-to-table meals, these spots exemplify excellence.
One thing unites them all: a commitment to quality and community. Read on to discover which Midwest eatery might be your next must-visit destination.
What's the best restaurant near you? Check out USA TODAY's 2025 Restaurants of the Year.
Need a break? Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
Inside look
Oak Park | Des Moines, Iowa
Few communities are lucky enough to have a restaurant like Oak Park, the New American gem that incorporates French techniques in the kitchen. Owner Kathy Fehrmann pulled together a stellar staff, designed a new building using the Prairie style of architecture made famous by Frank Lloyd Wright and considered every detail, from the acorn-shaped lights overhead to the local artwork on the wall.
The menu from chef Ian Robertson touches on Midwest staples, such as a bacon-wrapped pork chop, as well as beloved newcomers such as the carrot Wellington and potato gnocchi served with truffle beurre monté that have become standards on this rotating menu. Executive pastry chef Jess Robertson, Ian's wife, concocts desserts ranging from $4 oatmeal cream pies to $100 banana splits. Sam Tuttle heads up a wine program already lauded by Wine Spectator as one of the best in the country. — Susan Stapleton, Des Moines Register
Bodhi | Indianapolis, Indiana
Bodhi restaurant review: Our local food writer recommends the fresh and novel Thai dishes served at this buzzy bistro.
Named for the Sanskrit word for enlightenment, Bodhi quickly became one of Indianapolis' most acclaimed restaurants after opening at the north end of Mass Avenue in March 2021. The 21-plus Thai bistro and craft cocktail bar is a buzzing hangout approachable enough for a quick drink on the greenery-enclosed patio and refined enough for a celebratory splurge.
The creative spark behind Bodhi spans three generations of Thai women: owner Taelor Carmine; her mother, Nicky; and her grandmother, Pen Phojanasupan. The family and its staff curate dishes like papaya salad and massaman curry that look familiar on a menu, yet feel completely fresh and novel on your plate. When someone says, 'Just wait until you try really good Thai food,' they're talking about places like Bodhi. — Bradley Hohulin, Indianapolis Star
Roots Eatery and Pub | Wolcott, Indiana
Indiana's small towns are celebrated for hidden gem restaurants. But none is likely as locally sourced as Roots. Owned and operated by siblings Amber Farrington and Luke Furrer, Roots offers many Midwest-comfort favorites, like meatloaf and schnitzel.
But the real stars of this restaurant's plates are the beef and pork, raised on their family's farm just down the road in Reynolds. Beyond the restaurant's sign, it would be easy to look past the building while driving along US 231. Step inside and you'll soon understand how this spot quickly became a destination eatery in a town of fewer than 1,000 residents. — Jillian Ellison, Lafayette Journal & Courier
Mabel Gray | Hazel Park, Michigan
Details: 23825 John R Road; 248-398-4300, mabelgraykitchen.com
Mabel Gray restaurant review: Our local food writer recommends chef James Rigato magical and innovative dishes, including a 60-day aged Waygu strip steak and fall sweet corn tossed in umami miso butter.
Few Detroit-area restaurants offer the level of continuous excellence that Mabel Gray exudes. Celebrating its 10th anniversary this fall, the New American restaurant has maintained its staying power by striking a delicate balance of consistency and imagination. There are tried-and-true classics, like steak frites, a 60-day dry-aged, bone-in American wagyu strip steak served with a hearty bowl of house-made fries decorated with pecorino and herbaceous clippings of fresh rosemary.
And there are seasonal appearances, like a fall sweet corn tossed in umami miso butter, citrusy preserved lemon and salty, crunchy bits of chicharrónes. A decade in, James Beard Award-nominated chef James Rigato keeps the magic alive at Mabel Gray with innovative projects, like the restaurant's new vampiric wine cave and private dining room, where sommelier Paulina Schemanski flaunts her skills in Champagne and vino. — Lyndsay C. Green, Detroit Free Press
The color scheme at Tomato Brothers has changed since the 1980s, but everything else — from the classic soft lighting to the plush seats in the waiting area to the design of the children's menu — has been the same since today's adult diners were children.
You can count on the restaurant to have a wait on the regular. People come for the classic Italian and Greek menu: the tasty pizza and meatballs and the pasta portions as big as your head. But really, truly, they come for the breadsticks — an unintended family addition that's known across the country, and even by celebrity actor Dax Shepard. — Cassandra Lybrink, Livingston Daily
The Aperture | Cincinnati, Ohio
Book your reservation now on Open Table.
Located in a restored art deco building that most recently housed a pawn shop, The Aperture features a cool, minimalist dining room warmed by an open-fire kitchen. Here, chef-owner Jordan Anthony-Brown offers a mezze-style menu that demonstrates how to balance complex textures and flavors without abandoning comfort.
Case in point: his hamachi collar, served in a sweet orange glaze, zig-zagged with a crab paste miso aioli and polka-dotted with sliced serrano chilies. A Cincinnati native, Anthony-Brown left town for about 20 years, honing his craft at restaurants such as the Michelin-starred Rose's Luxury in Washington, D.C. Since opening The Aperture, he's received both local and national accolades, including a spot on the New York Times annual list of the 50 best restaurants in America. — Keith Pandolfi, Cincinnati Enquirer
Agni | Columbus, Ohio
Agni restaurant review: Our local food writer recommends this course-by-course trip around the world with meticulously prepared, beautifully plated dishes that takes you to a place that's meaningful to chef-owner Avishar Barua or his team.
An evening at Agni is a course-by-course trip around the world. Each meticulously prepared, beautifully plated dish takes you to a place that's meaningful to chef-owner Avishar Barua or his team: his Bengali background, Midwest upbringing and travels in Thailand; his kitchen staff's roots in Oaxaca, Mexico; his old job at a Chinese restaurant and more. Barua, a former 'Top Chef' contestant who has beaten Bobby Flay and cooked on 'Guy's Grocery Games,' is a serious but playful chef.
Among his creations are a masala ranch dressing for a fried-mushroom bar dish and a 'heckuva good' sauce for his chaat starter that's an ode to Heluva Good grocery-store dip. Agni was one of Bon Appetit's best new restaurants of 2024, and Barua was a James Beard Foundation semifinalist for Best Chef Great Lakes in 2024. — Bob Vitale, Columbus Dispatch
Social at the Stone House | Massillon, Ohio
Book your reservation now on Open Table.
There's a realization when you step into Social at the Stone House that this meticulously renovated Romanesque house built in the 1840s is a place to be enjoyed for any occasion. Wind down after a busy week with a creative libation, perhaps a hibiscus velvet mule or a luxe mocktail.
Grab a table by one of the five indoor fireplaces to chat with friends and enjoy Asian fusion dishes such as kung pao dumplings or baked feta with grilled focaccia. — Bev Shaffer, Canton Repository
Sanaa's Gourmet Mediterranean | Sioux Falls, South Dakota
At Sanaa's Gourmet Mediterranean, a two-time James Beard Foundation award nominee, there are freshly made fatayers, vegetarian kibbeh, kofta kabobs and, course, beloved baklava. But perhaps the daily line of lunchgoers hunger most for their chance to greet the charming restaurateur herself, Syrian-born Sanaa Abourezk. She will dance in the kitchen, fingers snapping and all, then approach the counter with her red lipstick and red pepper earrings on, serve a plate of organic cuisine for you and then ask how your kids are doing. Her menu is consistent and savory; the colors of the boutique restaurant are playful and warm – as are the low-hanging decorative lamps; and oh, our local darling Sanaa, she will teach you how to properly love food and how to love yourself. — Angela George, Sioux Falls Argus Leader
Three Brothers | Milwaukee, Wisconsin
Tucked into a residential area in Milwaukee's Bay View neighborhood, this sweet Serbian restaurant has been a cornerstone of the community for 68 years, a family-run space for three generations. Step inside the cozy dining room at Three Brothers and you're transported to Grandma's house, right down to the Formica tables.
Homestyle Serbian fare is brought to the table on mismatched plates and platters: A fresh Serbian salad that sneaks a wallop of flavor in its seeming simplicity, chicken paprikash that soothes and pickled sarma with fluffy dumplings that sings. And, of course, the burek: the restaurant's signature is squeeze-your-shoulder comfort with a crust that crackles into a flurry of buttery, paper-thin phyllo. Three Brothers is a time capsule of Old World charm with heaps of comfort to spare. — Rachel Bernhard, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel
BroKogi Korean Fusion Restaurant | Stevens Point, Wisconsin
Details: 108 Division St.; 715-618-6215, koreanrestaurantstevenspoint.com
Diners travel from across central Wisconsin to experience fried chicken, Korean corndogs, bulgogi beef, kimchi fried rice and other dishes at BroKogi Korean Fusion Restaurant in Stevens Point. Nestled in a small building next to Jimmy John's along the city's main thoroughfare, the unassuming restaurant has become the go-to for diners hoping to satisfy their Korean cuisine cravings.
Brothers Sangwoon Kim, 20, and Sangin Kim, 19, opened BroKogi in September 2023 after operating a successful food truck for just a few months. When owners of the only brick-and-mortar Korean restaurant in central Wisconsin closed, the Kim brothers took the leap, opening a permanent location, keeping Korean cuisine in the area. It was so successful that 10 months later, the brothers opened a second location in Wausau. — Caitlin Shuda, Stevens Point Journal

title: Chicago is one step closer to adding a NCAA Division-I college football team
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Chicago State hopes to be playing D-I college football in 2026. It's now officially seeking its first head coach.
content:
The 3,000-student college is building a program 'from scratch'
Chicago State would begin play as a member of the NEC in fall 2026.
The state of Illinois is one step closer to having another Division-I college football program.
Chicago State on Tuesday officially launched its search for a head coach to lead the newly created football program, expected to begin play in the NCAA Football Championship Subdivision in 2026.
'We are excited to reach this milestone in our football planning," Chicago State athletics director Dr. Monique Carroll said in a release. "Hiring a coach will give this program a face and bring us one step closer to D-1 football on the South Side."
Chicago State athletics announced in 2023 its intention to raise $4 million to expand its offerings, including football. The school retained Renaissance Search & Consulting to lead the search with the timeline to make a hire this spring. Interested candidates can apply online.
"Our ideal candidate," Carroll said, "is a leader who understands what it takes to build a program from scratch."
Chicago State, founded in 1867, is a predominantly Black institution of about 3,000 students, located on the south side of Chicago. It fields 16 college teams with more than 160 athletes. Adding football will add more than 200 students and "expand the school's reach, which furthers the university's goal of growing its student body," Carroll told The Athletic in 2023.
Chicago State in July 2024 officially became one of nine full members of the Northeast Conference (NEC), which as of fall 2024 had eight football-playing members: Central Connecticut, Duquense, Robert Morris, LIU, Saint Francis, Wagner, Mercyhurst and Stonehill.
It is unclear where Chicago State will play its home games. The school has 161 acres with room for locker rooms and a field for practices, Carroll told The Athletic. As of that 2023 story, Carroll said "possibilities range from Soldier Field to SeatGeek Stadium in Bridgeview to local high schools."
Chicago State would be the state's eighth NCAA Division-I football program. Illinois, Northwestern and Northern Illinois compete in the NCAA D-I Football Bowl Subdivision, while Illinois State, Southern Illinois, Western Illinois and Eastern Illinois are NCAA D-I FCS programs.

title: Iowa, Michigan continue climbing in latest Big Ten women's basketball power rankings
author: Dargan Southard
description: Iowa and Michigan are both surging and took big leaps in the latest USA TODAY Sports Big Ten women's basketball power rankings.
content:
Show Caption
The bright lights of March are inching closer. Big Ten women's basketball plans to make a huge splash once they officially arrive.
With the possibility of landing a stunning 13 NCAA Tournament bids next month, this league is full of teams that have big splashes in their futures. From now until Selection Sunday, it's all about March positioning for bigger things ahead.
With that in mind, here are the latest USA TODAY Sports Network Big Ten women's basketball power rankings. All results are reflective of games through Feb. 10.
1. UCLA (23-0)
Previously: No. 1
What to know: The Bruins were tested a bit more than usual last week but still managed double-digit wins over Ohio State and Oregon. Thursday's trip to USC is looming.
2. USC (21-2)
Previously: No. 3
What to know: After the stunning loss at Iowa, the Trojans got back on track with strong wins over Wisconsin and Ohio State. Now USC gets top-dog UCLA on Thursday.
3. Ohio State (20-3)
Previously: No. 2
What to know: The Buckeyes' Los Angeles swing was an 0-2 disappointment. Ohio State will look to get back on track with upcoming home games vs. Minnesota and Iowa.
4. Maryland (19-5)
Previously: No. 4
What to know: Maryland shook off the Illinois loss with a successful 2-0 West Coast swing vs. Oregon and Washington. The Terrapins now have upcoming home games vs. Nebraska and Michigan.
5. Illinois (19-5)
Previously: No. 6
What to know: It's now a six-game winning streak for Illinois after conquering Northwestern and Wisconsin last week. The Fighting Illini have upcoming home games vs. Penn State and Nebraska before the Los Angeles swing.

Previously: No. 5
What to know: A 10-point home loss to Michigan soured the Spartans' surge a bit. Michigan State hosts Wisconsin on Wednesday before its own Los Angeles swing.
7. Iowa (17-7)
Previously: No. 10
What to know: What a difference a few weeks make. Iowa has answered its five-game losing streak with a five-game winning streak. The Hawkeyes host Rutgers on Thursday.
8. Michigan (17-7)
Previously: No. 11
What to know: A strong week for the Wolverines following road wins over Nebraska and Michigan State. Michigan hosts Indiana on Wednesday.
9. Indiana (15-8)
Previously: No. 8
What to know: The Hoosiers lost some momentum with Sunday's road loss at Minnesota, but plenty of opportunities await for improvement.
10. Nebraska (16-8)
Previously: No. 7
What to know: Nebraska has suddenly dropped three straight following home losses to Michigan and Iowa. It doesn't get easier this week with trips to Maryland and Illinois.
11. Minnesota (19-6)
Previously: No. 12
What to know: A needed win Sunday over Indiana stopped Minnesota's three-game losing streak. The Golden Gophers play at Ohio State on Thursday.
12. Oregon (16-8)
Previously: No. 9
What to know: Oregon is on a three-game losing streak after falling to Maryland and UCLA at home. The Ducks will host Washington before a Midwest swing to Minnesota and Nebraska.
13. Washington (14-10)
Previously: No. 13
What to know: The Huskies are slowly slipping away from the rest of the pack, having dropped four of their last five. Washington plays at Oregon on Wednesday before hosting USC on Sunday.
14. Wisconsin (11-13)
Previously: No. 14
What to know: Home games against USC and Illinois went as expected. The Badgers host Michigan State and Penn State this week.
15. Rutgers (10-14)
Previously: No. 17
What to know: Rutgers picked up its second Big Ten win of the season last time out against Purdue. The Scarlet Knights head to Iowa on Thursday.
16. Northwestern (8-14)
Previously: No. 18
What to know: The Wildcats picked up their first Big Ten win and first win overall since Dec. 21 with a 69-63 home win over Penn State on Sunday. Northwestern plays at Purdue on Wednesday.
17. Purdue (8-15)
Previously: No. 16
What to know: Purdue has dropped 11 of its first 12 Big Ten games. The Boilermakers host Northwestern on
18. Penn State (10-14)
Previously: No. 15

The stretch run will decide a Big Ten title, and the slate for fans of the league should produce an entertaining finish.
Several teams have weird trends, like UCLA's travel and Purdue's luck against a Maryland 3-point shooter.
Will Michigan State coach Tom Izzo need to wait until March to pull away from Bobby Knight for the Big Ten wins record?
A back-loaded Big Ten Conference men's basketball schedule means none of the championship contenders have an easy closing stretch to the trophy. No one has it tougher than the Spartans, whose final seven games feature six ranked opponents and a road trip to Iowa.
Purdue must still play at Michigan State and Illinois and in the always hectic Assembly Hall environment at Indiana. Michigan still faces both ends of a home-and-home with the Spartans and home games against Illinois and Maryland.

title: 'Yellowjackets' Season 3: Premiere date, trailer, cast and where to watch
author: Amaris Encinas
description: "Yellowjackets" returns to Paramount+ with Showtime for a new season this Valentine's Day. See what the highly anticipated season has in store.
content:
A new "Yellowjackets" season will make its on-screen debut on Valentine's Day, nearly two years after the second season of the psychological thriller series was released.
The Emmy-nominated series tells the epic tale of an all-girl high school soccer team who were stranded in the northern wilderness after they survive a plane crash and the lengths to which they go to stay alive.
The teenage girls "hunted their friends, feasted on their flesh, and they went completely (expletive) nuts," young Shauna (Sophie Nélisse) narrates in the Season 3 trailer.
The girls' story alternates between past and present, offering the viewer a chance to see what became of the survivors nearly 25 years after the crash as they experience the devastating ramifications of the present. The new 10-episode season will pick up after the shocking death of adult Natalie Scatorccio, played by Juliette Lewis, in the Season 2 finale.
Watch Yellowjackets Season 3 with Sling
"The Yellowjackets continue to fight for survival after a brutal winter in The Wilderness. In the present day, still reeling from Natalie's death, the survivors are forced to uncover secrets they thought were buried for good," according to a Season 3 tagline.
Here's what to know about Season 3 of "Yellowjackets," including the premiere date, cast and how to watch.
When is the 'Yellowjackets' Season 3 premiere?
"Yellowjackets" Season 3 will premiere Friday, Feb. 14 on Paramount+ with Showtime. Both the season premiere and the second episode will be able to watch, per Forbes.
New "Yellowjackets" episodes will be released every Sunday starting on Feb. 23.
How to watch 'Yellowjackets' Season 3
"Yellowjackets" Season 3 and previous seasons can be streamed on Paramount+ with Showtime.
Only the first season of "Yellowjackets" is available to stream on Netflix.

title: Bracketology: NCAA Tournament projection has Michigan making major move forward
author: Paul Myerberg
description: Don't look now but Michigan is making a move in the Big Ten and also ascending in the latest Bracketology prediction for the NCAA men's tournament.
content:
Five wins in a row, capped by Tuesday night's victory at home against Purdue, has sent Michigan to the top of the Big Ten and pushed the Wolverines to the No. 4 line in our Bracketology projecting the NCAA men's tournament field.
After leading Florida Atlantic to back-to-back tournament berths and a Final Four appearance two seasons ago, Dusty May has already tied the program record for Big Ten wins by a first-year coach. The Wolverines are a half-game ahead of Purdue heading into Sunday's trip to Ohio State.
Michigan has a chance to continue scaling the tournament ladder — or getting knocked back a few rungs before the start of March Madness.
Six of the Wolverines' final seven games before the Big Ten tournament come against teams currently in our bracket. Two of those matchups come against rival Michigan State. They also play Nebraska on the road and host Illinois and Maryland.
Connecticut's win this week at Creighton – Dan Hurley would like to remind all of us he has two rings, by the way – moves the Huskies up to the No. 7 line, replacing Mississippi State. The Bulldogs fall to a No. 8 seed amid six losses in nine games, most recently at home to Florida.
Two new teams join the bracket. One is John Calipari's Arkansas, winners of three of four. The Razorbacks are up to No. 41 in the NET rankings. The second is Brigham Young. The Cougars won at West Virginia on Tuesday and will face Kansas State on Saturday in a game with major bubble implications.
And it's an ugly bracket for the extremely top-heavy ACC. After sending nine teams into March Madness a year ago, the league has only three teams in the projected field: No. 1 seed Duke, No. 7 Louisville and No. 7 Clemson. The last time the ACC had fewer than four teams in the bracket was 2000.
Last four in
San Diego State, Virginia Commonwealth, Brigham Young, Arkansas.
First four out
Georgia, SMU, Kansas State, Villanova.

description: On Thursday, the NFL released the list of prospects invited to the 2025 NFL Combine. Here's which Big Ten prospects were invited to the NFL draft showcase:

The next step of the NFL draft process is just around the corner with the annual NFL combine in Indianapolis.
On Thursday, the NFL released the list of the 329 prospects who have been invited to the NFL draft showcase at Lucas Oil Stadium — and the Big Ten will once again have a large presence.
Of the 329 players invited to participate at the combine, 80 are from Big Ten programs. Headlining the group of Big Ten prospects on offense is Ohio State quarterback Will Howard, Oregon quarterback Dillon Gabriel, Iowa running back Kaleb Johnson and Penn State tight end Tyler Warren among others.
Meanwhile on defense, the Big Ten will be represented by Penn State's Abdul Carter, who was listed as a defensive lineman, Michigan defensive lineman Mason Graham, Michigan defensive back Will Johnson and Ohio State defensive lineman JT Tuimoloau among others.
The 2025 NFL Combine is set to take place across the week of February 24, with skills competition and drills starting on Thursday, Feb. 27 and running through Sunday, March 2.

title: Bobbleheads, fireworks and more: Peoria Chiefs baseball promotion schedule for 2025
author: Dave Eminian
description: The Peoria Chiefs announced their promotions schedule for 2025. Here is every fireworks night and every bobblehead, plus all giveaways for the summer.
content:
The Peoria Chiefs minor league baseball team announced its promotional schedule Thursday for the 2025 season at its Downtown ballpark, Dozer Park.
The High-A affiliate of the St. Louis Cardinals open the 2025 Midwest League baseball season on Friday, April 4. The coaching staff was announced last month, and the opening day roster is expected to be announced in early April.
Here is a look at the Chiefs schedule and its slate of promotions.
2025 Peoria Chiefs baseball schedule
The Chiefs play a 132-game Midwest League schedule that begins April 4 and runs through Sept. 7. It's mostly set up in six-game series. Mondays are a universal day off for all teams in the league. Series run Tuesday-Sunday between the same two teams in the same ballpark. The Chiefs mostly will play a six-game home series, then a six-game road series, and rotate like that throughout the summer.
Below are some highlights from the 2025 schedule. For the complete Peoria Chiefs schedule, check the team calendar on its web page.
Opening day: The Chiefs open the 2025 season Friday, April 4, with three games at home vs Quad Cities, the first of which is at 7:05 p.m. Friday, followed by a 7:05 p.m. starts Saturday and 2:05 p.m. start Sunday.
First pitch: Chiefs home games start at 6:35 p.m. on weeknights; 7:05 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays; 2:05 p.m. on Sundays. Education Day games are 11:05 a.m., and night games before a day game move up to 6:05 p.m. There are exceptions for special events like fireworks and other themed nights, so always check the team's schedule on its site.
Rivalry series: The baby Cards-Cubs series will be 12 games, with a six-game series at South Bend on April 8-13, three-game series in Peoria on July 1-3 and a three-game series in South Bend from July 4-6.
Peoria Chiefs promotional nights in 2025
The Peoria Chiefs will stage 26 giveaways, 23 fireworks shows and 22 themed nights during their 66-game home schedule in 2025. Here is a look at each of those promotions, followed by the weekly promotions from the team:
Bobbleheads: There are three bobblehead nights, limited to the first 1,000 fans: Cardinals prospect Tink Hence (June 28), Cardinals minor league pitcher of the year Quinn Mathews (July 26) and Cardinals outfielder Lars Nootbaar (Aug. 9).
Other giveaways: Magnet schedule (April 4), youth T-shirt (May 2), lightswitch cover (May 4), adult T-shirt (May 9), rope hat (May 10), mini hockey stick (May 23), snack bowl (May 24), Morgan Wallen ticket raffle (May 25), youth jersey (June 6), Hawaiian shirt (June 7), tumbler (June 27), slap koozie (July 11), apron (July 12), sunglasses (July 13), COPA metal sign (July 24), santa hat (July 25), pickleball paddle cover (Aug. 8), lunchbox (Aug. 10) and Distillers-themed whiskey glass (Aug. 28).
Fireworks: The Chiefs host 23 fireworks nights, most on Friday and Saturday. The fireworks games take place on May 2, 3, 9, 10, 24, 25; June 4, 6, 7, 27, 28; July 2, 3, 11, 12, 24, 26; and Aug. 6, 8, 9, 28, 30, 31. The Chiefs are on the road July 4.
Theme nights: E-Sports Night (May 2), Star Wars Night (May 24), Hawaiian Night (June 7), Christmas in July (July 25), Faith and Family Night (July 12 and August 6), Fright Night (Aug. 29) and Fan Appreciation Night (August 30). New theme nights include Hockey Night (May 23) and Peanuts Night (June 6), during which the Chiefs will wear a Charlie Brown t-shirt jersey.
Education Day: Dozer Park also will host three morning games as part of an Education Day series: April 29, May 7 and 20).
Re-branded nickname: The Chiefs will play four Thursday games as the Peoria Distillers, a popular re-brand promotion (April 17, May 22, June 5 and Aug. 7). They will play at the Pork Tenderloins on July 11-12, and as the Orange Barrels on June 27-28 and July 25-26. They will also play as an alternate Hispanic team identity on May 6, July 24 and Aug. 9 — calling themselves the Perros Bomberos de Peoria, or Fire Dogs.

title: Every high school wrestler to win four IHSA individual state championships
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Here is a list of the 16 Illinois high school wrestlers to win four career IHSA state championships. A Mizzou-bound wrestler from Chicago joined in 2025.
content:
The 2025 Illinois High School Association individual wrestling state finals were held Feb. 20-22 at State Farm Center in Champaign.
This year, Chicago Mount Carmel senior Seth Mendoza joined a list of elite Illinois wrestlers to end their four-year career with a fourth state championship.
Here is a list of every Illinois wrestler to win four titles, their school, years of the title run and what to know about their careers after high school.
Seth Mendoza, Chicago Mt. Carmel
Championships: 2022-3A (106 pounds), 2023-3A (113), 2024-3A (126), 2025-3A (138)
What to know: The third Mount Carmel wrestler on the list is signed to wrestle at Missouri. Over 16 career matches at state, he won 15 by technical fall.
Austin O'Connor, Chicago St. Rita
Championships: 2014-3A (106), 2015-3A (132), 2016-3A (145), 2017-3A (152)
What to know: Second St. Rita wrestler on the list compiled a career mark of 181-4 before winning a national title and becoming an all-American at North Carolina.
Johnny Jimenez, Aurora Marmion
Championships: 2011-2A (103), 2012-2A (113), 2013-3A (120), 2014-3A (126)
What to know: He went 158-10 in his high school career, joining former teammate Jered Cortez of Glenbard North in the four-timers club in the same season. He went on to become a two-time NCAA qualifier at Wisconsin of the Big Ten.
Jered Cortez, Glenbard North
Championships: 2011-3A (112), 2012-3A (120), 2013-3A (126); 2014-3A (132)
What we know: He won his first title at Aurora Marmion before three at Glenbard North, ending his career with a record of 182-6. He began his college career at Illinois before transferring to Penn State, where he was on the Nittany Lions national championship teams.
Josh Alber, Dakota
Championships: 2011-1A (103), 2012-1A (120), 2013-1A (120), 2014-1A (132)
What to know: He went 177-0 in his high school career, becoming the second four-time champ from Dakota. He went on to become a four-time NCAA qualifier at Northern Iowa.
Seth Milks, Dakota
Championships: 2006-A (103), 2007-A (112), 2008-A (119), 2009-1A (130)
What to know: Five years before Alber came Milks, who won went 160-10 while winning four titles in a row for the 250-student school outside Rockford. He went on to wrestle at NCAA Division III Wisconsin-Plateville.
Mike Benefiel, Lombard Montini
Championships: 2004-A, 2005-A, 2006-AA (152), 2007-AA (171)
What to know: One of three Montini wrestlers on the list, Benefiel finished 200-4 in his career before a collegiate career that started at Northwestern and included a stop at Oklahoma State. He finished at NCAA Division III Elmhurst, where he won a national title.
Albert White, Chicago St. Rita
Championships: 2004-AA (135), 2005-AA (140), 2006-AA (145), 2007-AA (152)
What to know: White went 199-4 in four seasons before starting his career at North Iowa Area Community College, where he won an NJCAA title as a freshman. He went on to wrestle three seasons at Oklahoma State, making the NCAAs as a senior.
Conor Beebe, Lombard Montini 161-13
Championships: 2002-A (103), 2003-A (112), 2004-A (125), 2005-A (125)
What to know: He rolled up a 161-13 record in high schools, joining his older brother with four titles. He went on to become a four-time NCAA qualifier at Central Michigan. He coached in college before starting a wrestling academy.
Chase Beebe, Lombard Montini
Championships: 2000-A (103), 2001-A (112), 2002-A (125), 2003-A (130)
What to know: He went 177-11 over his career, his brother later joining him in the four-timers' club. He began his college career at Purdue before transferring to Eastern Illinois and participating in mixed martial arts.
David Douglas, Dolton Thornridge
Championships: 1994-A (112), 1995-AA (119), 1996-AA (130), 1997-AA (135)
What to know: Won his first title at Chicago Luther South and the final three at Thornridge. He finished 130-3 in high school before an all-American career at Arizona State.
T.J. Williams, Chicago Mt. Carmel
Championships: 1993-AA (135), 1994-AA (140), 1995-AA (145), 1996-AA (145)
What to know: Followed his brother, who also won four IHSA titles at Mount Carmel. Williams went 155-3 in high school before winning two NCAA national championships at Iowa. He is the wrestling coach at Tremont and runs a wrestling school.
Joe Williams, Chicago Mt. Carmel
Championships: 1990-AA (135), 1991-AA (152), 1992-AA (153), 1993-AA (160)
What to know: The brother of T.J. Williams went 159-1 in high school before a stellar career at Iowa. There, he made the NCAAs four times and won titles his final three seasons.
Mike Mena, Sterling Newman
Championships: 1989-A (112), 1990-A (119), 1991-A (125), 1992-A (125)
What to know: Mena went 157-0-1 in high school (he tied the first match of his junior season) before also attending Iowa. He finished in the top seven four times in the NCAAs, finishing second his senior year.
Joey Gilbert, Tinley Park Andrew
Championships: 1986-AA (126), 1987-AA, (132), 1988-AA, (132), 1989-AA (135)
What to know: He went 163-1 in his high school career before becoming a two-time all-American at Michigan State. He also qualified for the NCAAs as a senior at Boise State.
Mark Ruettiger, New Lenox Providence 152-5

title: How to stream 2025 SAG award winners from Shōgun to Conclave
author: Trisha Easto
description: Conclave wins best movie cast, but Shōgun really swept the 2025 SAG Awards. Here's where to find all the award-winning content and stream it today.
content:

— Recommendations are independently chosen by our editors. Purchases you make through the links below may earn us and our publishing partners a commission.
The 2025 Awards season is in full swing, with the Golden Globes and Grammy's both taking place earlier this year. The 31st 2025 Screen Actors Guild Awards show took place on Sunday, February 23. The SAG Awards present 13 awards in TV and film, as voted on by members of the Screen Actors Guild - American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA).
Here's how to stream all the 2025 SAG winners:
How to stream SAG-Award winning show, 'Shōgun'
'Shōgun' is a limited FX series based on a 1975 novel by author James Clavell. The series focuses on a historic period in Japan, in the 16th century when Japan hadn't had a shōgun (a central leader) in 30 years. The series follows the story of an English sailor shipwrecked in Japan at this time.
The limited series took home four SAG awards, including Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series, and both the Best Male and Female Actor in a Drama Series awards
'Shōgun' is only available for streaming on Hulu and Disney+. You can sign up for a Disney+ and Hulu bundle and save up to 44% to catch up on all the entertainment.
How to stream 'Conclave,' SAG's Best Ensemble Cast
'Conclave' is a political thriller focused on the Roman Catholic Church as Cardinal Lawrence (Ralph Fiennes) is tasked with selecting a new pope. He is surrounded by powerful religious leaders in the Vatican and begins to uncover secrets.
The 2024 film debuted on October, and has grossed $98.5 million worldwide, according to FilmNation Entertainment. It had a production budget of $20 million.
The film also stars Isabella Rossellini, Stanley Tucci and John Lithgow.
You can stream 'Conclave' on Peacock, with plans starting at $7.99/month.
Stream Demi Moore in 'The Substance' on Prime Video today
Demi Moore is back, and she looks fantastic at the age of 62. Her role in 'The Substance' earned her the SAG Award for Best Female Actor in a Leading Role. It's a horror film, where actress Elizabeth Sparkle feels like her career is fading after she is fired from a show. Sparkle takes a mysterious drug that promises a younger version of herself, where things go wrong.
'The Substance' stars Demi Moore, along with Margaret Qualley and Dennis Quaid. It is free to stream with a Prime Video subscription.
Stream 'The Substance' today
Watch Timothee Chalamet as Bob Dylan in 'A Complete Unknown'
Actor Timothee Chalamet was up for more than one SAG Award, for his lead role as Bob Dylan in a biopic, but another film he starred in was up for Outstanding Performance by a Stunt Ensemble in a Motion Picture. Sadly, Dune: Part Two did not take home the award, as it went to 'The Fall Guy' (you can stream The Fall Guy on Prime Video too!). But, Chalamet didn't go home empty-handed.
Chalamet portrays Bob Dylan, as he arrives in New York in the 1960's with his guitar and all of his incredible talent.
'A Complete Unknown' was released in December 2024, and has grossed more than $104 million, according to Billboard. You can stream the musical drama on Prime Video today.
Stream the Bob Dylan biopic today
How to stream 'A Real Pain' starring award-winner Kieran Culkin
'A Real Pain' pairs Kieran Culkin and Jesse Eisenberg as two mismatched cousins, Benji and David, who embark on a trip to Poland to honor their late grandmother. As the two tour their family history, old tensions resurface that complicate their adventure.
The comedy was released in November and has grossed over $20 million worldwide, according to Box Office Mojo. You can stream is today when you sign up for a Disney+ and Hulu bundle and save up to 44% to catch up on all the entertainment.

title: Bradley basketball vs Valparaiso score: How a one-of-a-kind star powered BU to victory
author: Dave Eminian
description: The Bradley Braves got five straight 3s from Duke Deen amid a late run to victory in a college basketball game at Valpo.
content:
Show Caption
VALPARAISO, Ind. — Duke Deen is a different breed of player, a one-of-a-kind talent who personally took apart Valparaiso three points at a time Wednesday in a Missouri Valley Conference game at The Arc.
The Bradley Braves senior point guard, shut out in the first half, came out firing in the second half and hit five straight 3-pointers to fuel a 19-3 run over 3:30 and blow open a close game on the way to a 76-65 victory for the Braves over Valpo that was also historic for their 5-foot-8 heart-and-soul.
"He's as elite as they get," Bradley coach Brian Wardle said via Zoom from Valparaiso. "Duke is kind of a unicorn. There's not many Duke Deens out there. There's not many players like him who can do what he does at his size.
"He's unique, and we're just happy he's wearing that Bradley jersey every game."
Deen's fourth 3-pointer gave him 96 made 3s for the season, pushing him into second-most in a single season in Bradley program history. His fifth 3-pointer — from nearly the logo — put him at 254 made 3s for his three-year career at Bradley. That moved him past Nate Kennell (253) for second all-time career 3s in BU program history.
"I didn't know that," Deen said. "I just go out there and hoop. I just do what I do. It's a testament to the work.
"I appreciate everybody letting me shoot those 3s, and I just thank God for it. It's good."
It was a testament to how explosive Bradley's offense can be on a night when senior forward Darius Hannah had a big first half on the way to a 22-point, nine-rebound game, and four Braves reached double figures in scoring.
"I love watching him do that," Hannah said of Deen's 3s. "I hate it when he's not aggressive. I tell him every time when we come in and he's not aggressive, I go to him and say, 'I need you, Duke Deen, I need you to get going. I don't care if you miss them. Shoot your shot, play your game.'
"When he's aggressive, the team energy goes up a lot."
MVC box score: Bradley 76, Valparaiso 65
Indeed, Deen's first of those five 3s fell at 16:14 to pull Bradley into a 37-37 tie.
By the time he delivered the fifth one, the Braves led 56-43 with 12:02 left.
Bradley kept its lead around 8-10 points the rest of the way, closing it out when freshman Jaquan Johnson hit a 3 with 58 seconds left for the game's final points.
Bradley, which leads the nation in 3-point shooting percentage, was 0-of-7 from long distance in the first half. But there was no crisis, as the Braves trailed by one point at the break and calmly put away seven 3-pointers in the final 20 minutes.
"I thought we turned down some good 3s in the first half and took some tough ones," Wardle said. "We talked at half time about shot selection and not turning down catch-and-shoot-3s. Duke only played like 8-9 minutes in the first half, so he was fresh.
"I told him, 'I don't think I'm taking you out all half, so be in attack mode.' He got in attack mode in transition and he can change a game, we all know that. Very quickly change momentum and he did that for us.
"I thought Darius (Hannah) was really good all game, Zek (Montgomery) was in attack mode, Almar (Atlason) played tough and physical, Jaquan (Johnson) got to the paint at will, made plays so just, overall, great team effort. (Demarion) Burch was solid, Meta (Jonovic) was solid in his minutes. Just an overall good team effort."
Darius has raised his level
Hannah has two game-winning buckets down the stretch, and on Wednesday was the best player on the floor in the first half. There is something that feels different about Hannah, maybe it's confidence, definitely intensity, but his game feels like it's at a higher level.
"Darius has that senior sense of urgency right now," Wardle said. "I saw it with Donte Thomas back in the day. Darrell Brown, Elijah Childs, Nate Kennell, Ja'Shon Henry, Malevy Leons, you see that in your seniors when they got that look and effort.
"Hannah is laying it on the line right now in practice and the games."
Said Hannah, of his mindset: "It's always get a bucket. Especially being senior with time trickling down. Help the team the best I can."
No overtime this time
Valparaiso pushed the Braves to a double-overtime scare back on Dec. 29 in Carver Arena, where Bradley battled to an 81-75 win.
Not gonna happen in the rematch Wednesday.
"They made 10 3s, and I was OK with that because that's not what they do," Wardle said. "They get to the free throw line a lot, they thrive on paint touches. We made some mistakes defensively … we need to start playing better … a good 15-16 solid defensive minutes per half, not 10-12.
"We just got to keep plugging away, tweak things, get better at it. I thought our paint toughness was good. I thought winning the rebounding war with them was good."
The Braves outscored Valpo in the paint, 38-22, and out-rebounded them 39-27. In the OT game in late December, the Beacons held a 47-40 rebounding edge.
Kaspar Sepp had 15 rebounds in that game, and 11 points. He was held to three points and six rebounds Wednesday. They got 17 points from Jefferson De La Cruz-Monegro in December, and he scored zero in the rematch.
"We knew it was their senior night, and they were going to give us their best shot," Hannah said. "We took advantage of the switches and just attacked the best way we could. Execute the game plan is what I did from the jump."
Braves rotation has adjusted
Bradley fifth-year senior Connor Dillon has not played in the last seven games, since he came off the bench Feb. 2 at Northern Iowa.
It's simply a change in rotation as Demarion Burch has recovered from illness and is playing well, and the Braves continue to tweak things down the stretch.
"Dillon is healthy now and feeling good," Wardle said. "He's just not in the rotation right now. I won't hesitate putting him in. We feel really good with how Burch is playing right now, and obviously Corey (Thomas) is there to go with Almar and Meta. We feel good right now about our rotation.
"But everyone has to be ready for Arch Madness, because I have no problem putting guys in that tournament and making big plays for us."
They said it
• Bradley head coach Brian Wardle, as the regular-season finale with Northern Iowa looms: "Let them celebrate tonight, and tomorrow it's right into Northern Iowa."
• Bradley guard Duke Deen, on the halftime discussions after the team made no 3-pointers in the first half: "Every time we go into the locker room we just be real with each other. We know what we have to do better, and we come out in the second half and try to do that. They were switching a lot, so I was trying to get the big fellas involved. When we came in at halftime (BU associate head coach Jimmie Foster) told me, 'Get the shots up.' And that's what I did. I got the shots up and tried to carry this team, do what we do best and that's shoot 3s. Once everybody sees one or two fall, we all start hitting some."
• Hannah, on how he capitalized on how Valpo was defending: "Just knowing they were switching 1 through 5, knowing I was going to have a little guy on me every time I set a screen … I want to thank my teammates for getting me the ball. Took advantage of that best way I could."
• Deen, on getting the ball to Darius Hannah in the paint: "I have the utmost faith in Darius to go get a bucket down there. I'll give it to him every time. If they would give the NBA assists, I swear I would average like 8."
• Hannah, on the weapon that is Bradley's 3-point shooting: "It's a game of runs. We know other teams make their pushes. But as the best 3-point shooting team in the country we can always rely on Duke Deen."
Bravely Speaking
Bradley moved up to 23-7 overall and 14-5 in the Missouri Valley Conference, tied for second with Northern Iowa. … Valparaiso slipped to 13-17 (6-13). … The Valley's top four seeds in the upcoming tournament, Drake (26), Bradley (23), Northern Iowa (20) and Belmont (20) are all 20-game winners. … Bradley senior forward Darius Hannah extended his ongoing Bradley program record for games played to 145, which is also eighth all-time in MVC history. … Bradley is 18-3 in games in which Duke Deen makes at least three 3-pointers. … The Braves are 13-1 when Bradley freshman guard Jaquan Johnson has at least two free throws, 1 assist and 1 steal. He had 10 points against Valpo, with two free throws, 6 assists and 3 steals. … Bradley coach Brian Wardle coached his 326th game at the Braves' helm Wednesday at Valparaiso, which tied him with Jim Molinari for third-most in program history. Wardle also moved past Joe Stowell for second in MVC games coached all-time at BU. … Bradley's 23 wins are tied for 11th-most in the NCAA. … In addition to 19 second-half points, Bradley's Deen finished with 1 assist, 3 steals and 6 rebounds. … Christian Davis had 8 points and 7 rebounds. … Valpo's Cooper Schwieger had 21 points on 9 of 16 shooting. … Beacons guard All Wright had 17 points. … Next up for Bradley is the regular-season finale at 1 p.m. Sunday in Carver Arena in a showdown with Northern Iowa to settle the No. 2 and No. 3 seeds in the Valley tournament.
Below are game updates from The Arc in Valparaiso, Indiana.
Bradley-Valpo score updates
TEAMS 1st half 2nd half — FINAL
Bradley 28 48 — 76
Valparaiso 29 36 — 65
FINAL: Bradley 76, Valparaiso 65
Deen with 19, Hannah 22
The Braves lead 71-63 with 3:29 left at The Arc.
Duke Deen has 19 points -- all in the second half -- and Darius Hannah has a game-high 22 points plus 7 rebounds.
Historic significance
Duke Deen's fourth 3-pointer gave him 96 made 3s for the season, second-most in a single-season in Bradley program history.
His fifth 3-pointer -- from nearly the logo -- puts him at 254 for this three-year career at Bradley. That moves him past Nate Kennell (253) for second all-time in BU program history.
Deen is incredible
Duke Deen hits two more 3s -- that's five in a row -- including the last of which was a pull-up from nearly the logo to destroy the game as Bradley races to a 56-43 lead.
It's a 19-3 run in the last 3:30 and Deen has five 3s in that run.
Deen strikes again
Duke Deen with his third straight 3 and Bradley has a 46-40 lead with 14:33 left. Almar Atlason makes a 3 -- that's four in a row for the Braves -- for a 49-43 lead with 13:38 left.
10 lead changes, 7 ties
Back-and-forth battle continues as Jaquan Johnson's layup and-1 gives Bradley a 43-40 lead with 15:07 left.
Deen gets BU into the 3 column
Bradley senior guard Duke Deen hits back-to-back 3s just 40 seconds apart to tie the game at 37-37 and 40-40 with 15:34 left.
Those are the first two 3-pointers made by the Braves in 10 tries.
Numbers after 20
Bradley got 10 points from Darius Hannah and 8 from Zek Montgomery, but the Braves were 0 of 7 from 3-point range in the half.
Bradley holds the boards, 21-12, leads in the paint, 20-12, and is shooting 45% from the floor. The Braves had 8 turnovers in the first half, three of them coming on offensive fouls.
Valparaiso got 10 points from Cooper Schwieger and 8 from All Wright. The Beacons shot only 37% from the field, but they made five 3s among their 11 buckets to stay in the game.
HALFTIME: Valparaiso 29, Bradley 28
No 3-pointers yet
The Braves, who came in as the No. 1 3-point shooting team in the nation, are 0 of 6 from distance so far in this game, with 2:30 left in the first half.
Braves on a 6-0 run
Bradley rattles off six straight points in 52 seconds to take a 26-22 lead and force a Valpo timeout with 4:22 left.
Demarion Burch hit a jumper baseline left to open that sequence. Jaquan Johnson stole the ball from All Wright, and it led to an alley-oop dunk by Zek Montgomery.
A BU defensive stop followed and Montgomery hit a long two from the right corner for 26-22.
Hannah dunks
Terrific feed by freshman guard Jaquan Johnson to set up Darius Hannah for a dunk and a 20-17 lead at 8:34.
Hannah has game-high 10 as the break arrives with 7:54 left.
Hannah leading the way
Bradley forward Darius Hannah with 7 points in the early going to help build a 14-11 lead with 10:50 left.
Standings update
Northern Iowa has beaten UIC, 74-52, to move to 14-5 in the Valley.
Braves are 13-5 with this game in the works, and trying to keep pace with UNI ahead of regular-season finale between the two on Sunday.
Braves without a 3
Bradley hits the 12-under break with a 12-11 lead. They are 0 of 4 from 3-point range. Points in the paint are 10-4 in BU's favor.
Braves with early lead
Christian Davis going to work on the boards, grabs an offensive rebound and tips in layup to put BU up 6-5.
Davis then grabs defensive rebound and gets Zek Montgomery started toward a mid-range jumper for 8-5 lead as the 16-under break arrives.
Starting lineups
The Braves stick with guards Duke Deen and Zek Montgomery, wing Christian Davis, forward Darius Hannah and center Ahmet Jonovic.
Valpo goes with guards Jefferson De La Cruz Monegro, All Wright, Darius DeAveiro and Tyler Schmidt, with forward Cooper Schwieger.
MVC Tournament projected seeding
Drake has clinched the No. 1 seed in the MVC Tournament and Belmont has clinched the No. 4 seed.
Bradley and Northern Iowa are tied in between and will likely settle the No. 2 and No. 3 seed position on Sunday when the Panthers face the Braves in Peoria.
If Bradley beat UNI to split the season series, and the teams exit the season finale tied in the standings, the higher seed will go to the Braves because they have a better NCAA Net ranking. At least, as of today. Noted analytics modeler Matt Hackman has Bradley at a 62% chance for No. 2.
It might seem like a little thing, but the No. 3 seed in the Arch Madness schedule plays its quarterfinal round game at 8:30 p.m. Friday night, the latest start of the tournament. The last No. 3 seed to come out of that 8:30 start and go on to win the tournament was Indiana State in 2011 season.

title: House approves bill on TikTok that would force sale or effectively ban company
author: Riley Beggin
description: The House approved a bill that would force TikTok's parent company to sell the social media app or face a practical ban in the U.S.
content:
WASHINGTON – The House approved a bill Wednesday that would force TikTok's parent company to sell the popular social media app or face a practical ban in the U.S.
President Joe Biden has said he would sign it if it makes it to his desk, but the legislation's fate is uncertain in the Senate, where the bill has proved much more divisive. The bill cleared the House 352 to 65 with one member voting present.
TikTok launched an intense lobbying campaign ahead of the House vote, urging its users to call their representatives and urge them to vote against the bill. The company's CEO Shou Chew also visited Capitol Hill on Tuesday in an effort to persuade lawmakers – mainly senators – to oppose it.
Former President Donald Trump waded into the debate as well, coming out against the bill and posting on Truth Social, his social media app, 'If you get rid of TikTok, Facebook and Zuckerschmuck will double their business,' referring to Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg.
The bill was fast tracked to the House floor after it was approved by the powerful House Energy and Commerce Committee last week by a unanimous vote of 50-0, a stunning, unusual sight for the lower chamber.
The legislation's proponents argue the app poses national security risks because its parent company, ByteDance, is based in Beijing and may expose American user data to Chinese government surveillance.
For its part, TikTok says it stores all American user data in a U.S.-based entity, and the storage is solely managed by the company's U.S.-based security. Their efforts, however, have evidently done little to alleviate lawmaker concerns.
As bipartisan as the bill's support was, the effort still received pushback from lawmakers who say an effective ban on the app would limit freedom of expression. Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., along with a handful of other progressive lawmakers, held a press conference Tuesday with TikTok content creators warning against an effective ban.
'Any ban on TikTok is not just banning the freedom of expression. You are literally causing huge harm to our national economy,' Garcia said, noting TikTok's use as a platform for small businesses.
The upper chamber has also been less bullish about the legislation. Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., has not said whether he would bring the House's bill up for a vote, explaining he would have to confer with committee chairs.
While most senators agree that TikTok's Chinese parent company poses a security threat to the United States, many have concerns about the legality of singling out one company.
Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., the chair of the Senate Commerce Committee, said Tuesday she's 'not sure' what her committee would do once the House passed the bill.
The committee has been 'working on this (issue) diligently for a while' with the goal of finding a tool that could stand up to legal scrutiny.
'The whole point here is you have a dilemma: You want free speech, but you also want the United States to have some ability to protect U.S. citizens or U.S. military from foreign actors who might be deleterious in what they would be using as a tool of communication,' she said.
Trump attempted to ban TikTok when he was president, but it was blocked by courts for failing 'to adequately consider an obvious and reasonable alternative,' a federal judge wrote at the time.
Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, the top Republican on the Commerce Committee, said he has 'deep concerns' with TikTok, but said he hasn't looked at the House bill yet.
Some lawmakers are instead proposing Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va.'s RESTRICT Act, which has bipartisan support and would allow the Commerce Department to further regulate foreign social media apps.
Warner, who chairs the Senate Intelligence Committee, said Tuesday he thinks it's 'good news' that the House was poised to pass the bill, but 'I have some different ideas.'
Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., said Monday he would block speedy passage in the Senate because it 'violates the First Amendment rights of 180 million Americans.'
Others have said they're strongly supportive of any effort to block TikTok.
'I think if you get it to a vote, it's hard to vote no on,' Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., who supports the House bill and banning TikTok generally, said Monday. 'But I think there will be a fierce effort to prevent any vote.'

title: Can Bradley basketball make the NIT? Here's what we know about the BU's chances in 2024
author: Dave Eminian
description: Bracketologists like the Bradley Braves chances of earning a bid to the 2024 NIT. Here's what we know.
content:
PEORIA — The Bradley Braves know they have no path to the NCAA Tournament after their loss in the semifinals of the 2024 Missouri Valley Conference Tournament on Saturday.
But the Braves, with a record of 22-11, also have good reason to believe their 2023-24 postseason journey is not over. Projections have them earning a berth in the NIT.
"These guys up here with me (at the Valley postgame podium), all those guys in the locker room, I don't think we're done playing," Bradley coach Brian Wardle said Saturday after his Braves built a 14-point lead over Drake, but eventually lost, 72-67, in the final two minutes of the semifinals. "But we obviously wanted to get to the NCAA Tournament … it's pretty hard on us all."
Can Bradley make the 2024 NIT?
The NIT field is 32 teams, including 12 automatic bids from the Power 6 conferences of Atlantic Coast, Big East, Big Ten, Big 12, Pac-12 and Southeastern. The Braves seem like a solid fit for the tournament, in which they played last postseason and lost to Wisconsin.
"That's what I've heard (NIT as a possibility for BU)," Wardle said. "We won't be in the NCAA, no way. It stinks to say that, but that's the reality of it, unfortunately. We know that. I love what I've seen in (NIT) projections. We're not a lock, but hopefully we can maybe keep playing, we'll see."
One well-regarded NIT bracketology site, The Barking Crow, updated its projected field on Monday and showed Bradley in the tournament facing No. 3 seed Syracuse in a New Mexico Region that includes No. 1 New Mexico, No. 2 Ohio State, No. 3 Syracuse, No. 4 Mississippi plus Bradley, Oregon, SMU and Butler. That predictive model — which updates with 10,000 simulations daily — showed Bradley leading all teams on Monday with a 99.7% chance of earning an NIT invite.
The site dratings.com had Bradley among the "top four unseeded" teams, or in the 17th-20th range. The site nitbracketology.com has Bradley as one of four unseeded teams in a quadrant with seeded teams Pittsburgh, Butler, Cincinnati and Iowa — but that part of the bracket was deemed "fluid" by the creator.
What changes did the NIT make in 2024?
The NCAA bought the NIT years ago for $56.5 million, but announced a significant change in how the tournament field is filled in 2024.
Gone are automatic NIT bids for teams that won their regular-season conference championships but lost their conference postseason tournament. In its place, the NCAA reached an agreement with the Power Six conferences to give automatic bids to the NIT to the top two teams in each conference (based on NCAA Net rankings) that don't make the NCAA Tournament.
It was a move in part to head off a scheme proposed by Fox Sports in 2023 in which the network wanted to sign deals with the top five conferences requiring their best non-NCAA Tournament teams play in a proposed new tournament.
Instead, the NIT stayed alive under a similar deal struck by the NCAA with the top six major conferences.
Will Indiana State make the NCAA Tournament?
National media and bracketology sites are lining up behind Indiana State in lobbying for an NCAA at-large bid. It's loud, and will get louder as the week goes on.
NCAA Net rankings, updated through Sunday's games, showed Indiana State at No. 29 (previously 26) and Drake at No. 47 (previously 47). So their title game Sunday had virtually no impact on one key metric used by the NCAA Tournament Selection Committee's selection process. Another top metric site, Kenpom.com, has Indiana State at No. 43 and Drake at No. 50.
Indiana State's NET ranking is within range of a traditional NCAA at-large bid, but the argument against the Sycamores remains their 1-4 record against teams ranked in the top 25 percent of all teams, or Quad 1.
The Valley should be a two-bid league this season. We'll know Sunday if the committee agrees.
Here is a sampling of bracketology for Indiana State:
Indiana State is the top team in the "Last Four In" category for DJ Bauer's well-respected bracketology site, Bauertology.
ESPN's bracketology, under Joe Lunardi, had Indiana State in on Monday, and the Sycamores were in the "Last Four In" category.
Barking Crow's predictive model rates Indiana State at 59% to grab an NCAA bid.
MVC coaching changes
Three Missouri Valley Conference coaches were fired over the weekend. Here is a rundown:
UIC fired coach Luke Yaklich on Sunday. The LaSalle, Illinois, native and former LaSalle-Peru high school coach was 47-70 in four seasons at UIC's helm. His No. 11-seeded team upset No. 6 seed SIU on Thursday night in the Valley tournament.
SIU coach Bryan Mullins was fired after the weekend. He was 86-68 in five seasons at his alma mater, including a 19-13 record this season.
Missouri State coach Dana Ford was also fired on Sunday. He was 106-82 in six seasons with the Bears.
Dave Eminian is the Journal Star sports columnist, and covers Bradley men's basketball, the Rivermen and Chiefs. He writes the Cleve In The Eve sports column for pjstar.com. He can be reached at 686-3206 or deminian@pjstar.com. Follow him on X.com @icetimecleve.

title: This East Peoria buffet is now open. Here's what to know before you go
author: Cassidy Waigand
description: The new buffet will offer a variety of American dishes such as pizza, pock chops and wings.
content:
The wait is over, buffet lovers.
Farmer's Buffet − located at 206 W. Camp St. in East Peoria − is open for business. The building had once operated as Grand Village Buffet but was most recently home to Pho Noodle House.
The community has been abuzz with discussions about the fate of Pho Noodle House and speculation about the buffet's opening. So, here's what to know before visiting Farmer's Buffet.
What's on the menu at Farmer's Buffet?
Customers will find a variety of American dishes at Farmer's Buffet. Before the restaurant's opening, owner Sam Mach said the business would include a salad bar, a carving station, a dessert bar and menu items such as:
Pork chops
Chicken wings
Pizza
Meatloaf
Mach said he planned to offer daily specials at Farmer's Buffet, as well.
How much does the buffet cost?
According to a photo uploaded by the business on Google, Farmer's Buffet will charge $19.50 for adults. Those 65 and older can dine for $17.50, and to-go orders are listed for $12 per pound. The price varies for children 3 to 14 years old − ranging from $3 to $17.
Beverages are offered for an additional charge. These include:
Fountain drink for $2
Tea for $3.50
Coffee for $5
When is Farmer's Buffet open?
The buffet will be open from 11:30 a.m. until 7 p.m. Thursday through Sunday, according to Google. Farmer's Buffet will be closed Monday through Wednesday.
