title: Raising Cane's location in the works for Peoria. Here's what we know
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Work has started on the Peoria property that will become a location of the popular chicken chain.
content:
Fourth District City Councilmember Andre Allen hopes to see the restaurant open in late winter or early spring of 2026.
Raising Cane's staple, and sole, entrée is its chicken fingers.
The lot was formerly home to Firestone Tire but has been vacant for a number of years.
In Peoria, a Raising Cane's location is in the works. The city's first storefront is working to open at 4200 N. Sterling Ave. in Peoria – right next to Northwoods Mall.
Fourth District City Councilmember Andre Allen told the Journal Star he learned a company was interested in developing the former Firestone Tire building late last summer.
'It's been dormant for a number of years,' Allen said. 'Honestly, it's become somewhat of an eyesore. And so, I was immediately interested that there was a development company that was interested in that space.'
Allen said he coordinated a meeting with Quattro Development and various city staff members. He said the conversation went well, and now, the company is working to bring Raising Cane's to the community.
Need a break? Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
Quattro Peoria Deux LLC and Joseph Urbana Investments LLC purchased the property from WPG Management Associates Inc. for $1 million late last year.
On Thursday morning, an excavator worked to demolish and clear away the former Firestone building that currently sits on the lot.
Allen expects work on the building to begin in early summer once demolition is completed. Should everything progress smoothly, he hopes to see the restaurant open in late winter or early spring of 2026.
'I'm excited not only to bring a national recognized restaurant and franchise to District 4 in the city of Peoria and the greater Peoria region,' Allen said, 'but also, too, anytime you can address blight – which that Firestone had unfortunately become – on a popular corridor of our district right in front of Northwoods Mall ... it's a win-win.'
Raising Cane's staple – and sole – entrée is its chicken fingers. Fans can currently find one storefront in Springfield, which is over an hour away from Peoria.
While Allen has never visited a Raising Cane's restaurant before, he looks forward to visiting the coming storefront.
'I'm excited for it,' Allen said. 'I'm excited to bring my wife and my kids to check it out. I hear great things about it.'
In a statement to the Journal Star, a Raising Cane's representative said:
"The Crew at Raising Cane's is excited to expand in Illinois and we are actively exploring opportunities to bring our signature ONE LOVE® – craveable Chicken Finger meals – to Peoria. We cannot confirm this location at this time, but are always looking for the right sites to bring Raising Cane's to the Community!"
The Journal Star also reached out to Quattro Development for comment and is awaiting a reply.

title: HGTV lists this Illinois town as the most charming in the state
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: HGTV released list of the 50 most charming small towns in America, and this Illinois town is said to be the most charming in the state.
content:
Alton, Illinois, is a history buff's dream, nestled along the Mississippi River where the Great River Road meets Route 66, where it beckons visitors with its quaint traditions, riverside views and limestone bluffs.
HGTV named Alton one of the 50 most charming small towns in America, spotlighting its nature and historical significance. Founded in 1837, Alton sits on the Illinois-Missouri border, just 35 minutes from St. Louis — but has plenty of its own charm to offer visitors and locals.
HGTV did not explain what it considered a "small town," but includes Alton and its population of 25,000. Here's why the town placed in HGTV's top 50 small towns.
Alton's limestone bluffs
With a 3,000-mile-long scenic route running through the town, there are picturesque views and towering white cliffs that might make them forget they're in the Midwest. There are several parks, including Cliff Cave County Park and Two Rivers National Wildlife Refuge for a more immersive experience. The area also is known for its spectacular views conducive to eagle-watching — so good, in fact, that locals come together every year in January and February for the Alton Audubon Eagle Ice Festival.
McPike Mansion
Alleged to be one of the most haunted towns in America, the town's McPike Mansion is a three-story mansion where at least 10 spirits are said to haunt the grounds. Built by Henry Guest McPike in 1869, the mansion is owned today by Sharyn and George Luedke but has not been occupied since the 1950s.
McPike Mansion has been featured on multiple supernatural-focused television programs and frequently catches the attention of paranormal groups. Many psychics and mediums have felt the presence of spirits, and photos often show figures, orbs and balls of light, according to the mansion's website.
Jazz and abolitionist history
HGTV highlights Alton's rich local history, including being the birthplace of legendary jazz singer Miles Davis, who was raised in nearby East St. Louis.
In the 19th century, Alton grew into an industrial river trading town and became an important site for abolitionists and fleeing enslaved people due to Illinois' status as a free state. Abolitionist printer Elijah P. Lovejoy came to Alton to print and distribute anti-slavery material.
On the western side of the Clark Bridge, at a spot once called Sunflower Island, a monument marks the site of the duel between Abraham Lincoln and then-state auditor James Shields, who found themselves squabbling during Lincoln's stint in the state legislature. The same spot holds a grave site for the 260 Confederate prisoners buried on the island.
HGTV also recognized the Alton Military Prison, which opened in 1833 and was Illinois' first state penitentiary.

Freshman Will Riley (12.2 ppg, 3.9 rpg, 2.3 apg) was named the Big Ten Sixth Man of the Year. The 6-foot-8 forward, expected to be a first-round NBA Draft pick, is the second Illini to win the award since it began in 2006, joining Andre Curbelo in 2021.
Freshman Kasparas Jakucionis, a possible lottery pick in the upcoming NBA Draft, was named third-team Big Ten All-Conference and to the league's all-freshman team. The 6-foot-6 guard led Illinois in scoring at 15.2 ppg, along with 5.6 rpg and 4.8 apg.
Sophomore 7-footer Tomislav Ivisic (12.6 ppg, 7.6 rpg) was selected as an all-conference honorable mention pick by the media.

title: Man identified as victim of deadly crash with semi in Tazewell County
author: Zach Roth
description: The 67-year-old was pronounced dead at the scene after his vehicle collided with a semi near Tremont.
content:
A Danvers man was killed Tuesday after his vehicle collided with a semi truck while he exited off Interstate 155 in Tazewell County.
The Tazewell County Coroner's Office said that Charles Jackson, 67, was pronounced dead at the scene at 4:01 p.m. after his car collided with a semi at the top of the off-ramp along the Townline Road exit near Tremont.
Law enforcement and emergency services were called to the scene at 2:56 p.m., after Jackson took the Townline Road exit and was hit by a semi while he attempted to turn onto the road.
An autopsy is scheduled for Friday.

title: Keith Urban, Jonas Brothers added to Illinois State Fair Grandstand lineup. What to know
author: Steven Spearie
description: Two more headliners have been added to the Illinois State Fair musical lineup. We have everything you need to know.
content:
Grammy-winning country singer Keith Urban and the Jonas Brothers have been added as headliners at the Grandstand at the 2024 Illinois State Fair.
Urban will perform Aug. 9 while the Jonas Brothers will take the stage Aug. 15.
Here's what you need to know.
Who is Keith Urban?
Started off in Australia and grew to be one of the biggest names in country music. Some of his hits include 'Blue Ain't Your Color,' 'Wasted Time," 'Somebody Like You," 'Long Hot Summer' and 'One Too Many'.
Throughout his career he has won four Grammy Awards, two People's Choice Awards and 13 CMA Awards. He also was inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2023.
Opening for Urban will be Canadian singer MacKenzie Porter ('Thinking ‘Bout You').
Who are the Jonas Brothers?
The Jonas Brothers -- Kevin, Joe and Nick -- emerged nearly 20 years ago from their appearances on the Disney Channel television network.
With 20 million in album sales, the trio has garnered three top 10 hits -- "Sucker," which went to number one, and "Burnin' Up" and "Tonight."
The Jonas Brothers recently claimed a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.
How much are tickets?
Tickets for the Jonas Brothers are $85-$150 and go on sale at 10 a.m. Saturday through Ticketmaster. Tickets for Urban are also $85-$150 and available through Ticketmaster.
Can I get tickets at the box office?
The state fair box office opens in June for in-person/phone sales from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday. Call 217-782-1979 or 217-782-6661 for any additional inquiries.
Who else is performing?
Other headline acts booked to perform at the fair are Mötley Crüe (Aug. 10); Jason Isbell and the 400 Unit with Ashley McBryde on Aug. 11 and Jordan Davis with Ashley Cooke and King Calaway on Aug. 13.
When is the state fair?
The fair runs from Aug. 8-18.
For more information visit the Illinois State Fair website.

title: Thousands of dollars raised for families of fatal school bus, semi crash in Illinois
author: Claire Grant
description: More than $39,000 has been donated in a matter of days following a fatal crash involving a school bus and semi-truck roughly 60 miles from Springfield.
content:
Residents from Illinois and all over the country are coming together to support the mourning families after a fatal crash involving a school bus and semi-truck crash in Rushville, Illinois, which took the lives of two adults and three children on Monday.
A GoFundMe was set up following the tragedy to support the grieving families of the children for funeral arrangements that will need to be made following the loss of their family members.
Authorities identified the victims as:
5-year-old Maria Miller, of Rushville.
3-year-old Andrew Miller, of Rushville.
3-year-old Noah Driscoll, of Rushville.
57-year-old Angela Spiker, of Rushville.
72-year-old David Coufal, of Browning.
Since Monday, the GoFundMe has already raised over $39,000 in assistance to the families, with 552 donations.
'Every contribution, big or small, will make a difference and show these families that they're not alone during this incredibly difficult time,' organizer for donations Dominic Thurman wrote on the page. 'Your support will help cover funeral expenses, medical bills, and other unforeseen costs, allowing these families to focus on healing without the added stress of financial worries.'
Funeral arrangements will be made public by the Worthington Funeral home website at a later date for Noah, Maria and Andrew.
The crash happened around noon in Schuyler County, about 60 miles northwest of Springfield. The school bus was heading eastbound when the bus crossed into the west lane and collided with a semi-truck, according to authorities.
The vehicles became engulfed in flames, where both drivers and children riding were pronounced dead at the scene by police.
To support the Driscoll-Miller assistance fund, anyone can donate to the GoFundMe online or share the website by Facebook or email, which have links on the website's page.
Illinois State Police are investigating the crash.

title: Ahead of primary in Illinois, Trump renews war of words with Pritzker
author: Zach Roth
description: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker said that Democrats would rather have Donald Trump on the ballot due to his negative impact on fellow Republicans.
content:
Former U.S. President Donald Trump took a shot at Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker during a rally Saturday in Dayton, Ohio, reigniting a public feud between the two politicians ahead of the primaries in both states.
While speaking to a crowd at the headquarters of an aviation fuel supplier at Dayton International Airport, Trump said of Pritzker that he, "wants to eat all the time. 'I'll have five burgers, please.' Who the hell orders five burgers?" The quote was a shot at Pritzker's weight.
The quotes about Pritzker came during the same speech in which Trump said that if President Joe Biden won re-election in November, it would be a "bloodbath" for the country. Pritzker endorsed Biden last March.
As expected from a high-ranking Democrat, Pritzker has been a long-time critic of Trump, attacking his rhetoric on issues such as immigration and the state of American democracy. After Trump referred to his political opponents as "vermin" in a speech in November 2023, the governor said that Trump's language was reminiscent of that of Nazi Germany in the 1930s. Pritzker said that he was concerned about the direction of the county if Trump was brought back into power.
"In Germany in the 1930s people that they didn't want to have power, people that they wanted to separate and segregate, they began calling them immigrants, even people who had been in Germany for generations," Pritzker said in an interview on MSNBC. "This is a way to begin to segregate people and then eventually dehumanize and kill people."
Pritzker continued his attacks on the 45th president earlier this month during a fundraising speech in Virginia, calling him "stupid and ignorant" and asking Democrats to be on the offensive against Trump's attacks.
"Don't mince words in the fight of your life," Pritzker said. "Don't hold back. This is an existential battle. I'm done giving any of these insurrectionists the benefit of the doubt. I'm done pretending that we can debate nuance in this fight."
During another MSNBC interview the following day, Pritzker said that Democrats were looking forward to having Trump as their opponent, despite polling showing him with a slight edge over Biden nationally and in the battleground states.
"He's in trouble in Illinois," Pritzker said. "We want him on the ballot because he's a detriment to Republicans across the United States but especially in Illinois."
Both Biden and Trump have reached the necessary number of delegates to clinch their party's respective nomination, which will be made official at the party conventions in Milwaukee from July 15-18 for the Republicans and in Chicago from Aug. 19-22 for the Democrats.

title: March Madness 2024: How deep can the Illini go in the NCAA Tournament? We take a look
author: Wes Huett
description: How far can the No. 3-seeded Fighting Illini of Illinois go in the NCAA Tournament? Here's what the experts have to say ahead of March Madness.
content:
The NCAA Tournament field of 68 is set and the Illinois Fighting Illini earned a No. 3 seed in the East Region behind No. 2 seed Iowa State and No. 1 seed UConn — the defending champion and tournament favorite.
The Illini (26-8) won the Big Ten tournament championship and now face No. 14 seed Morehead State in a first-round game Thursday in Omaha.
How deep can the Illini advance in the bracket? We took a spin around the Internet to see how pundits felt the Illini will fare in March Madness.
Andy Katz, NCAA.com
Iconic college basketball expert Andy Katz has Illinois defeating Iowa State in the Sweet 16 before a matchup with No. 1 seed UConn in the Elite Eight.
"I just love the way the Illini are playing right now," Katz wrote, but he says UConn will eventually be too much.
"These games will be in Boston, so it's a de-facto home game for the Huskies," Katz wrote. "It will be an absolute war between these two teams, it's going to be incredibly intense, but In a late-possession game I like UConn to get to the Final Four for a chance at back-to-back championships."
Who wins March Madness game? Morehead State vs Illinois picks, predictions, odds
Sports Illustrated
Both of Sports Illustrated's experts, Kevin Sweeney and Pat Forde, have the Illini getting back both Morehead State and No. 6 seed BYU before losing to Iowa State in the Sweet 16.
Fox Sports
John Fanta of FOX Sports has the Illini losing to BYU in the second round before the Cougars bow to Iowa State in the Sweet 16.
His colleague, Michael Cohen of FOX Sports, has the Illini going a bit further — advancing to the Elite Eight before a loss to No. 1 UConn. He has the Illini defeating BYU and Iowa State on the way.
SBNation
Ricky O'Donnell at SB Nation has the Illini advancing to the Elite Eight before a fateful meeting with No. 1 tournament favorite UConn.
O'Donnell has the Illini facing three double-digit seeded teams in Morehead State, Duquense and Drake in the first three rounds, which would be quite the fortuitous path for the Illini.
"The Illini finally make the second weekend under Brad Underwood, and advance all the way to the Elite Eight," wrote O'Donnell. "We'll take UConn over Illinois to reach the Final Four. Danny Hurley's team checks every box for a potential national champion, and this is the first step by winning the region."
Bleacher Report
Bleacher Report writer Kerry Miller also has the Illini advanced to the Elite Eight and again falling short to tournament favorite UConn — but the Illini did make him think about an upset.
"Though I had already decided before the brackets were announced that I would be picking Connecticut to win it all, I did pause for a moment here," Miller wrote. "Illinois is a very good, very large team that has been hot for a few weeks. But I don't trust the Illini's defense in this matchup against the most efficient offense in the nation. Could be one hell of a game, though ... "

title: Former IVC state champion earns national track and field coaching honor
author: Adam Duvall
description: Illinois Valley Central graduate Zach Glavash was named the nation's top college assistant track and field coach.
content:
Zach Glavash was named the 2024 U.S. Track & Field and Cross Country Coaches Association men's national assistant coach of the year on Monday.
The Texas Tech sprints and hurdles assistant coach — an Illinois Valley Central grad — helped guide the Red Raiders to the 2024 NCAA indoor national champion in Boston earlier this month. His coaching was instrumental in Terrence Jones winning back-to-back 60-meter dash national titles, with Don'Dre Swint taking third and Caleb Dean finishing sixth in the event.
"Love our team," Glavash posted on Twitter. "Blessed to work with incredible people. Such amazing coaches, athletes and administration. A close friend once told me 'We just drive the bus.' ... It's all about the athlete."

title: Pekin Starbucks workers petition for union membership
author: Mike Kramer
description: Workers at the Pekin Starbucks store joined employees at eight other stores in filing petitions for union membership Wednesday.
content:
Workers at the Starbucks store at 3442 Court St., Pekin filed a petition Wednesday with the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) to unionize with Starbucks Workers United.
They are joined by baristas at nine Starbucks stores in eight states who announced they are also seeking union elections.
According to a Wednesday press release from Starbucks Workers United, the announcements mark one of the largest busiest days for union petition filing since the campaign began in 2021.
'We are all united through shared experiences and in our demand for fair and consistent scheduling,' wrote workers from a dozen stores in a co-authored letter to Starbucks Chief Executive Officer Laxman Narasimhan. 'Overwhelmed skeleton crews face constant pressure to keep up with orders, meet drive-through times and fulfill an ever-growing menu of promotions.'
The workers added that they 'look forward to forging a productive relationship based on mutual respect' and to using their 'voices to help make the company stronger.'
The Pekin Starbucks workers join 10,000 union baristas at more than 400 union stores nationwide organizing to better their working conditions, including living wages, fair scheduling and policies that respond to discrimination and harassment on the job. The campaign hinges on peer-to-peer worker-led organization.
'I'm joining this movement so that we can finally be heard by the company,' said Kat Flores a barista and union organizer at the Pekin Starbucks location. 'Starbucks is always talking about the third-place policy, but it feels as if it only applies to customers. Most baristas that I know spend more time at Starbucks than we do with our own families. Starbucks should be a third place for us too. When customers think of Starbucks, they don't think of some corporate employees sitting behind a desk, they think of the baristas that they see every day when they stop in to get their morning cup of coffee on their way to work. We deserve to have fair, consistent scheduling, a livable wage, and to feel safe at work.'
The filings come just weeks after Starbucks Workers United and Starbucks announced an agreement to begin discussions on a foundational framework to achieve collective bargaining agreements for represented stores and partners; the resolution of litigation between the union and the company, including brand litigation; and a fair process for workers to organize.
The move signals an about-face for Starbucks from past policies related to workers.
In more than fifty separate decisions, federal administrative law judges found that Starbucks had committed more than 400 violations of federal labor law, including dozens of unlawful firings, refusal to bargain, and denying benefits and wage increases to union members that are offered at non-union stores.
Since 2021, more than 400 Starbucks stores in 42 states and the District of Columbia have successfully unionized.

title: Pekin bicentennial event invites residents to learn local history for prize package
author: Mike Kramer
description: Pekinites are being encouraged to explore local historic sites at a chance for a prize package as the city celebrates its 200th birthday.
content:
As Pekin celebrates its 200 th birthday, the Pekin Bicentennial Committee has created an event that will encourage Pekinites to explore local historic sites for a chance at a prize package.
Participants in Pekin's Historic Adventure Quest will use their GPS-enabled devices to travel to 20 different locations throughout the city. Each site will provide a letter or number needed to unscramble a prominent Pekin woman's name and the year and an important year in the city's history.
'It's called geo-caching,' said Adventure Quest coordinator Lindsay Jameson. 'You use GPS coordinates to go locate caches out in the city.'
Jameson added that clues to the puzzle will be placed in historic locations including the Carl Herget Mansion, the Dirksen Congressional Center, and Legins-Costley Park. Containers will be placed at 10 of the locations, while caches at the other 10 will consist only of information.
'I think it will be fun because it's a way to get out in the community and out into nature a little bit,' she said. 'People can explore some sites they didn't know were there, or maybe learn some more about a site they already knew about. It's a way to get everybody involved. Kids of all ages will enjoy it, and so will adults.'
Clues to the Quest will be posted Apr. 1 on pekinbicentennial.com.
The activity is designed so a participant can collect clues in a day or spread out the adventure throughout the year, said Jameson. Once contestants have gathered all of the clues to solve the puzzle, they must submit their correct answers by Dec. 31. A drawing will take place Jan. 6, 2025.
The winner will receive a prize package that includes locally printed three-dimensional Flat Everett, $50 in Chamber Checks that are redeemable at various local businesses, and a selection of official Pekin Bicentennial swag.

title: Illinois' Marcus Domask records 10th NCAA Tournament triple-double in March Madness history
author: Ehsan Kassim
description: Illinois' Marcus Domask on Thursday became the 10th player ever to record a triple-double in the NCAA Tournament. More on his historic achievement:
content:
Marcus Domask etched his name in NCAA Tournament lore on Thursday.
The Illinois basketball guard recorded the 10th triple-double in March Madness history vs. 14 seed Morehead State with a 12-point, 11-rebound and 10-assist performance in an 85-69 Fighting Illini victory over Morehead State.
Domask notched his triple-double with a 3-pointer with 2:57 remaining in the game. He and the other starters were subbed following the basket, with Illinois leading by 24. Ja Morant recorded the last NCAA Tournament triple-double, for Murray State, against Marquette in the first round of the 2019 NCAA Tournament.
Domask, from Waupun, Wisconsin, came into the game averaging 16.0 points, 4.9 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game. He joins an exclusive list of players to record a triple-double in an NCAA Tournament game.
The Fighting Illini will play No. 11 Duquesne in the second round on Saturday.
Marcus Domask triple-double
Here's a look at Domask recording the 10th triple-double in NCAA Tournament history:
How many NCAA Tournament triple-doubles are there?
Domask's triple-double is the 10th in NCAA Tournament history. Prior to his outing vs. Morehead State, the most recent March Madness triple-double came in 2019, from Murray. The first came from Michigan's Gary Grant in 1987.
To date, only Michigan State's Draymond Green has more than one triple-double in NCAA Tournament history: He recorded his first in 2011, and his second in 2012 (both in the second round). The furthest into the tournament a triple-double has occurred was the Elite Eight, first by Utah's Andre Miller in 1998 and then by Marquette's Dwyane Wade in 2003.

title: Hit-and-run accident that killed 23-year-old Galesburg woman remains unsolved
author: Dean Muellerleile
description: Destiny Dixon, 23, the mother of two young daughters, was among multiple motorists who stopped to help a victim of a rollover crash.
content:
Illinois State Police are seeking the public's assistance in the investigation of the January hit-and-run death of a Galesburg woman who tried to help another driver who was trapped inside his vehicle after a rollover crash.
Destiny Dixon, 23, the mother of two young daughters, was among multiple motorists who stopped to help the driver, ISP said in a news release.
On the evening of Jan. 1, 2024, ISP responded to a fatal hit-and-run collision on Interstate 55 northbound near Braceville, in Grundy County, the release said. Dixon was standing near the rolled vehicle when another motorist drove through the crash scene at a high rate of speed, striking her and another, male, subject. Dixon later died as a result of her injuries.
The offending driver fled the scene northbound on I-55 and was last seen near the I-80 interchange, the release said. The vehicle was identified as a dark gray 2010-2011 Mitsubishi Endeavor. The vehicle sustained significant damage to the front left corner, left side headlight, and left side mirror.

title: Where is Duquesne basketball? Location, more about Illinois' NCAA Tournament second round foe
author: Craig Meyer
description: Here's more to know about Duquesne, Illinois' second-round NCAA Tournament foe, including location, pronunciation and its connection to LeBron James
content:
Even before the 2024 NCAA Tournament officially tipped off earlier this week, the Duquesne basketball program was one of the best, most compelling stories of March Madness.
The Dukes entered the Atlantic 10 Tournament as the 15-team league's No. 6 seed, but reeled off four wins over a five-day stretch to earn the conference's automatic bid to the NCAA Tournament, marking their first appearance in the Big Dance since 1977.
Once there, Duquesne continued to make history, upsetting No. 6 seed BYU 71-67 Thursday to earn the program's first NCAA Tournament victory since 1969 and set up a second-round matchup with No. 3 seed and Big Ten Tournament champion Illinois.
The Dukes have the profile of a burgeoning Cinderella. There was the since-snapped tournament drought that had turned the once-proud program into an afterthought. The person who led it to that destination, coach Keith Dambrot, is the son of a former Duquesne standout who played at the school during its heyday in the 1950s. On Monday, the 65-year-old Dambrot announced that he will retire at the end of this season, in part to help take care of his wife, Donna, as she continues treatment for breast cancer.
As the Dukes have thrust themselves into the national spotlight after decades away from it, they remain something of a mystery for casual fans and even some who follow the sport closely.
Heading into Saturday's contest against Illinois, here's everything you need to know about Duquesne:
Where is Duquesne located?
Location: Pittsburgh
Enrollment: 8,179
Duquesne is a private Catholic university located in the Uptown neighborhood of Pittsburgh, only two blocks from PPG Paints Arena, the home of the NHL's Pittsburgh Penguins.
Notable alumni include Art Rooney, the founder and former owner of the Pittsburgh Steelers, and former NBA all-star Norm Nixon. German filmmaker Werner Herzog briefly attended the university, but did not graduate. According to enrollment data from the school, it has a student population of 8,179.
How do you pronounce Duquesne?
Though it doesn't look like it, Duquesne is pronounced 'Doo-kane.'
The university is named after Michel-Ange Duquesne de Menneville, the governor of the New France colony in North America who is credited with being the first person to bring Catholic observances to Pittsburgh.
LeBron James-Duquesne connection
While there are bigger, more prestigious programs in the 68-team NCAA Tournament, few, if any, have a valid claim to a more famous fan than Duquesne.
NBA superstar LeBron James regularly posts on social media about the Dukes, including a congratulatory message on X, formerly known as Twitter, after the win Thursday against BYU. Before they began their NCAA Tournament march, Duquesne's players were gifted pairs of the Los Angeles Lakers forward's signature shoe.
Though James' connection to the Dukes may seem strange, it's deeply personal. Dambrot coached James for two seasons at St. Vincent-St. Mary High School in Akron, Ohio. The coach presumed to be Dambrot's successor, Duquesne associate head coach Dru Joyce III, was a high school teammate of James.
Duquesne basketball history
Despite going 47 years between NCAA Tournament appearances, Duquesne was once a national power.
In 1940, it became the first college basketball program to compete in the NCAA Tournament and the NIT in the same year, going to the Final Four in the former and losing in the championship game of the latter. Over a six-season stretch from 1950-55, it finished the season ranked in the top 10 nationally five times. In 1955, it won the NIT back when it was a more prestigious tournament than the NCAA Tournament.
The Dukes were also among the first programs to actively recruit and play Black players.
Duquesne's first Black player, Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Famer Cumberland Posey, joined the team in 1916, just two years after the Dukes played their first-ever game. In 1950, Duquesne all-American Chuck Cooper became the first Black player to be drafted by an NBA team after he was selected by the Boston Celtics with the No. 14 overall pick. In the 1954 NIT championship game, Duquesne had a starting lineup featuring three Black players and two Jewish players, with the latter group including Dambrot's father, Sid.
At that time, the Dukes regularly had some of the most talented players in the sport. Two of their players, Dick Ricketts and Sihugo Green, were selected as the No. 1 overall pick in back-to-back NBA drafts (1955 and 1956), making Duquesne the only program in college basketball history to manage that feat.

The skilled nursing facility Hallmark Healthcare of Pekin will host an early Easter celebration Friday for residents, area children, and families.

title: In a first, Rockford homicide suspect will walk under no-cash bail system
author: Jeff Kolkey
description: In a cashless bail first for Winnebago County, a Rockford homicide suspect will walk free pending trial.
content:
A Rockford man arrested in connection with a 2023 suspected gang-related killing will be released under provisions of the Pretrial Fairness Act.
Winnebago County State's Attorney J. Hanley said it is believed to be the first time anyone from Winnebago County charged with first-degree murder will be allowed to go free pending trial under the new no cash bail system.
Along with two other men, Marcus Copeland Jr., 25, of Rockford, was charged with first-degree murder, aggravated battery and aggravated discharge of a firearm in connection with the Feb. 8, 2023, shooting death of Joshua Ewing, 26. He has pleaded not guilty to the charges.
Although Winnebago County Judge Debra Schafer found there was probable cause to arrest Copeland, she ruled that prosecutors had not met the burden of "clear and convincing" evidence needed under the act to detain him until trial.
"The first prong, the first test, we have to meet, is can we prove the case by clear and convincing evidence — which is a higher standard than probable cause," Hanley said. "The judge found yesterday that while she acknowledged that we had proven probable cause despite the, I don't know, 46-page factual summary, we had not proved the case by clear and convincing evidence. The other two co-defendants were ordered detained."
Despite the ruling, Hanley said prosecutors plan to indict Copeland, and he is confident they will win a conviction at trial.
Copeland will be released from jail once officials with Winnebago County Probation confirm he has a phone landline that can be used for monitoring him. He is also ordered to have no contact with codefendants or members of the Ewing family and not to possess any firearms.
The Pretrial Fairness Act was implemented in September, ending the practice of posting monetary bail to be released from jail before trial. Proponents say money should not determine if someone is allowed freedom before they are proven guilty in court and it should instead be based on certain criteria.
Those include clear and convincing evidence the accused is guilty, that the accused poses a danger to a person or the community or is a flight risk. In addition, only certain mostly violent crimes are considered detainable unless someone is arrested after already being granted pretrial release.
Police say Ewing, a Rockford man, was shot while driving in the area of Chestnut and Winnebago streets by occupants of a white SUV. He crashed the black Volvo he was driving into other vehicles at First Avenue and Charles Street.
In addition to Copeland, officers with the Rockford Police Gang Crime Unit arrested co-defendants Michael Blue, 26, and Dezha Manning, 27. Both Blue and Manning were ordered held in the Winnebago County Jail before trial. They have pleaded not guilty.
Copeland's lawyer, Kunal Kulkarni, declined to comment on the pending criminal case.
"I believe the judge was on sound footing," Kulkarni said.

title: Downtown Pekin buildings getting new lease on life after sitting vacant more than 30 years
author: Mike Kramer
description: A Pekin couple purchased two buildings that have been vacant for over 30 years and is remodeling them for new storefronts.
content:
Two downtown Pekin buildings are being remodeled for new occupants after sitting vacant for more than 30 years.
'We need to get both buildings up to code,' said Crista Flynn of Pekin, who bought the buildings with her husband Gary last October. 'They need everything.'
Renovations needed for the buildings at 525 and 527 Court St. include rewiring, new roofing, a new HVAC (heating, ventilation and cooling) system, new flooring, renovated bathrooms and rehabilitated storefronts.
The Flynn's purchased the buildings for $75,000, and city of Pekin Economic Development Director Josh Wray said renovation costs for the properties are estimated at about $400,000.
At its March 11 meeting, the Pekin City Council unanimously approved a Tax Increment Financing (TIF) redevelopment agreement that will provide the Flynn's with $50,000 in annual TIF assistance for three years.
'Given the scope of work and outcome of two new storefronts that will be (useable) for years to come, with fire suppression and all the necessary improvements to meet code, staff recommends considering this a high impact project,' Wray said.
The Flynn's have already incurred over $100,000 in TIF-eligible expenses since purchasing the building, according to Wray.
Once renovations are complete, the Flynn's intend to rent the 2,800-square-foot space at 527 Court Street to their daughter, Ashley Simmons, to open the Take Two resale boutique and Gigi's Pet Treats there. The couple hopes to rent the 1,300-square-foot space at 525 Court Street to a local business.
'We really wanted to invest in downtown,' said Flynn. 'We both have great memories of downtown and hated seeing these buildings sitting empty. So, we invested in that.'
Flynn added that she hopes 527 Court Street will be remodeled to the point where Take Two and Gigi's Pet Treats can open this summer or fall. She expects 525 Court St. to be ready for occupancy next year.
'I'd love for it to be a retail store,' she said. 'But there's a lot of interest from people such as attorneys who want it for office space. We haven't committed to anybody yet.'

title: Rockford man reaches $5.4M settlement in wrongful conviction suit against Normal, officers
author: Jim Hagerty
description: Alan Beaman of Rockford spent 13 years in prison for a murder he didn't commit. On Monday, the town of Normal plans to approve a settlement.
content:
A Rockford man who spent nearly 13 years behind bars for a murder he didn't commit has reached a settlement in his wrongful conviction lawsuit.
Alan Beaman will receive $5.4 million from the Town of Normal to settle the suit he brought against the municipality and three retired officers he claims fixed a case against him that sent him to prison in the 1993 death of Illinois State University student Jennifer Lockmiller, his girlfriend at the time.
Because the settlement is still pending approval by the Normal Town Council, Beaman told the Rockford Register Star Friday that he cannot yet comment on the matter.
The Town of Normal issued a statement to council members, admitting no wrongdoing.
"The proposed settlement mitigates any risk of an excess verdict and protects the municipality from any excess verdict where damages could far exceed insurance coverage," the report said.
Beaman was a senior at Illinois Wesleyan University when Lockmiller was strangled to death on Aug. 28, 1993, inside her off-campus apartment. Police claimed Beaman drove 120 miles from Rockford, killed her, then raced back to his parents' home.
His legal team later showed there wasn't enough time for him to kill Lockmiller and make it home as prosecutors claimed at trial. They also argued that police failed to focus on others suspects, including men who were also seeing Lockmiller at the time.
Beaman's conviction was overturned in 2008 when the Illinois Supreme Court ruled there wasn't enough evidence to convict him.
A minimum of $4 million of the settlement will be paid through Normal's liability insurance pool. The remaining $1.4 million would be paid out of the general fund, the town's report said.
The Town of Normal City Council is expected to the approve the settlement Monday.
Beaman now lives in Rockford with his wife and two children.

title: Here are 5 bills that could impact your child's classroom in Illinois
author: Hope Gadson
description: One bill would ban corporal punishment inside private schools across Illinois while another would require schools to use electric buses.
content:
Illinois students returning from spring break are now entering the home stretch of the 2023-2024 academic year. Upcoming school years, however, could be significantly different as state lawmakers consider new legislation and budget funding requests from Gov. JB Pritzker.
Lawmakers are crafting a budget for the upcoming fiscal year starting in July, where education is again expected to be a major focus. For the Illinois State Board of Education, Pritzker is requesting $10.9 billion in state funds mostly going towards evidence-based funding for public schools.
It's also year two of the Smart Start Illinois initiative, a signature program for the governor aiming to provide universal preschool by 2027. This year, Pritzker calls for $400 million for Smart Start along with $13 million to establish the new state Department of Early Childhood.
Along with the budget there are several pieces of education legislation advancing in committee. Here's five bills to know that could be affecting your classroom.
Electric school buses
How your student gets to school could be changing in coming years.
Through House Bill 2287, led by Rep. Marty Moylan, D-Des Plaines, newly purchased and leased school buses would have to be electric starting in 2028. By 2035, all school districts would be required to have solely electric school buses.
The state is targeting having one million EVs on the road by 2030 but is not on pace to accomplish this goal. According to data from the Illinois Secretary of State's office, there are just less than 98,000 EVs in the state as of March 2024 — the plurality of which being in Cook County and surrounding counties.
Those purchasing EVs can receive up-to a $4,000 rebate from the state. Similarly, the new legislation would offer grants up to $200,000 to purchase or lease an electric school bus.
Teacher planning period
As a way to help teachers during the school day, Sen. Meg Loughran Cappel, D-Shorewood introduced Senate Bill 2721, a bill that would carve out at least 45 minutes during the school day for teachers to plan. The bill states that during the plan time an educator cannot be forced to substitute or attend meetings or training sessions. If this bill passes it will become a requirement for all public-school districts across the state.
The bill has caught the attention Springfield are school districts, including Rochester School District superintendent of schools Dan Cox, who expressed his concerns about the pending legislation.
'The nuance with this particular bill as it stands today is it can have a disproportionate or negative impact on instructional time for students,' Cox said in a recent interview. 'This bill would also likely have a greater impact on smaller school districts that don't have staff.'
Corporal punishment
Illinois has banned corporal punishment in public schools since 1994. That same policy has not been applied to private schools, yet new legislation could change that.
House Bill 4175 would prevent nonpublic schools from slapping or paddling a student, placing a student in a physically painful position and the intentional infliction of bodily harm on a student.
The bill comes from Rep. Margaret Croke, D-Chicago, and passed unanimously out of a House committee. It now awaits a full House vote before advancing to the Senate.
Passage of the legislation would make Illinois the fifth state in the nation to ban corporal punishment in private schools, joining New York, New Jersey, Maryland and Iowa.
Intentional down-time for students
In recent years it has been reported that more students are dealing with higher levels of stress and anxiety in school. This bill aims to help reduce those stress levels and help keep kids focused during the school day.
Introduced by Sen. Rachel Ventura, D-Joliet, Senate Bill 2872 would require each school district to offer relaxation time or relaxation activities for at least 20 minutes a week. The time would be used to emphasize self-care and downtime as a way to improve overall health.
The bill would also encourage schools to use various practices like yoga, meditation, mental health education and mindfulness practices.
New curriculum
What's being taught in the classroom could change in the coming years.
Before the House Elementary and Secondary Education: School Curriculum and Policies Committee are several bills that would require the teaching of Arab-American history, the impacts of climate change and a one-semester course on personal finance.

title: Election board demands 'media watchdog' sites remove Illinois voter data
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: The data appeared in dozens of articles purporting to show which voters in certain precincts had — and had not — voted in 2020.
content:
The Illinois State Board of Elections is asking the publisher of numerous Illinois websites to remove thousands of voters' personal data from the 2020 election from its sites.
Since late March, the agency says it has received calls from voters concerned their dates of birth and addresses were published on websites run by Local Government Information Services, a self-described 'media watchdog' based in Lake Forest, Illinois, that operates 20 websites and 11 print publications geared toward specific cities and regions of Illinois. Peoria is among the cities with such a website, dubbed the Peoria Standard.
The data appeared in dozens of articles purporting to show which voters in certain precincts had — and had not — voted in the 2020 presidential election.
Data on the Peoria Standard's website, as of Friday night, includes purported voter information for numerous precincts in central Illinois, including Peoria, East Peoria, Pekin, Washington, Morton, Creve Coeur and Tremont.
The site also lists town names such as 'Central E Town of Mortonship' and "Central S Town of Mackinawship."
The SBE, in a release issued Friday, said it did not provide the data to Local Government Information Services.
Under Illinois statute, political committees that are registered with the SBE are allowed to buy the agency's voter data for "bona fide political purposes." The data is not allowed for use in other business purposes.
The State Board of Elections is an independent state agency that has general supervision over how election laws are administered in Illinois. Elections are administered locally by 108 election authorities across the state.
The board of elections says in January 2018 it stopped providing voters' dates of birth in the voter file provided to such political committees.
Through communications with a representative of Local Government Information Services, the agency says it believes that the company combined 2016 and 2020 data sets for the voter stories. A copy of the 2016 voter file was likely used to obtain birth dates and street addresses that were published.
SBE says it believes the company gained access to the 2016 voter file because, at that time, it was affiliated with a political committee — Liberty Principles PAC, which funded its operations.
Liberty Principles PAC ended its financial support of the company in 2016 and closed in 2020, according to the election board.
It its statement Friday, the election board said it has confirmed some of the published voter lists are inaccurate. The agency also has asked the data be removed from the company's sites.
'While LGIS may arguably have had legal access to the voter data when it was being financed bya political committee, any semblance of legality ended when the relationship with the PAC was severedin 2016,' SBE Executive Director Bernadette Matthews said in the statement. 'In 2018, we decided to remove dates of birth from the voter file provided to political committees as an added security measure for voters. It isdisappointing when an organization shows such little regard for voters.'
SBE said it has contacted the Illinois Attorney General's Office about potential legal action.

title: Peoria County home listings asked for more money in March – see the current median price here
author: USA TODAY Network
description: Here's a look at how monthly real estate listings changed in Peoria County last month.
content:
The median home in Peoria County listed for $125,000 in March, slightly up from the previous month's $124,948, an analysis of data from Realtor.com shows.
Compared to March 2023, the median home list price decreased 4.2% from $124,225.
The statistics in this article only pertain to houses listed for sale in Peoria County, not houses that were sold. Information on your local housing market, along with other useful community data, is available at data.pjstar.com.
Peoria County's median home was 1,528 square feet, listed at $92 per square foot. The price per square foot of homes for sale is up 6.3% from March 2023.
Listings in Peoria County moved briskly, at a median 33 days listed compared to the March national median of 50 days on the market. In the previous month, homes had a median of 41 days on the market. Around 240 homes were newly listed on the market in March, a 44.6% increase from 166 new listings in March 2023.
The median home prices issued by Realtor.com may exclude many, or even most, of a market's homes. The price and volume represent only single-family homes, condominiums or townhomes. They include existing homes, but exclude most new construction as well as pending and contingent sales.
Across the Peoria metro area, median home prices rose to $149,900, up 0.1% from a month earlier. The median home had 1,618 square feet, at a list price of $95 per square foot.
In Illinois, median home prices were $316,900, a 0.1% increase from February. The median Illinois home listed for sale had 1,710 square feet, with a price of $180 per square foot.
Throughout the United States, the median home price was $424,900, a slight increase from the month prior. The median American home for sale was listed at 1,826 square feet, with a price of $228 per square foot.
The median home list price used in this report represents the midway point of all the houses or units listed over the given period of time. Experts say the median offers a more accurate view of what's happening in a market than the average list price, which would mean taking the sum of all listing prices then dividing by the number of homes sold. The average can be skewed by one particularly low or high price.

title: What time is the eclipse on Monday and how to watch solar eclipse 2024 in Illinois
author: Dean Muellerleile
description: Illinois is home to a rare total solar eclipse on April 8, 2024. We have important info about how to watch the eclipse and eclipse times.
content:
The solar eclipse is upon us.
As the day progresses and the 2024 celestial event crosses into Illinois, the Journal Star will provide coverage from the path of totality — where the effect is greatest — to the partial eclipse seen elsewhere in the state and the country.
But first, some basics:
What to know about the eclipse
During a total solar eclipse, the moon appears the same size as the sun and blocks the latter. The daytime darkness will last a few minutes within the path of totality — where the effect of the eclipse is greatest. Within the U.S., the eclipse path will stretch from Texas to Maine and includes, Illinois, Indiana and Ohio, among others. Only certain parts of those states will be within the path of totality.
Other parts of those states and the rest of the country will experience a partial eclipse.
What time is the eclipse on Monday?
The total eclipse enters the U.S. just after 01:27 p.m. central time April 8 at a point in Eagle Pass, Texas, according to eclipse2024.org. The eclipse will end in Maine at 3:35 p.m. eastern time. Even if you're not in the path of totality, you may still experience the eclipse to a lesser degree.
How to watch solar eclipse
Many people are traveling to the path of totality to see the total solar eclipse in Illinois or somewhere in the United States. Others will enjoy a partial eclipse outdoors. If you'd like to watch indoors, you also have options.
NASA will stream coverage of the solar eclipse on its various social channels, including an official broadcast and a telescope feed on YouTube.
Illinois solar eclipse 2024: Here's a traveler's guide with warnings and advice
Eclipse time by zip code
USA TODAY has an interactive graphic that shows you how the eclipse might look in major cities and, if you enter your zip code, it shows the start time of the partial eclipse, the length of totality and the end.
When does the eclipse start in Illinois?
A partial phase of the eclipse will begin in southern Illinois just before 12:42 p.m. near East Cape Girardeau, where totality will enter the state after 1:58 p.m. and last about 4 minutes. Totality will exit Illinois after 2:07 p.m. near Palestine. For a list of all communities in the path of totality, visit eclipse2024.org.

title: Country star Morgan Wallen arrested after throwing chair off rooftop for 'no legitimate purpose,' police say
author: Natalie Neysa Alund
description: Morgan Wallen was arrested after Nashville police said he threw a chair from a bar's 6-story rooftop, "an act that served no legitimate purpose."
content:
Country music singer Morgan Wallen was arrested overnight in Nashville on felony charges after he allegedly threw a chair from a downtown rooftop for "no legitimate purpose," police said.
Wallen, 30, was booked into jail early Monday morning on three counts of reckless endangerment and one count of disorderly conduct in connection to the late Sunday night incident, the Metro Nashville Police Department reported.
According to an arrest affidavit obtained by USA TODAY, at 10:53 p.m. local time, two police officers were standing in front of Chief's Bar in the city's entertainment district on Lower Broadway when they saw a chair fall from above and hit the street about three feet from them.
In the affidavit, police wrote, the bar's staff members told officers Wallen threw the chair, and when officers reviewed video footage of incident, it showed him "lunging and throwing an object off the roof."
Chief's Bar, owned by country music singer, Eric Church, is a six-story building.
Witnesses told police they stood next to the country singer and watched him 'pick up the chair, throw it over him, laughing afterward,' the affidavit continues.
Police wrote they arrested Wallen on reckless endangerment charges because two officers were in the area and the incident posed a danger to public.
The affidavit goes onto say officers arrested him for disorderly conduct because "he created a hazardous condition by an act that served no legitimate purpose."
Davidson County Sheriff's Office online records show Wallen was released from jail around 3:30 a.m. local time.
A court official told USA TODAY Wallen posted a $15,250 bond.
No injuries were reported.
In a statement issued to USA TODAY through his representatives, Wallen's lawyer, Worrick Robinson, confirmed knowledge of the arrest and wrote Wallen is "cooperating fully with authorities."
'Cowboy Carter' on the charts: Beyoncé's 'Cowboy Carter' becomes Spotify's most-streamed album in single day in 2024
Where is Morgan Wallen from?
Morgan was born in Sneedville, a small city in Hancock County, Tennessee, roughly 70 miles northeast of Knoxville.
In February, the singer announced he plans to open a six-story bar along Lower Broadway called "This Bar." The title comes from Wallen's 2019 song where he sings, "I found myself in this bar / Making mistakes and making new friends."
Morgan Wallen to open bar in Nashville: The country singer will open 'This Bar' downtown in 2024
Wallen previously criticized for video of him saying racial slur
The arrest is not the first time Wallen has drawn scrutiny for his actions in public.
In February of 2021, Wallen apologized after a video surfaced of him shouting a racial slur in Nashville that prompted swift backlash from the music industry.
In a video posted to YouTube, Wallen described what is depicted in the video as "hour 72 of 72 of a bender."
"Obviously, the natural thing to do is to apologize further and just continue to apologize but because you got caught and that's not what I wanted to do," the singer said in the video. "I let so many people down. And [people] who mean a lot to me and give so much to me. And that's just not fair."

title: Solar eclipse could be economic boom for Illinois and businesses
author: Patrick M. Keck
description: Favorable weather and a longer total exposure time has Illinois officials confident this year's eclipse will generate similar fortunes.
content:
Monday's total solar eclipse, spanning 128 miles in southern and southeastern regions of the state, is expected to draw more than 200,000 visitors to Illinois. And, with it, a major boost to tourism.
The state's most recent eclipse in 2017 saw $15 million to $18 million in total economic impact. Favorable weather and a longer total exposure time has Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity Office of Tourism deputy director Daniel Thomas confident the eclipse will generate similar fortunes.
Beyond the eclipse though, Thomas hopes travelers will take advantage of the area's outdoor opportunities on Saturday and Sunday.
"Maybe take a hike in one of our state parks, maybe people want to do rock climbing or canoeing or biking," he said in a phone interview. "There really is something for everyone and to really make an extended weekend getaway to see how beautiful the Southern Illinois region is."
The total eclipse will be best seen in Carbondale, where Southern Illinois University Carbondale is partnering with NASA to host the Southern Illinois Crossroads Eclipse Festival. Doors open for the event, held at Saluki Stadium seating 15,000, at 11 a.m. Thomas said businesses in the Carbondale-area made approximately $5 to $7 million from the 2017 eclipse.
Other sites for viewing are more than 30 Illinois state parks, recreation areas and wildlife areas are in the path of totality in addition to local viewing parties.
Besides the tourism dollars, businesses are also trying to cash in by offering eclipse-branded products and holding eclipse-themed events. Big Muddy Brewing in Murphysboro planned weekend events beginning on Friday with representatives of the Adler Planetarium in Chicago. On Sunday, the brewery will also host a Pink Floyd cover band to play 'Dark Side of the Moon.' On Monday, Chuck Stuhrenberg, owner and operator of Big Muddy Brewing, said he will let the heavens provide the entertainment.
'We will cede to the great show in the sky,' he said.
The size of the crowd depends on the weather, not only in southern Illinois, but along the path of totality.
'In 2017 during the eclipse, we had our absolute busiest day ever,' Stuhrenberg said. 'If it's cloudy in Texas, we can expect lots of travelers to head here and we will have an even busier day than we had in 2017.'
In addition to events, Big Muddy Brewing not only created a beer called Dark Noon, but they also collaborated with four other breweries in the path of totality. The collaboration yielded Sasquatch Black Lager with Molly's Pint, Totality Hazelnut Stout with St. Nicholas Brewing in DuQuoin and Murphysboro, Midnight Veil with Minglewood Brewery in Cape Girardeau, Missouri, and Dark Sour with Scratch Brewery in Ava.
Those making the trip south are recommended by the Illinois Department of Transportation to prepare for heavy interstate traffic both on the arrival and departure trips. They also ask drivers to not stop along roads or bridges, take photos or wear eclipse glasses while driving and to watch out for pedestrians.

title: Proposed annex to Tazewell County Justice Center takes one step closer to reality
author: Mike Kramer
description: New business at Monday's Pekin City Council meeting featured two actions in support of a proposed Tazewell County Justice Center annex.
content:
The proposed annex to Tazewell County Justice Center took a step closer to becoming a reality during Monday's Pekin City Council meeting.
Two items at the top of Monday's new business were an ordinance approving the vacation of the alley between Elizabeth Street and Court Street, from Capitol Street to 3rd Street, and a resolution to approve an intergovernmental agreement between the City of Pekin and Tazewell County for the sale of city-owned property on Court Street.
"It's great to be able to partner with the city on this new Justice Center project, which we feel will be a great addition to downtown,' said Tazewell County Administrator Mike Deluhery,
The city will vacate an alley between Elizabeth and Court Street and running from Capitol to Third Street in support of the Justice Center annex project. Additionally, the city will sell property in the 300 block of Court Street to the County for $1.
'The township assessor had (placed) the collective value of those parcels at around $31,000,' said City of Pekin Director of Economic Development Josh Wray. 'However, there is significant environmental remediation that would have to take place prior to any development that the County would be taking over.'
The actions passed by identical 6-1 votes, with Council member Rick Hilst voting against both measures.
In other business:
A resolution approving an employee leasing agreement with GovTemps for an Interim Finance Director passed 7-0. The term of the agreement is from April 1 to June 28. It will automatically extend on a bi-weekly basis, but can be terminated at any time with up to a 14-day advanced written notice.
The Council passed a resolution approving an agreement with Tazewell County for a $74,000 recycling grant. Funds will be used primarily to support the city's recycling efforts, help with equipment repairs, disposal fees, and educational materials. The action passed 6-1, with Hilst casting the contrary vote.
A resolution approving an amendment to the lease existing agreement with Cruce Aviation LLC passed unanimously. The updated agreement grants Cruce two hangar additions at Pekin Municipal Airport and a lease extension to October 2043.
The Council unanimously approved an amendment to the city's Fiscal Year 2024 Operating and Capital Budget.

title: O.J. Simpson dies of cancer at 76, his family announces
author: Josh Peter
description: O.J. Simpson, the football star and actor whose life took a shocking turn when he was accused of stabbing to death his ex-wife and a man who was with her the night of the killings, died Wednesday.
content:
O.J. Simpson, the football star and actor whose life took a shocking turn when he was accused of stabbing to death his ex-wife and a man who was with her the night of the killings, died Wednesday of prostate cancer at the age of 76, according to a post on social media attributed to the Simpson family.
"Our father, Orenthal James Simpson, succumbed to his battle with cancer,'' the post said. "He was surrounded by his children and grandchildren. During this time of transition, his family asks that you please respect their wishes for privacy and grace."
Simpson was acquitted of two counts of murder during a televised trial that gripped America and divided the country largely among racial lines. But the jury in a civil trial found Simpson liable for the double murder, and he later served nine years in prison for his role in a botched armed robbery. He was granted parole in 2017.
It completed a stunning fall from grace for the once-celebrated running back who won the Heisman Trophy in 1968 while starring at the University of Southern California. At times he looked unstoppable in the NFL, too, as a member of the Buffalo Bills who was inducted into both the College Football Hall of Fame and the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
He capitalized on his athletic success in Hollywood, developing a career as a successful actor and TV pitchman. But it all came crashing down after the murder charges that riveted America.
There was the televised low-speed car chase in 1994, with Simpson in his white Ford Bronco and police in pursuit as Los Angeles residents cheered from freeway overpasses.
There was the so-called "Trial of the Century" in 1995, when a host of high-powered figures emerged, including Johnnie Cochran, one of Simpson's defense attorneys. He turned a bloody glove found at the scene of the crime into one of the most memorable moments of the trial. In the courtroom, when Simpson struggled to put his hand inside of the glove, Cochran told the jury, 'If it doesn't fit, you must acquit."
Simpson's acquittal set off celebrations from those who pointed to historically unjust treatment of Black people by the U.S. justice system but dismay from those who argued that, regardless of race, the system favored those who could afford high-priced lawyers.
Orenthal James Simpson was born July 9, 1947, in San Francisco and was known as 'O.J.' from birth, the son of Eunice Simpson and Jimmy Lee Simpson.
At San Francisco's Galileo High School, Simpson emerged as a football star.
Saddled with poor grades, he enrolled at City College of San Francisco in 1965, where his exploits on the football field continued. He was named to the Junior College All-America team and was a coveted prospect by Division I colleges.
Simpson elected to transfer to the University of Southern California, where he led the nation in rushing during the 1967 and 1968 seasons while playing under coach John McKay. He was runner-up for the Heisman Trophy as a junior before winning the award as a senior.
'O.J. Simpson was the first player to reach a rushing mark many thought could not be attained in a 14-game season when he topped 2,000 yards,' said Pro Football Hall of Fame president Jim Porter in a statement Thursday. 'His on-field contributions will be preserved in the Hall's archives in Canton, Ohio.'
Simpson married his first wife, Marguerite, in 1967 and they had three children, including one who drowned in the family's swimming pool at age 2 in 1979, the year the couple divorced.
Simpson met future wife Nicole Brown when she was a 17-year-old waitress and he was still married to Marguerite. Simpson and Brown married in 1985 and had two children. She later called police after incidents in which he struck her. Simpson pleaded no contest to spousal abuse charges in 1989.

title: Antisemitic incidents in Illinois, US saw sharp increases in 2023, report says
author: Zach Roth
description: The 143 total incidents in Illinois since Oct. 7 was 20% more than all of the incidents reported statewide in 2022 combined.
content:
A report from the Anti-Defamation League released Tuesday said that incidents of antisemitism skyrocketed in the United States and Illinois in 2023, particularly following the Oct. 7 terrorist attack by Hamas militants that kick-started its current conflict with Israel.
The ADL's Audit of Antisemitic Incidents reported that Illinois saw 211 separate antisemitic incidents of assault, harassment or vandalism last year, up 74% from 2022. Out of that total, 68% took place following the Hamas attack, which killed over 1,100 people in the deadliest attack against Jews since the end of the Holocaust and began an ongoing war in the Gaza Strip.
The 143 total incidents in Illinois since Oct. 7 was 20% more than all of the incidents reported statewide in 2022 combined.
Peoria saw no reports of antisemitism in 2023, but Brimfield — 18 miles northwest of Peoria — reported an incident in March in which students at the local high school made antisemitic comments to a Jewish classmate.
Since the report was limited to events that in 2023, it did not include the March 15 incident at Bradley University in which antisemitic graffiti was found at several buildings on campus, including the Alpha Epsilon Pi fraternity house.
Bloomington reported one incident of antisemitic in 2023, a December incident in which a local synagogue was targeted. Springfield reported one incident during an October protest organized by a local Muslim group in which those in attendance chanted, "From the river, to the sea", considered by the ADL to be a call to genocide of Jews in their homeland.
Antisemitic incidents were also reported in places such as Belvidere, Geneseo, Orion, New Baden and Steelville, among others.
The 200-plus incidents of antisemitism in Illinois were among over 8,000 reported to the ADL last year, up 140% from 2022, with 5,204 incidents nationwide being reported since the Hamas attack.
ADL's Midwest chapter held a news conference in Springfield on Tuesday alongside members of the Illinois General Assembly's Legislative Jewish Caucus in hopes of pushing politicians to support efforts to combat antisemitism. David Goldenberg, the regional director for ADL Midwest, said that he was "alarmed" and "terrified" over the jump in antisemitic incidents since that attack on Israel by Hamas.
"These incidents were fueled in large part by anti-Zionist and anti-Israel groups whose activities have fanned the flames of antisemitism in Chicago, the suburbs and on college campuses throughout Illinois," Goldenberg said. "It is going to take a whole of society approach to reverse this dangerous trend."
