title: Illinois vs Nebraska score today: Live updates, highlights from Week 4 game
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: It's Illinois vs Nebraska in Week 4 of the 2024 college football season. Follow our live game and score updates as the Fighting Illini and Cornhuskers open Big Ten play.
content:
(This story was updated to add new information.)
Illinois football is off to its best start in 13 seasons, but the Fighting Illini trail 17-10 at halftime of their Big Ten Conference opener tonight against No. 22 Nebraska at Memorial Stadium in Lincoln, Nebraska.
The Fighting Illini are 3-0 to start a season for the first time since 2011 when they started 6-0 to start the regular season under Ron Zook. Illinois has wins over Eastern Illinois, No. 19 Kansas and Central Michigan at home.
Behind freshman sensation Dylan Raiola, Nebraska is off to a 3-0 start to the season. The first-year signal-caller is 59-of-80 passing (73.8%) for 670 yards, five touchdowns and one interception to begin his collegiate career.
Illinois-Nebraska halftime score: Huskers 17, Illini 10
The defenses ruled the day in the late part of the second quarter in this Big Ten opener — but Nebraska was able to make one late push. Isaiah Neyor secured his second TD of the game with 16 seconds left in the second, making a great grab while dragging his feet to complete the catch.
Illinois defense: Interception total equals 2023
The interception for Illinois defensive back Torrie Cox was the seventh of the season for the Illini — equalling the team's total from the entire 2023 season, according to Illini Inquirer's Joey Wagner.
Torrie Cox interception for Illinois
Cornerback Torrie Cox came away with an incredible interception in the Nebraska endzone, pulling away a near catch from Huskers receiver Isaiah Neyor. Officials initially ruled the catch an touchdown, but further review gave the Illini the ball and a touchback.
Take a look at the play below:
Illinois-Nebraska score: Illini 10, Huskers 10
Illini kicker David Olano nails a 26-yard field goal to even things up in Lincoln with 11:37 left before halftime.
Nebraska football has 400th sellout
The Illinois vs Nebraska game is the 400th consecutive sellout in Memorial Stadium history in Lincoln. The attendance for the milestone game is 86,936.
Illinois-Nebraska score: Huskers 10, Illini 7
Four plays after the turnover, QB Dylan Raiola finds Isaiah Neyor for a 6-yard touchdown with 32 seconds to play in the first quarter. Turnovers, as always in football, are devastating.
Nebraska forces a turnover
Illinois receiver Hank Beatty has the ball stripped after grabbing a pass, and Nebraska takes gets the ball back in Illinois territory.
Illinois-Nebraska score: Illini 7, Huskers 3
Illinois should feel fortunate to get limit Nebraska to a field goal after quarterback Dylan Raiola had the Huskers with first-and-goal from the 5 after an 18-play drive. Nebraska kicker John Hohl capped the drive with a 21-yard field goal. Usual Huskers placekicker Tristan Alvano is unavailable.
Kaleb Patterson of Illinois with great tackle
Illini cornerback Kaleb Patterson made an incredible tackle to set up a third-and-7, battling a defender — who committed a penalty on the play — to stop the Nebraska player in the backfield.
Illinois-Nebraska score: Illini 7, Huskers 0
Pat Bryant streaks in for a 27-yard touchdown with 11:54 left in the first quarter and the Illini strike first. Bryant, who now has five TDs this season, had a big third-and-1 catch earlier in the drive.

title: Few know the heroic story of Albert Cashier. Looking for Lincoln hopes to change that
author: Erich Murphy
description: Albert Cashier lived in Belvidere before going off to fight in the Civil War in 1862. What no one knew at the time was Cashier was born a woman.
content:
The story of an Illinois soldier in the U.S. Civil War who was born a woman and took on the identity of a man may soon get its own historic marker as part of the state's expansive Looking for Lincoln program.
The Abraham Lincoln National Heritage Area covers 43 counties and 32 communities and allows Lincoln's story — and the stories of others who played significant roles in Illinois history during Lincoln's time — to be easily shared with visitors and the next generation of Illinoisans.
There are 260 such wayside exhibits in the state, and according Liz Vincent, Pontiac's director of community enrichment, there's talk of adding more — more specifically a storyboard for Albert Cashier, who has ties to both Belvidere and Saunemin, Illinois.
Vincent recently updated Pontiac city leaders on the expansion, informing them that while Cashier's home is located in nearby Saunemin, the marker could end up in Pontiac, where Looking for Lincoln already has nine storyboards marking everything from the courthouse where Lincoln won his first lawsuit to the historic Strevell House, the home of a fellow lawyer whom Lincoln visited.
'Recently, the Abraham Lincoln National Heritage Area, which is Looking For Lincoln, (was) granted funding from Union Pacific to create some new wayside exhibits,' Vincent told the council. 'The Albert Cashier story was one of the exhibits.'
Wayside exhibits also are located in Freeport, Galesburg, Macomb, Lincoln and Springfield among dozens of other Illinois communities.
Jennie Hodgers was born on Christmas Day in 1843 in Ireland.
Hodgers adopted a male identity in order to gain employment after moving from Ireland to Belvidere, Illinois.
In 1862, Albert D. J. Cashier enlisted to fight with U.S. Army during the Civil War. Cashier went through training at Rockford's Camp Grant and was assigned to the 95th Illinois Infantry, which eventually became part of the Army of Tennessee under the command of General Ulysses S. Grant.
After the war, Cashier returned to Illinois and continued to live as a man, working and voting in elections as well as receiving a pension as veteran. Cashier worked as a farmhand and a laborer in Belvidere and Saunemin, which is about 12 miles east of Pontiac.
Cashier died at the age of 71 and was buried with full military honors in Saunemin.
Cashier's house in Saunemin house ended up in Pontiac for a short time and was destined for destruction by the Pontiac Fire Department, who planned to use it as during a training exercise. But then the house was saved and moved back to Saunemin, where it remains today.
Although the Cashier house is in Saunemin, Pontiac was chosen as the storyboard site because the local groups involved felt it was better suited for visitors.
'I spoke with the people in Saunemin, and they thought it would be better served to actually be in Pontiac with the rest of our Looking For Lincoln-Livingston County exhibits,' Vincent said. 'So, Dale Maley, representing the Livingston County Historical Society, we worked together and came up with the idea that it would be best suited to be at the Strevell House due to the time period it is discussing.'
The Strevell House, located at 401 W. Livingston St., was owned by local attorney Jason Strevell, who moved to Pontiac in 1855. Strevell and Lincoln were friends.
According to the Visit Pontiac website, after speaking at the Pontiac Young Men's Literary Society, Lincoln spent the night as Strevell's guest at the Strevell home, which is one of the Lincoln exhibits in Pontiac.

title: Earth's new mini moon: Will we be able to see it in Illinois?
author: Mike Kramer
description: Earth's orbit will temporarily capture a mini moon — a tiny asteroid called Asteroid 2024 PT5. Local educators tell us whether we'll be able to see it and if we can watch it.
content:
A second moon orbiting a planet may seem like something out of a science fiction novel. But a second 'moon' entered Earth's orbit Sunday and will loop around the planet until late November.
This so-called 'mini moon' is an asteroid about 10 meters in diameter, according to The Scientific American. Dubbed Asteroid 2024 PT5, it was initially spotted in South Africa in early August by the Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System. It belongs to the Arjuna asteroid belt that follows Earth-like orbits around the sun.
"In its orbit around the sun, it sort of sidled up to the Earth very slowly," said Nick Rae, senior planetarium educator at the Peoria Riverfront Museum. "While it's in Earth's gravity, it will go partly around Earth, but will not make a full orbit."
Will the mini moon be visible in Illinois?
The vast majority of sky-watchers in Illinois and anywhere else in the world will not be able to view 2024 PT5. The asteroid will be too small and too dim to view with the naked eye or with a backyard telescope, according to Space.com.
Dan Son, president of the Peoria Astronomical Society said Peoria's Northmoor Observatory is not equipped to view the asteroid. "It's about the size of a bus flying around the Earth," Son said. "It will be too small to see."
Viewing the mini moon requires a telescope at least 30 inches in diameter, plus a components called a " charged coupled device" or a " complementary metal oxide semiconductor," says Carlos de la Fuente Marcos, a professor at Universidad Complutense de Madrid.
Is the mini moon a rare event?
Not particularly. In a paper announcing 2024 PT5's discovery, Marcos and his brother and co-author Raul de la Fuente Marcos wrote that Earth's gravitational pull can regularly capture asteroids from the Near-Earth population. They noted that four other such events have been confirmed and reported in scientific literature including 2022 FX1, which was pulled into Earth's orbit in 1981 and 2022; 2006 RH, which was captured in 2006; and 2020 CD3, which spent several years in Earth's orbit before escaping in 2020.
When will 2024 PT5 return to Earth's orbit?
The Scientific American projected that Earth will briefly pull the asteroid into its orbit again in 2055.

title: Victim identified after single-vehicle crash in Tazewell County
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: The man's vehicle left the roadway and crashed into a farm field outside Tremont.
content:
A Bloomington man died early Saturday morning after he reportedly crashed his vehicle into a farm field outside Tremont.
Jeffrey Flaugher II, 41, was pronounced dead at 4:35 a.m. after his vehicle left the roadway and crashed into a field in the 21000 block of Townline Road southwest of Tremont.
The Tazewell County Coroner's Office said that at 3:47 a.m., authorities were alerted to a single-vehicle crash in the area. Upon arrival, they found Flaugher's vehicle, with him as the only person inside at the time of the crash.
An autopsy was conducted Monday, with Coroner Charles Hanley saying that Flaugher's death was caused by multiple blunt force injuries sustained in the crash.
The coroner's office and the Tazewell County Sheriff's Office are continuing to investigate the crash. The Tremont Fire Department and Tremont Rescue assisted the sheriff and coroner at the scene.

title: 8 breakout high school girls golfers heading to the 2024 IHSA sectionals
author: Adam Duvall
description: Here are eight girls golfers from around Peoria who shined in the first round of the IHSA playoffs at regionals across Illinois.
content:
Illinois High School Association girls golf regionals took place across the Peoria area on Tuesday.
Peoria Notre Dame (Class 1A) and Dunlap (Class 2A) each hoisted plaques as regional champions with sectional action taking place next Monday. The IHSA state finals will be Oct. 18-19 at two different Decatur courses.
Here are eight breakout golfers looking to carry that regional momentum into the sectionals, while advancing to the state finals.
Preseason picks: Here are 12 of the Peoria area's high school golfers to know ahead of the 2024 season
Kelis Morris, Dunlap
The senior has been the perfect complement to super sophomore Sydney Hunt, who took medalist honors at the Class 2A Galesburg Regional. Morris was the individual runner-up with a 13-over 84 at Lake Bracken Country Club. The Eagles, who now head to the Normal U-High Sectional, have been a roll over the last few weeks, winning the Mid-Illini Conference crown and now their fourth regional in program history.
Kami Jarvill, Pekin
The senior remains consistent and it showed with her fifth-place individual finish at the Class 2A Galesburg Regional. Her 16-over 87 at Lake Bracken Country Club helped the Dragons take third, advancing to the Normal U-High Sectional as a team. Jarvill was one shot better than sophomore teammate Leah Brown (88) and nine shots ahead of classmate Molly Cottrell (96).
Payton Hays, Morton
As a sophomore, Hays kept the Potters in contention for the Class 2A Galesburg Regional crown. She was Morton's top-finisher, carding a 17-over 88 at Lake Bracken Country Club. Her score mixed with junior Morgan Robinson's 91 gave Morton a runner-up team finish and send them off to the Normal U-High Sectional. The Potters were last a state qualifier in 2022.
Clara Gregg, Richwoods
Gregg was the lone freshman individual to advance out of the Class 2A Galesburg Regional. She carded an 27-over 98 at Lake Bracken Country Club, finishing one stroke inside of the top-10 cutoff. This isn't the first time Gregg has been in the mix. She just took a tied-for-third-place finish last week at the Big 12 Conference Tournament, making her the top finisher among all Peoria-area golfers.
Avery Taylor, Metamora
Taylor advanced herself to the Class 2A Normal U-High Sectional by being one of the top-10 individuals not on a qualifying team. The senior shot a 14-over 86 at the Senica's Oak Ridge Golf Club in LaSalle. Her finish at the Class 2A LaSalle-Peru Regional along with sophomore teammate Gillian Tyra, who carded a 91, earn them an opportunity to potentially make the state finals.
Mackenzie Howard, Peoria Notre Dame
Howard showed that PND could be on its way to repeat as a top-3 finisher. The senior shot a 9-over 81 at Wee-Ma-Tuk Country Club in Cuba, capturing the Class 1A Canton Regional individual medalist honors. She shot a 4-over 39 on the front 9, then followed that up with a 5-over 42 on the back 9. PND has a great shot at repeating as sectional champions for the first time in program history next week at the El Paso-Gridley Sectional.
Sara Finn, Illini Bluffs
Finn isn't just an all-state softball player. The junior is also a pretty good golfer, finishing as the fourth-place individual at the Class 1A Canton Regional. She mixed in a pair of birdies on the seventh and 12th holes to shoot a 17-over 82 at Wee-Ma-Tuk Country Club in Cuba. Her finished mixed with a 92 from senior Kennedy Kawolsky helps advance the Tigers to the El Paso-Gridley Sectional and a potential berth at the state finals.
Natalie Downing, Canton
The senior made the most of her final appearance on her home course — Wee-Ma-Tuk Country Club in Cuba. She took fifth place as an individual at the Class 1A Canton Regional, turning in a scorecard that was for a 19-over 91. Her finish along with classmates Allison Wheeler (20-over 92) and Ella Demler (20-over 92) gave the Little Giants a second-place finish to PND, 361-369. Canton has never won a sectional title, but could next week at the El Paso-Gridley Sectional.

title: Coming soon: Restaurant on Washington Square opening 'in the near future'
author: Mike Kramer
description: The date has not been set, but the Tangled Roots Brewing Company is nearly ready to launch its new location on Washington Square.
content:
While they have not yet set a specific opening date, the management of Tangled Roots Brewing Company is looking forward to opening its new location on Washington Square ' in the near future.'
' Tangled Roots is very grateful for the warm welcome from both the City of Washington and the Washington Chamber of Commerce, and residents,' Tangled Roots director of marketing Anna Wright said. 'We are thrilled to be a part of such a vibrant and supportive community and truly appreciate the kindness and enthusiasm you've shown us. We're excited to build lasting relationships, share our passion for craft beer and food, and contribute to the growth and success of Washington.'
Tangled Roots Craft Beer & Kitchen will be located at 140 Washington Square, Washington. The company will also operate an events center at 120 Walnut Street and a retail facility at 126 Walnut Street.
In a June story by the Journal Star, Nathan Watson, the CEO of CL Real Estate Development said construction would be completed in the fall and the grand opening slated to take place by the end of the year.
The Washington location will be the fifth for the Ottawa-based Tangled Roots franchise. The company also operates locations in Ottawa, Glenview, Lockport, and Vernon Hills.
More information is available at tangledrootsbrewingco.com.
Wright added that Washington is a good fit for the restaurant group because of its "commitment to community engagement aligns with the community's keen sense of local pride," Wright said. Tangled Roots will provide a unique dining option while creating jobs and supporting local suppliers, Wright said.
'This economic boost can have a positive ripple effect on the community,' Wright said.
Known for a wide range of 'farm to foam' beers brewed from locally grown barley, other Tangled Roots Craft Beer and Kitchens offer lunch and dinner menu with a selection of starters, soups, salads, flatbread, sandwiches, and entrees. The Tangled Roots brunch menu features Korean BBQ Chicken and Waffles, brunch burgers, and pancake tacos.

title: Sen. Bernie Sanders to Belvidere UAW, 'Outrageous level of corporate greed' must stop
author: Jeff Kolkey
description: U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vermont, delivered a blistering speech Friday demanding Stellantis keep its promised investments in Belvidere.
content:
(This story was updated to add new information.)
U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders told people at a rally Friday in Belvidere that Stellantis should keep its promise to reopen the Illinois city's assembly plant and encouraged attendees to vote for Vice President Kamala Harris for president.
Sanders, I-Vermont, was a speaker at the "Rally with the Working Class to End Trump's NAFTA 2.0" along with UAW President Shawn Fain and UAW Local 1268 President Matt Frantzen.
Sanders said car manufacturer Stellantis is spending billions of dollars on stock buybacks for shareholders and millions on raises for its CEO Carlos Tavares while stiffing Belvidere on its promised investments to revive the idled Belvidere Assembly Plant.
"All that we are saying here in Belvidere is not complicated, and it is supported by the overwhelming majority of the American people," Sanders said. "We have got to stop this outrageous level of corporate greed. Nobody objects to a CEO making a decent compensation package. Nobody objects to corporations making profits, but enough is enough. This country belongs to all of us — not just a handful of billionaires."
Sanders said the richest 1% of Americans have grown far richer over the last 50 years as he argues trillions of dollars in wealth have been transferred to them from the bottom 99% of earners.
An estimated 275 people filled the union hall in Belvidere to hear fiery speeches from Sanders, Fain and Frantzen.
Sanders, who was heading to a town hall in Dubuque, Iowa, after his stop in Belvidere, has long opposed free trade agreements he argues do not protect American jobs, harm the environment and speed climate change. He supported the UAW during its 2023 Stand Up Strike in which it won wage increases and a promise to invest nearly $5 billion to re-open the Belvidere Assembly Plant and build a joint-venture battery production facility in Belvidere.
Citing market conditions, Stellantis recently told UAW officials that it is delaying the promised investments in Belvidere. The company said it will not launch a Belvidere consolidated Mopar hub as planned in 2024, will not begin stamping operations in 2025 and will not begin production of a midsize truck in 2027.
In response, the UAW has held several "Keep the Promise" rallies and filed grievances in preparation for a strike.
Meanwhile, Stellantis has claimed that language in its labor agreement with the UAW would make a strike illegal and it has filed lawsuits against the union, the Detroit Free Press reports.
UAW President Shawn Fain told the crowd Friday that Stellantis is "crying poverty" while taking advantage of free trade deals like Donald Trump's U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, which replaced NAFTA, to shift production to low-wage countries.
'The reason Stellantis is refusing to keep its promise to the working class, the reason Belvidere has fallen behind when this should be the home of thousands of the best blue-collar jobs in the country is because our political and economic system is broken,' Fain said. 'Stellantis is making record profits, handing out billions of stock buybacks to juice up their stocks and help their Wall Street buddies instead of reopening and expanding a plant right here in Belvidere like they promised.'
Frantzen said he is encouraging workers to support Harris in part because the free trade agreement had no protections built in for American manufacturing workers.
"When things went down here, I didn't have one Republican step up and say, 'Hey what can I do for your local?'" Frantzen said. "Every damn Democrat we got around here was calling us, asking 'What can we do?' What we have done is taken Belvidere and made it a national scene. People have heard about Belvidere."
In a written statement issued Friday, Illinois Gov. JB Prizker called on Stellantis to live up to its commitments. He said the state had for two years offered its full support to Stellantis including millions in financial incentives to put workers from across the Rockford and Belvidere region back to work.
"Working families' lives have been turned upside down and they deserve peace of mind," Pritzker said. "Our Illinois workforce is second to none, and Stellantis knows it. With significant work and support from the state of Illinois, a historic national contract was signed that will restart the Belvidere plant. It is good for workers, good for the company and good for Illinois."

title: Illinois vs Purdue score today: Recap, highlights from wild Week 7 game
author: Dave Eminian
description: It's Illinois vs Purdue in Week 7 of the 2024 college football season. The Fighting Illini survive 50-49 in overtime shootout at Memorial Stadium.
content:
The nationally ranked Illinois Fighting Illini survived the Purdue Boilermakers, 50-49, in overtime to win the Week 7 college football game at Memorial Stadium.
Purdue (1-5) gave the Illini everything they could handle, rallying from a 27-3 third-quarter deficit to force overtime.
No. 23 Illinois (5-1) scored on the first play of OT, with quarterback Luke Altmyer hitting Pat Bryant for a 25-yard scoring strike. David Olano's point after gave Illinois a 50-43 lead.
The Boilermakers answered, scoring two plays into their OT possession. Instead of kicking to tie, Purdue attempted a two-point conversion. Quarterback Ryan Browne dropped back, scrambled and could not escape — as Dylan Rosiek sacked him and the Illini celebrated the rivalry win.
Altmyer led the Illini, going 20-for-34 with 379 yards and three touchdowns. He added 60 rushing yards and a score for Illinois, which played without leading rusher Kaden Feagin, listed as "out" on the pregame availability report.
Josh McCray filled in as the top rushing option, finishing with 78 yards and two touchdowns on 16 carries.
Illinois spread the ball around, with eight receivers catching passes. Bryant led the way with four catches for 104 yards and a TD. Zakhari Franklin added 60 yards and a TD on four catches, while McCray, Hank Beatty, Collin Dixon and Tanner Arkin all had multiple catches.
Browne finished 18-for-26 with 297 yards and three touchdowns — 288 of those yards after halftime, during which he pulled Purdue from a 24-point deficit to force overtime. He also ran for 118 yards on 17 carries.
Purdue's two big playmakers were running back Devin Mockobee (133 total yards, 2 TDs) and tight end Max Klare (six catches, 133 yards).

What Illinois coach Bret Bielema said after win over Purdue
• Illini coach Bret Bielema, on his team building a big lead, falling to a Purdue comeback, then coming back to win in OT: 'It sounds incredible to say, but I think that was the best thing that could have ever happened to us. To be up like that and have it start to go the other way, then show the resiliency to make plays at the end."
• Purdue coach Ryan Walters, on his decision to attempt a 2-point conversion in OT in a bid to win the game: "(We) made a decision to go for it, and I wouldn't change that decision."
• Bielema, on Purdue's 2-point conversion attempt in OT: "I called it when they won the coin toss. I toldTanner ArkinI wanted to keep our defense on the sideline and go through some calls. I told the defense 'our offense is going to score and go for one, but when Purdue gets it if they score they're going to go for two.' We called their two-point play before our offense even stepped on the field. There was a calmness in our defensive staff with shooting Rosiek up the middle and if there's one guy who I know who's going to make that tackle it's him and he has plenty of them."
• Bielema, on Josh McCray: "He sees all these other running backs come in Kaden Feagin, Aidan Laughrey, and Ca'Lil Velentine; everyone's writing about all those other guys and not him and he continues to persevere. It's a one-handed catch against Nebraska, a flat route today in the first half, a tough 1-yard run near the end zone to score. He continues to battle through as a young man who lost his mom early in life and was raised by his grandma. Unfortunately, he lost her before I ever met him. He gets beat down but keeps getting back up so I couldn't be prouder of him today."
• Illini QB Luke Altmyer, on watching Purdue go for 2 points in an attempt to win it in OT: "I have trust in my defense and we constantly practice these situations. It was so cool to see them do it in that fashion. I knew we had to create pressure and Dylan made an incredible sack."
• Illini defender Dylan Rosiek, whose sack on Purdue's 2-point attempt in OT sealed a victory for Illinois: "The first half they ran a lot of what we expected. In the second half they went into plays that challenged our eyes. They're good scheme plays. We have to have our eyes in better places, we have to be able to adjust and be ready."

The Boilermakers need just two plays to score and pull within 50-49. Purdue tried to win the game, but its two-point conversion failed. Ryan Browne dropped back, scrambled and was sacked to end the threat.
Illini strike fast in overtime
Luke Altmyer hits Pat Bryant for a 25-yard touchdown pass on the first play in overtime. What a throw. David Olano puts the Fighting Illini ahead 50-43.
Illinois-Purdue headed into overtime
Fighting Illini kicker David Olano hits a 38-yard field goal to tie the game at 43-43 and send the game into overtime. The kick was set up by a big catch from Hank Beatty.

After recovering the onside kick, Purdue drives down and Devin Mockobee catches the go-ahead touchdown on a throw from Ryan Browne.
Purdue recovers onside kick

Devin Mockobee dives in from 2 yards out to pull the Boilermakers within five points with 95 seconds remaining. Purdue has all three timeouts remaining.
Illinois holding on to lead late vs Purdue
Purdue has the ball with two minutes remaining, threatening to pull within a score. Boilermakers QB Ryan Browne has engineered a solid drive and has Purdue threatening. Brown has thrown for 238 of his 247 yards in the second half.
Score update: Illinois 40, Purdue 28
The Fighting Illini answer back as Josh McCray scores his third touchdown of the day with 5:05 remaining. The TD was set up by another key run from Luke Altmyer and a big third-down catch from McCray earlier in the drive.
After a penalty, the Illini tried an 18-yard two-point conversion try — but the pass fell short.

Ryan Browne finds Jaron Tibbs for an 8-yard touchdown to pull the Boilermakers within 34-26 — and then adds the two-point conversion to pull within 34-28 at the 10:35 mark of the fourth quarter.
Score update: Illinois 34, Purdue 20
Quarterback Luke Altmyer took it into his own hands this drive, rushing for a 13-yard touchdown to put the Fighting Illini back ahead by two touchdowns early in the fourth quarter. Altmyer also had runs of 22 and 37 yards on the drive to set up the TD.
Purdue trick play sets up field goal
The Boilermakers used a flea flicker to set up a 62-yard passing connection from Ryan Browne to tight end Max Klare, who was wide open after the double handoff flea flicker.
Purdue is shut down inside the 10, but pulls within 27-20 after the 24-yard field goal from Spencer Porath.
Purdue returns fumble for touchdown
The Boilermakers are back in this game. Nyland Green sacked Illinois QB Luke Altmyer, forcing a fumble picked up by Will Heldt and returned 16 yards for a score. Illinois still leads 27-17, but is on the ropes for the first time today.

Purdue scores its first touchdown in two weeks, getting a 53-yard reception by Jahmal Edrine, who dove to stretch for the TD in the final yards. The call was upheld after an officials' review. This is the Boilermakers' first TD since Sept. 28 vs. Nebraska.
David Olano extends the Fighting Illini lead to 27-3 with a 49-yard field goal into the wind, clearing the uprights easily. Olano pumped his fist after the make.

Illinois has scored twice in the last 90 seconds of game time, this one a short pass from Luke Altmyer to Josh McCray with 19 seconds left in the second quarter. The five-play, 25-yard drive puts the Illini in control.

Luke Altmyer finds Zakhari Franklin for a 27-yard pass on third-and-20 — and incredible conversion — to get inside the Purdue 10 in the final minute of the first half.

Illinois gets the ball back when the kickoff gets caught in the wind and is recovered by Luke Zardzin in an unexpected onside kick of sorts.

Dylan Rosiek makes an open-field tackle to halt Purdue, which settled for a 22-yard field goal after having first-and-goal from the 4. The score was set up by a 34-run from Devin Mockobee, which took the Boilers down inside the 5.
Illinois QB Luke Altmyer career-best quarter
Illini QB Luke Altmyer threw for 111 yards in the first quarter, staking Illinois to a 10-0 lead over Purdue. That is a career high for Altmyer.

Purdue is now 1-for-4 on third-down conversions, and Illinois forces another punt — this one returned 24 yards by former Rochester High star Hank Beatty. If Illinois can score on this possession, it will seize control of this game.

Purdue turned the ball over on downs after eating nearly 3 minutes off the clock. Illinois takes over for the first time, and we get a look at the Illini without starting running back Kaden Feagin.

title: Illinois prison employees to picket for safer working conditions
author: Erich Murphy
description: Drug smuggling and assaults on staff are just two of the reasons why Illinois correctional center officers will be picketing Thursday.
content:
Government workers will be picketing outside Illinois prisons Thursday afternoon to demand safer working conditions.
Members of the AFSCME Could 31 union will hold an informational picket from 2 to 4:30 p.m. Thursday.
Members will be outside the Pontiac Correctional Center and other prisons throughout the state, according to local AFSCME President William Lee.
A flyer advertising the event states "Safety Matters" followed by the words 'Say no to drug smuggling,' 'Say no to assaults on staff' and 'Join the picket line.'
The picket in Pontiac will be at the intersection of West Reynolds and South Vermillion streets, just two blocks north of the main gate of the prison. There will also be a banner on West Lincoln Street across from the main gate.
According to Lee, drugs have been making their way into correctional facilities all over Illinois through various means, including mail delivery.
In 2022, an inmate in the Pontiac prison attacked two correctional officers, stabbing one of the guards in the neck with a piece of metal that he had sharpened. Both officers sustained serious injuries.
Illinois has five maximum security prisons, one of which is in Pontiac. The other four are in Canton, Sumner, Menard and Joliet.
The state's prison system operates 46 facilities in total, including prisons in Kewanee, Lincoln and Galesburg and an adult transition center in Peoria.

title: Illinois high school football scores: Peoria-area IHSA highlights from Week 8
author: Adam Duvall
description: It's Week 8 of Illinois high school football in the Peoria-area. Here is a recap, highlights and IHSA scores from Friday night.
content:
Something about a must-win game that brings out the best in high school football teams.
Morton and Deer Creek-Mackinaw were among the myriad schools across the state that kept their playoff hopes alive with their fourth victories on Friday night; those four-win teams can become playoff eligible with wins next week. Meanwhile, Washington won to clinch a share of the Mid-Illini Conference, and Peoria High dropped Bloomington to keep alive its hopes of a Big 12 Conference title.
We're wrapping up Week 8 of the Illinois high school football season — with the IHSA postseason fields starting to take shape and conference championship races coming down to the wire.
Here is your Journal Star preps experience for Week 8 — your one-stop shop as we look around the Peoria-area football landscape each week during the 2024 high school season.
Peoria High wins state-ranked matchup
Peoria High defeated Class 6A No. 10 Bloomington 44-28 in a battle of state-ranked teams to move to 7-1 overall and 6-1 in the Big 12 Conference.
The win sets up a huge showdown next week: Class 5A No. 4 Peoria High at Normal Community (7-1, 7-0), ranked No. 6 statewide in Class 7A.
Washington clinches share of Mid-Illini title
After starting the season 0-2, the Washington Panthers have won six in a row to clinch a share of the Mid-Illini Conference title after a 42-6 victory in Canton.
The Panthers (6-2, 6-0) have a one-game lead over Pekin (6-2, 5-1) with one game remaining. Washington hosts Morton next week, and the Dragons are at East Peoria.
Morton gets big win over Dunlap
Morton has kept its playoff hopes alive with a 39-14 upset of Dunlap in a Mid-Illini Conference game Friday night. The Eagles played without quarterback John Bargen, who did not play after injuring his knee in last week's loss to Washington. Bargen told John Komosa of Clutch Sports Media he is not sure when he will return.
Morton (4-4, 4-2) likely needs to win next week at Washington to secure a bid. Dunlap (5-3, 3-3) won its fifth game last week.
Princeton coach gets milestone win
Princeton football coach Ryan Pearson won his 100th career game on Friday with a 57-20 victory against Aledo Mercer County, according to Bureau County Republican sports editor Kevin Hieronymous.
Pearson had previous stops at Iroquois West, Flanagan-Cornell/Woodland and Canton. This is his 65th victory in eight seasons at Princeton.
Dee-Mack keeps playoff hopes alive
Deer Creek-Mackinaw defeated Clinton 38-20 on Friday night to move to 4-4 headed into Week 9.
The Chiefs host Colfax Ridgeview/Lexington next week needing a win to become playoff eligible.
Morton extends lead vs Dunlap
Morton is fighting to keep its playoff hopes alive, leading Dunlap 32-14 in the fourth quarter of their Mid-Illini Conference game.
Morton (3-4, 3-2) needs to win out to secure a playoff bid, while Dunlap (5-2, 3-2) has already likely secured its bid.
Princeville loses first game of the season
Princeville lost its first game of the season, 34-21, to Rushville-Industry. The Princes had joined the state ranked this week, coming in at No. 8 in Class 1A.
The Princes (8-1) will close out the regular season with a game vs. Annawan/Wethersfield.
Peoria High extends lead in huge Big 12 game
Peoria High has scored 20 unanswered points and leads Bloomington 44-20 with 4:56 remaining in their key Big 12 Conference game. Both came into the game with 6-1, 5-1 records and both state ranked.
TQ Webb grabbed a 6-yard TD catch to cap a nearly 10-minute drive.
Peoria High grabs lead early after halftime
Peoria High grabs a 22-20 lead just after halftime, getting a 4-yard run from QB Breon Green. The Lions are wearing special Peoria police jerseys; get a look at them below on this fourth-down conversion catch by TQ Webb.
Morton-Dunlap in a tight game
Morton leads Dunlap, 20-14 late in the second quarter, getting a 49-yard TD run from Cole Rinkenberger to take a lead.
Rinkenberger also had Morton's first TD, and Julian Alexander added another. Dunlap has scores from Jackson Oldham (rushing TD) and Dawson Marmion (interception return).
Dunlap is playing without starting quarterback John Bargen, who is on the sideline in street clothes, according to Clutch Sports Media reporter John Komosa.
Washington on way to share of conference title
Washington leads 21-0 about half way through the first quarter of their game at Canton. The Panthers (5-2, 4-0) will clinch a share of the Mid-Illini Conference title with a victory.
The latest TD for Washington was a fumble return by defensive back Andre Lewis.
Pekin sophomore keeps TD streak alive
Pekin sophomore Dylan Anderson opened the scoring on Friday, corralling a TD pass from Brogan Benassi in the Dragons' game against Limestone.
Anderson has scored at least one TD in every game this season for Pekin (5-2, 4-1). Read all about Anderson's exploits here.
Peoria High honoring Peoria Police Department with uniforms
The Peoria High football team will honor the city's police department with specialty jerseys for its 7 p.m. game Friday against Bloomington.
The uniforms are black with neon numbering. The Peoria skyline is across the top of the front and back, with the word "PEORIA" on the back. What's more, the same logo will be on a CityLink bus that transports the team from the school to Peoria Stadium along with a police escort.

Nine teams from the Journal Star area have six or more wins and have secured automatic playoff bids: Peoria High, Eureka, Farmington, Princeville, Elmwood/Brimfield, Stark County, Princeton, Rushville-Industry and Monmouth-Roseville. Another five teams come into this week with five wins and can clinch with victories tonight: Pekin, Washington, Dunlap, Metamora and Macomb.

title: Prison employees picket over drug safety concerns across Illinois
author: Erich Murphy
description: Union members at 23 Illinois Department of Corrections facilities walked out on Thursday over safety concerns.
content:
An explosion of drug use in Illinois prisons has drawn the attention of corrections officers and others working inside the walls of the state's correction facilities.
Members of AFSCME Council 31 walked an informational picket line at 23 Illinois Department of Corrections facilities from Vienna in southern Illinois to Dixon in the northern part of the state on Oct. 17.
In a statement from Anders Lindell of AFSCME Council 31, the prison employee union members demonstrated in a call for safer working conditions. A major problem as of late, Lindell said, is the drug issue overtaking virtually all of the prisons in the state. Not only is it affecting inmates, but employees have been exposed as well.
In a written statement, Lindell noted that 'Safety Matters,' adding that 'AFSCME members are calling on the Department of Corrections to prevent illegal substances, enforce policies requiring clear consequences for offenders abusing substances or assaulting staff, and expedite hiring for safe staffing levels."
'AFSCME members should not have to face violent assaults, illegal drugs and chronic staff shortages as common occurrences when just doing their jobs,' Council 31 Executive Director Roberta Lynch said. 'We demand that leadership of the Department of Corrections step up and do more to make this essential work safer.'
William Lee, president of AFSCME Local 494, said that the drug issue has become a bigger problem in recent years. The main issue is inmates getting drugs through the mail, particularly legal mail, which is mail coming to inmates from their attorneys.
An AFSCME Council 31 report notes the growing problem of drugs in IDOC. The report notes incidents from employees at various correctional centers. One incident took place at Menard, a maximum security facility near Chester along the Mississippi River in southern Illinois.
The report cites an August incident at the Menard Correctional Center where 12 staff members were taken to the hospital after a mass exposure event.
The report also cites an April incident at the Henry Hill Correctional Center in Galesburg where a correctional lieutenant was attacked by an inmate over two pieces of paper which tested positive for fentanyl.
A quote in the report from an unidentified Sheridan Correctional Center employee stated, 'It's been getting worse over the past couple years, so much of it, it's overwhelming.'
Lee said he met with leaders discussing the Pontiac Correctional Center and possible solutions.
'Everything was talked about at the table,' Lee said. He pointed out what he called 'a very simple solution,' which would be to scan the inmate mail.
'It's an easy solution but who's going to push the button to make it happen?' Lee said. 'At some point, DOC and the governor and everybody who has the power to change everything needs to use their power and ability put it to something useful, like staff and help the safety of everybody who works in their facilities.'

title: Exclusive look at the Peoria Rivermen championship rings for 2023-24 SPHL title
author: Dave Eminian
description: A detailed look and description of the SPHL championship rings awarded to the Peoria Rivermen in an opening night ceremony on Friday.
content:
PEORIA — The wait is over.
The Peoria Rivermen received their SPHL championship rings Friday in a pre-game ceremony at their 2024-25 home opener in Carver Arena.
The rings are bigger and heavier than the title rings the Rivermen earned in 2021-22. And the bling is loaded with messages and meanings from a team that hoisted the President's Cup on home ice last spring.
The ring was made by Canadian company Baron in collaboration with design concepts from Rivermen co-owner Bart Rogers.
"I come from merchandise beginnings with this team, and I love creating things like this," Rogers said. "It's in my blood. This was so much fun to put together, Baron did a great job bringing our concepts to life. The ring is big and bold, and it's the honor we wanted to give our players and coaches and staff, something they will keep and celebrate forever."
What's on the Peoria Rivermen championship ring?
Here's an exclusive first look at the 2024 Peoria Rivermen SPHL championship rings:
The encrusted ring top features the President's Cup, above the Rivermen logo in gold.
Inside the Cup, at the bottom, are six shimmering stones that represent the six playoff victories that led to Peoria's championship.
On one side of the ring are three words, chosen by head coach and general manager Jean-Guy Trudel to represent the franchise during its championship season: Leadership, Humility, Dynasty.
The word dynasty is offset in gold and according to Rogers represents "the unity and strength of our dedicated coaches, players and staff who rose to greatness together."
Below those words is a sculpture, taken from a championship celebration photo, with players in silver in the background and captain Alec Hagaman, wearing his No. 17, in gold capturing the moment he raised the President's Cup at Carver Arena. It was Hagaman's final career moment, as he led the team to a title, earned SPHL Playoff MVP honors and then retired.
Encircling the top of the ring is a band which reads "2024 SPHL CHAMPIONS, with three colored gemstones that represent the teams official colors.
On the inside of the ring is engraved the results of the three playoff series won by the Rivermen, and at the bottom the acronym "LFG" which we'll leave fans to interpret.
The ring's shank carries the name Peoria, and the right shoulder displays the player's name, uniform number, and the team's 43-15-5 record.

title: Former deputy in Sonya Massey shooting moved to Macon County Jail
author: Tom Ackerman
description: The former Sangamon County Sheriff's deputy charged in the fatal of Sonya Massey has been transferred to a different jail.
content:
The former Sangamon County Sheriff's deputy charged in the fatal of Sonya Massey has been transferred to the Macon County Jail in Decatur from the Menard County Jail in Petersburg.
Sean P. Grayson was moved to Decatur because it is a larger facility, Menard County Sheriff Mark Oller said Monday.
The move was decided mostly because Presiding Circuit Judge Ryan Cadagin ruled that Grayson would continue to be detained in accordance with the Pre-Trial Fairness Act, leading sheriffs to decide where best to place Grayson while he awaits trial.
Grayson has a new status hearing for Dec. 2. A Fourth District Appellate Court ruling regarding Grayson's ongoing detention is expected around the time of the hearing.
Oller said he and former Sangamon County Sheriff Jack Campbell had arranged for Grayson to be jailed in Menard County rather than in Sangamon County as a security precaution, but it was their intention to only hold Grayson in Menard County for a short-term stay.
'I think some of (former Sheriff Campbell's) concerns were that he had worked in Sangamon County, so his arrestees could have possibly been in the jail," Oller said. "Some of the staff could have been familiar with him. None of our staff knew him."
Oller said he had some concerns about holding Grayson because of the notoriety in the case, but he wanted to assist neighboring sheriffs. Jails holding inmates for neighboring counties is not an uncommon practice.
Sangamon County Sheriff Paula Crouch and Macon County Sheriff Jim Root were unable to be reached for comment. Grayson's defense attorney Daniel Fultz did not immediately return messages to The State Journal-Register.
During the time that Grayson was held in Menard County, Sangamon County was responsible for any expenses such as medical expenses, Oller said, though Grayson experienced no major medical issues while in the Menard County Jail.
Grayson was dealing with complications from a diagnosis of Stage 3 colon cancer, Fultz said in court in late August.

title: 420 rushing yards and state trophies: Vote for Journal Star athlete of the week for Oct. 21-26
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Nominees from Metamora, Pekin, Dunlap and more. Vote in the Journal Star athlete of the week award. Poll open until Friday.
content:
After plenty of solid fall sports performers over the last week, here are the Journal Star high school athlete of the week nominees for Oct. 21-26.
Head to pjstar.com/sports to vote. The poll closes at noon Friday. Information about the nominees is below.
If you have a nominee for the honor, email us at sports@pjstar.com or tag us on Twitter @pjstarsports. Last week, Chloe Fabry of the Brimfield volleyball team was named JS athlete of the week.
Brogan Benassi, Pekin football
The junior quarterback put together an impressive Week 9. Benassi threw for 208 yards and five touchdowns on 9-for-11 passing in a 62-20 win over East Peoria. Pekin (7-2) heads into the Class 7A playoffs on a five-game win streak and hosts New Lenox Lincoln-Way West (6-3) at 7 p.m. Friday.
Jimmy Lollar, Olympia football
The running back put together a school-record effort in a Week 9 win. Lollar rushed for 420 yards and five touchdowns in beating Auburn, 66-44. His yardage mark sets the all-time single-season program record and is just outside of the top 20 IHSA single-game performances. The Spartans (6-3) head to Nashville (8-1) at 2:30 p.m. Saturday in the first round of the Class 3A playoffs.
Addison Pacha, Metamora volleyball
The senior closed out the regular season in a big way last Thursday. Pacha posted a double-double — 16 kills and 12 digs — as Metamora beat Dunlap, 23-25, 25-20, 25-14 at Bradley University's Renaissance Coliseum. Her week started last Tuesday with a 12-kill effort to beat East Peoria, 25-16, 25-17. The Redbirds (20-13) host a Class 3A regional, playing Washington (21-11) on Tuesday.
Elle Blunier, Eureka volleyball
The senior setter came away with a big week for the Hornets. Blunier ran the offense as Eureka won the Heart of Illinois Conference Tournament championship on Saturday. She helped the Hornets with 11 assists and eight digs to knock off regular-season HOI champion Tremont, 25-23, 25-20. Her 17 assists and seven aces came in last Thursday's 25-14, 25-19 semifinal win over Deer Creek-Mackinaw. Blunier's week began last Tuesday with 19 assists and 10 digs in a beating quarterfinal opponent Lexington, 24-26, 25-20, 17-15.
Coriell Green, Delavan boys cross country
Green was a Class 1A individual regional champio n on Saturday. He won the Olympia Regional by running the Olympia High School 3-mile course in 15:45.7. His was almost six seconds faster than the runner-up finisher. The sophomore will now run this upcoming Saturday in the Elmwood Sectional at Maple Lane Country Club.
Meghan Zopel, Peoria Notre Dame girls cross country
Zopel was a Class 1A regional winner this past Saturday. The senior ran her 5,000-meter home course at Donovan Park in 19:32.12. This time was 14.14 seconds ahead of second-place finisher Meika Bender of Eureka (19:46.26). PND (46 points) took second to regional winner El Paso-Gridley (38 points). The Irish head to Maple Lane Country Club for the Elmwood Sectional on Saturday.
Josh Walton, Peoria Christian boys soccer
The Chargers goalkeeper put together a pair of great postseason matches last week. In Saturday's 4-1 win over Rock Island Alleman, Walton allowed his first goal of the postseason on the Illinois Valley Central High School pitch. His week started with a clean sheet to beat Quincy Notre Dame, 4-0, last Tuesday. PCS (22-2-2) heads into Wednesday's Class 1A sectional title against Mendota (22-2-1), which beat the Chargers, 4-2, on Oct. 15.
Lily Furrow, Galesburg girls swimming and diving
Furrow was named the Western Big Six Conference swimmer of the year following the Silver Streaks league championship on Saturday. The junior won the 100-yard freestyle (53.62 seconds) and 100-yard backstroke (59.84 seconds) along with being a member of the winning 200-yard medley (1:56.95) and 200-yard freestyle (1:44.73) relay teams. Galesburg edged out Moline, 282-275 for the conference title.
Anna Yu, Dunlap girls tennis
Yu capped a memorial freshman season with a fifth-place singles finish at the Class 1A state finals on Saturday. She beat Elmhurst Timothy Christian's Jane Carter, 6-2, 6-2 to capture first-team all-state honors. Yu's finish helped Dunlap repeat as state third-place finishers with 27 points.

It's the first round of the Illinois high school football playoffs, and predictions for the IHSA games around the Peoria area are in. Games are either Friday or Saturday.
Last week, the picks in this space went 11-6 (.647) and are 120-30 (.800) on the season. This year's team records are in parentheses.
Class 7A
20 New Lenox Lincoln-Way West (6-3) at 13 Pekin (7-2), 7 p.m. Friday
Pekin 41, Lincoln-Way West 20: The Dragons ended the regular season on a five-game winning streak including two wins by a combined 10 points over Morton and Metamora. Pekin quarterback Brogan Benassi threw for 208 yards and five touchdowns in putting up 62 points on East Peoria in Week 9. Lincoln-Way West is averaging 37.6 points per game against 17.7 allowed.
Class 6A
15 Dunlap (6-3) at 2 Oak Lawn Richards (8-1), 7 p.m. Friday
Oak Lawn Richards 35, Dunlap 20: The Eagles ended a two-game skid with a dramatic come-from-behind victory over Metamora in Week 9. That was Dunlap's lone win over a team with a winning record this season. However, four-star recruit Mack Sutter, QB John Bargen and RB Jackson Oldham have a chance to play spoiler in the lower bracket. Richards is in the playoffs for a 15th consecutive season, including a 2013 Class 6A state runner-up.
10 Palos Heights Shepard (7-2) at 7 Washington (7-2), 7:30 p.m. Friday
Washington 34, Palos Heights Shepard 8: The Panthers made an unbeaten run through the Mid-Illini Conference, winning their final seven games following a 0-2 start. Washington has been stingy on defense — giving up 13.8 points per game — led by Carter Prina and Noah Bell. Palos Heights Shepard has won just five playoff games in program history, allowing 11.0 points against 34.4 scored.
Class 5A
9 Metamora (6-3) at 8 Centralia (6-3), 3 p.m. Saturday
Metamora 39, Centralia 16: Three times this season the Redbirds won back-to-back games, then lost one. Those trio of defeats all came to playoff-bound teams (Washington, Pekin, Dunlap). Metamora's 66 playoff victories is fourth-most in the Class 5A field. Metamora QB Stephen Petri (165 yards, 2TDs) is coming off a huge game on the ground against Dunlap. This just Centralia's 10th playoff appearance, playing four playoff opponents this season.
15 Country Club Hills Hillcrest (5-4) at 2 Peoria High (7-2), 7 p.m. Friday
Peoria 61, Hillcrest 22: Peoria High enters the postseason averaging 507.7 yards per game and 48.4 points a game. The Lions have scored 37 rushing TDs, while rushing for 3,012 yards. QB Breon Green is partly responsible for 1,587 passing yards and 20 TDs, finding WR TQ Webb for a large portion of those yards and scores. Hillcrest is making its eighth successive playoff appearance, averaging 31.1 points a game.
Class 4A
9 Murphysboro (7-2) at 8 Macomb (7-2), 3 p.m. Saturday
Murphysboro 42, Macomb 23: Both of the Bombers' losses came to teams — Farmington (9-0) and Elmwood/Brimfield (8-1) — that finished ahead of the team in the LincolnLand-Large Division standings. Macomb is averaging 33.3 points a game against 15.4 allowed. The Red Devils are the playoffs for a sixth successive season.
13 Peoria Notre Dame (5-4) at 4 Rochester (7-2), 7 p.m. Friday
Rochester 36, Peoria Notre Dame 35: PND won in Week 9 to get into the playoffs for the 19th time in program history. The Irish averaged 55.8 points in their five wins including 60 points or more three times. The Rockets are the reigning state champions, having won nine state championships since 2010 under coach Derek Leonard, who was suspended in Week 9 after a hazing and bullying investigation with the program. Rochester is averaging 39.6 points a game against 19.1 allowed.
15 Kewanee (5-4) at 2 Olney Richland County (9-0), 3 p.m. Saturday
Richland County 41, Kewanee 26: The Boilermakers are making their 14th playoff appearance in program history. Kewanee won four of its final five games including a 10-point over Orion in Week 9. Richland County, which went 0-9 last season, is ranked No. 5 statewide in Class 4A and averages 45.6 points a game.
Class 3A
13 Oregon (5-4) at 4 Princeton (8-1), 7 p.m. Friday
Princeton 42, Oregon 6: The Tigers are in the playoffs for a sixth time in a row and 15th time in program history. Princeton is averaging 42.0 points a game against 14.0 allowed. Oregon picked up a win in Week 9 to secure its 16th playoff berth program in history.
10 Peotone (6-3) at 7 Eureka (8-1), 7 p.m. Friday
Eureka 56, Peotone 27: The Hornets wrapped up Week 9 with a shutout victory, marking the fourth time not allowing any points this season. Eureka, however, is no slouch on offense either by scoring 31.9 points en route to its sixth playoff berth in a row. Peotone has won five playoff games in program history.
11 Paxton-Buckley-Loda (6-3) at 6 Monmouth-Roseville (8-1), 4 p.m. Saturday
Monmouth-Roseville 48, Paxton-Buckley-Loda 6: The Titans come into the playoffs following a shutout victory in Week 9. M-R started the season 7-0 before a 10-point loss in Week 8 loss to Class 2A Taylor Ridge Rockridge. P-B-L, which lost its final three regular-season games, is the playoffs for nine successive season.
13 Olympia (6-3) at 4 Nashville (8-1), 2:30 p.m. Saturday
Nashville 34, Olympia 26: The Spartans come off a big Week 9 victory, getting a school-record 420 yards from Jimmy Lollar, who also scored five TDs. Oly is averaging 34.7 points, against 30.7 allowed. Nashville has made the playoffs for the last five seasons including a pair of back-to-back Class 2A state runner-up finishes.
Class 2A
16 Deer Creek-Mackinaw (5-4) at 1 Farmington (9-0), 3:30 p.m. Saturday
Farmington 41, Dee-Mack 6: The Farmers came out unscathed in winning the LincolnLand-Large Division, which features four playoff-bound teams. Farmington QB Lane Wheelwright (ankle) will be back under center after missing the last two regular season games. Dee-Mack is one of five playoff teams in the Heart of Central Illinois-Large Division. The Chiefs will look to utilize QB Chuck Hathaway III and RB Max Eccles.
13 Fithian Oakwood (5-4) at 4 Elmwood/Brimfield (8-1), 7 p.m. Friday
Elmwood/Brimfield 48, Oakwood 16: The Trojans are playing with a heavy heart following the passing of coach Todd Hollis' father, David Hollis. Elmwood will continue to utilize its impressive ground game, rushing for 410 yards a game behind Bo Windish (1,574 yards, 22 TDs) and Matthew Glenn (1,473 yards, 18 TDs). Oakwood is led by QB Jackson Dudley (1,572 yards, 17 TDs) and is in the playoffs for the first time since 2019.
10 El Paso-Gridley (6-3) at 7 Seneca (8-1), 7 p.m. Friday
Seneca 41, El Paso-Gridley 26: EP-G is another of the five playoff teams from the HOCI-Large Division. The Titans are averaging 20.8 points, against 17.1 allowed. Seneca, which finished as the No. 5-ranked team statewide in Class 3A, is back in the playoffs for the 18th time, scoring 33.8 points a game.
11 Illini West (6-3) at 6 Chicago Christian (8-1), 5 p.m. Saturday
Chicago Christian 27, Illini West 18: IW is back in the playoffs for the first time since 2018. The Chargers are one of four LincolnLand-Large Division teams in the playoffs. The Knights are on a six-game win streak, allowing 12.8 points a game on the season. CC is in the playoffs for the 15th time in program history.
Class 1A
9 Rockford Lutheran (6-3) at 8 Annawan/Wethersfield (6-3), 1 p.m. Saturday
Annawan/Wethersfield 14, Rockford Lutheran 13: The Titans are one of four LincolnLand-Small Division teams in the Class 1A field. Annawan all-state running back Zeb Rashid left last week's game against Princeville with an injury. Lutheran is averaging 24.8 points and is one of six Big Northern Conference teams.
13 Ottawa Marquette (5-4) at 4 Rushville-Industry (8-1), 7 p.m. Friday
Rushville-Industry 34, Ottawa Marquette 16: The Rockets are another of the LincolndLand-Small Division squads in the Class 1A bracket. R-I has 10 playoff appearances in its program and two in the last three years. Marquette has lost two games heading into the playoffs, but has played five playoff teams.
12 Galena (5-4) at 5 Stark County (8-1), 2 p.m. Saturday
Stark County 42, Galena 18: The Rebels are going into the playoffs for the 26th time, having claimed 29 victories over that time including three state runner-up finishes. Stark County was the LincolnLand-Small Division champion despite a loss to Princeville in Week 7. Galena is in the playoffs for the first time since 2021.
10 Stockton (6-3) at 7 Princeville (7-2), 2 p.m. Saturday
Princeville 35, Stockton 17: Princeville is the final LincolnLand-Small Division team in the Class 1A field. The Princes has lost their last two games after beating Stark County in Week 7. A stopped two-point conversion by Annawan/Wethersfield in Week 9 was the lone difference in the Princeville getting the victory. Stockton last made the playoffs in 2019.

title: Peoria property listed at $1.3 million includes modest home, sprawling horse farm
author: Mike Kramer
description: Situated on a nearly 15-acre lot on Galena Road, this Peoria home offers a number of outbuildings, including arenas and a massive stable.
content:
This modest ranch home at 9203 N. Galena Road in Peoria seems somewhat small when measured against the $1.3 million price tag.
Yet the obvious selling point of the property isn't the 2,016-square-foot home with three bedrooms and two baths. It's the sprawling ranch attached.
The 14.7 acre lot comes with a large ranch built in 1930, with the listing calling it an "amazing piece of land with so many possibilities."
The property is currently home to the Heart of Illinois Horse arena and features a large indoor arena, several smaller outdoor arenas, a stable with the capacity to house about 130 horses, a public address system and a concession stand.
The home's asking price was reduced by $200,000 on October 8. Keller Williams Premier Realty is the listing agency.

title: Sleepers, final four and champs: IHSA football playoff predictions for all eight classes
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: With the playoffs here, the Journal Star predicts the 2024 IHSA high school football playoffs across all eight classes.
content:
The Illinois High School Association high school football playoffs begin this week, as 256 teams across eight classes begin their journey to win a state championship.
Peoria Journal Star sports reporter Adam Duvall lays out his predictions for each class, highlighting their final four teams, potential sleepers and who he think will be crowned the state champion in five weeks at Hancock Stadium.
Here's a look at this year's predictions, starting in Class 1A.
IHSA Class 1A predictions
What to watch: Three undefeated teams highlight the 32-team field. Le Roy (9-0) and No. 2 Lena-Winslow are the one and two seeds, respectively, in the upper half of the bracket. Lower half top-seed Belleville Althoff (9-0) will have a tough road to the Final Four.
Sleeper team: Stark County
IHSA Class 2A predictions
What to watch: Farmington (9-0) and Bismarck-Henning-Rossville-Alvin (9-0) are the lone undefeated teams in the Class 2A field. There are 12 8-1 teams in the bracket, ranging from the No. 1 to No. 7 seeds. Reigning Class 2A state champion Wilmington isn't the field this season.
Sleeper team: Downs Tri-Valley
IHSA Class 3A predictions
What to watch: This bracket as four 9-0 teams with top-seeds Byron (9-0) and St. Joseph-Ogden (9-0) as well as No. 2 seeds Wilmington (9-0) and Sullivan (9-0). Three Peoria-area teams are 8-1 with Princeton, Eureka and Monmouth-Roseville. Byron is the reigning Class 3A state champion.
Sleeper team: Lombard Montini
Title pick: Byron over Williamsville
IHSA Class 4A predictions
What to watch: Four undefeated teams are in the Class 4A field with Chicago Sullivan (9-0) and Chicago South Shore (9-0) being the top-two seeds in the upper half. Breese Central (9-0) and Olney Richland County (9-0) are the No. 1 and No. 2 seeds in the lower half of the bracket. Reigning state champ Rochester is in the field.
Sleeper team: Geneseo
IHSA Class 5A predictions
What to watch: Sycamore (9-0) is the lone undefeated in the field, getting the top seed in the upper half of the bracket. Peoria High (7-2) and Metamora (6-3) could potentially meet in the semifinals. Two-time reigning state champion LaGrange Park Nazareth (7-2) is the No. 3 seed in the upper half.
Sleeper team: Joliet Catholic Academy
Final four: Wheaton St. Francis, LaGrange Park Nazareth, Troy Triad Peoria High
Title pick: Peoria High over LaGrange Park Nazareth
IHSA Class 6A predictions
IHSA Class 7A predictions
What to watch: Two undefeated teams — Chicago Whitney Young (9-0) and Quincy (9-0) — are the top two seeds in the Class 7A bracket. Quincy made a run to the 2023 Class 7A quarterfinals last season. Chicago Mt. Carmel is the reigning state champion.
Sleeper team: Chicago Brother Rice
Final four: Batavia, Bradley-Bourbonnais, Chicago St. Rita, Chicago Mt. Carmel
Title pick: Chicago Mt. Carmel over Batavia
IHSA Class 8A predictions
What to watch: Four unbeaten teams — Frankfort Lincoln-Way East (9-0), LaGrange Lyons (9-0), Oswego (9-0) and West Aurora (9-0) — are the top-four seeds in the bracket. Wilmette Loyola Academy is the two-time reigning state champion. Lincoln-Way East and Loyola played for the title last season.
Sleeper team: Naperville Central

title: Several contested races emerging in spring 2025 races for Rockford City Council, mayor
author: Jeff Kolkey
description: Here is who has filed so far to run in next year's races for Rockford City Council and mayor. The deadline to file as a party candidate is today.
content:
(This story has been updated to include new information.)
Six primary battles and a contested race for mayor took shape on the last day of candidate filing for Rockford City Council.
Several City Council members filed to run for re-election next year and several newcomers also have come forward.
The filing period to run in the Feb. 25 consolidated primary election for municipal offices opened last week.
Monday was the last day for party candidates to file. Winners of the primary will go on to an April 1 consolidated general election, which will include races for City Council and mayor.
Here is an update on who submitted paperwork for Rockford City Council and mayor during the filing period..
Mayor
Rockford Mayor Tom McNamara has filed to run for re-election as a Democrat. McNamara announced a year ago that he was planning to seek a third term.
Androcles Morell, a computer repair business owner, has filed to run for mayor as a Republican.
Joseph "Joey" Canova, the former owner of Joey C's Cucina and Cocktails, has for a second time filed to run as a Republican candidate for mayor. Canova filed to run in the 2021 election was prevented from appearing on ballots following objections to his paperwork.
Ward 1
Longtime Ald. Tim Durkee, R-1, a physician with UW Health, has filed to run for re-election. Durkee has served on Rockford City Council since being appointed in December 2010 and was first elected in 2011. He is seeking a fifth term in office.
Ward 2
Ald. Jonathan Logemann, D-2, has filed for re-election. Logemann is a Rockford Public Schools teacher and U.S. Army Illinois National Guard officer. He is seeking his third term as alderman of the city's Second Ward.
Ward 3
Rockford native Ald. Chad Tuneberg, R-3, owner of a financial management firm, will seek a third term in office after first being elected in 2017.
Ward 4
Ald. Kevin Frost, R-4, a Rockford lawyer first elected alderman in 2013, is seeking re-election to a fourth term in office.
Ward 5
Ald. Gabrielle Torina, D-5, has filed paperwork to seek another four years representing Rockford's Fifth Ward. During her first term, Torina fought hard for approval of a $170 million project to redevelop the dilapidated former Barber-Colman factory campus into Colman Yards, a neighborhood of residential units, businesses, recreation and green space.
Torina faces challenges from Democrats Christopher Williams and Virgil Hobson, both of whom filed paperwork Monday before the deadline to run in the primary.
Ward 6
U.S. Postal Service letter carrier Lawrence L. Steward II emerged as a leader after the tragic killing of his friend and colleague Jay Larson during a March 27 spree violence in a Rockford neighborhood. President of the National Association of Letter Carriers Branch 245 in Rockford, Steward has filed to run for alderman of the Sixth Ward as a Democrat.
Ald. Aprel Prunty, D-6, a Rockford Public Schools teacher, has filed to seek re-election to a second term representing the ward where she grew up.
Ward 8
Ald. Karen Hoffman, D-8, has filed paperwork to seek a third term representing Rockford's Eighth Ward.
Ward 9
Ald. William "Bill" Rose, D-9, has filed seeking a third term on Rockford City Council.
Dawn Granath, a former Rockford Education Association president, has filed to run in the Ninth Ward as a Democrat.
Jeff Jaworowski, a Democrat and Rockford Housing Authority employee, has filed paperwork to represent Rockford's Ninth Ward.
Ward 10
Ald. Frank Beach, R-10, a U.S. Army veteran, has filed for re-election to represent the city's 10th Ward. Beach has represented the ward for 43 years.
Ward 11
Appointed to fill a vacancy left by the death of Ald. Tuffy Quinonez, D-11, Isidro Barrios has filed to seek election in the city's 11th Ward.
Barrios will face a challenge from Winnebago County Board Member Jaime Salgado who has also filed to run as a Democrat in the ward.
Ward 12
Ald. Gina Meeks, D-12, has filed to run for re-election. She will face a primary challenge from Democrat Carrie Crosby has filed paperwork to run for alderwoman in the city's 12th Ward.
Ward 13
Ald. Jeffrey Bailey, D-13, co-founder of Energy for All, where he provides marketing, consultant and business development services, was appointed to fill the remainder of longtime Ald. Linda McNeely's term when she died in April 2023. He has filed paperwork seeking election to the seat.
Bailey faces primary challenges from community advocate Tamir Bell, 21, Rockford resident Eddie Jane Harrell and Rockford resident Giovanni Mikaelson who have also filed to run as Democrats in the 13th Ward.
Ward 14
Lifelong Rockford resident and former Rockford Register Star journalist, Ald. Mark Bonne, D-14, will seek a second term in next year's election representing the 14th Ward.
Bonne faces a primary challenge from Rockford resident Ali Abuihmoud.

title: Where is my polling place? What to know about voting on Election Day in Illinois
author: Tom Ackerman
description: For those heading to the polls on Tuesday, here are some tips to help you know where to go and when in Illinois.
content:
Don't worry, the political ads are almost over as Election Day is quickly approaching.
If you haven't voted early, here's what you need to know about heading to the polls on Nov. 5.
Am I registered to vote?
Residents can check to see if they're registered to vote online at ova.elections.il.gov.
Can I register to vote online still?
No, online registration is closed.
Can I register at my polling location?
Yes, you can register at your polling location if you still need to register. Simply bring two forms of ID with at least one showing your current Illinois address.
Where is my polling place?
You can find your polling place online at ova.elections.il.gov.
When can I vote?
You can cast your vote between 6 a.m. and 7 p.m. on Nov. 5.
What do I need to bring?
If you are already a qualified, registered voter of Sangamon County, you will only need to bring yourself. Still, it's a good idea to have ID just in case of a technical issue. At your polling location, you will sign an application to vote, which pollsters compare with your signature from your voter registration.
Is it too late to vote-by-mail?
The deadline to request a mail-in ballot was Oct. 31. Once a voter receives their ballot in the mail, it must be postmarked no later than Nov. 5 or must be dropped into a designated drop box.
If you received a mail-in ballot but decide to vote in person, you must bring the mail-in ballot with you to your polling place to surrender the ballot so you can vote in person.

title: When CFP rankings are released, what to know for Big Ten football
author: John Leuzzi
description: The Big Ten will soon learn its place in the first CFP rankings of the 2024 season. We'll get a look at the 12-team playoff bracket as it stands now.
content:
With 10 weeks in the books, the picture for the College Football Playoff is becoming clearer.
On Tuesday, the CFP rankings will receive their first data point of the 2024 college football season, as the first of six playoff rankings will be released at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN.
As is the case every year, the usual suspects will doubtless make up the top of the rankings, including severall teams from the Big Ten in Oregon, Ohio State and Penn State. But because of the expanded field this year, other teams such as Indiana make a fascinating case as we approach the end to the season.
Here's what you need to know on when the first College Football Rankings come out, including how to watch, how many teams are in the CFP this season and much more:
When do CFP rankings come out?
The first College Football Playoff rankings will be released on Tuesday, Nov. 5 at 7 p.m. ET.
Here's a look at the full list of when the six CFP rankings will be released:
All times Eastern
Tuesday, Nov. 5: 7 p.m.
Tuesday, Nov. 12: 8:30 p.m.*
Tuesday, Nov. 19: 7 p.m.
Tuesday, Nov. 26: 8 p.m.
Tuesday, Dec. 3: 7 p.m.
Sunday, Dec. 8: Noon
* The second set of College Football Playoff rankings will be unveiled between games at the Champions Classic.
What time are CFP rankings?
The first of six College Football Rankings will be released at 7 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Nov. 5.
College Football Playoff rankings projections, predictions
Through the first 10 weeks of the season, the Big Ten has four contenders to make the College Football Playoff this year: No. 1 Oregon, No. 3 Penn State, No. 4 Ohio State and No. 13 Indiana.
Here's where some college football analysts have those four teams projected in the CFP rankings:
USA Today's Matt Hayes
Oregon: No. 2 seed
Penn State: No. 7 seed
Ohio State: No. 5 seed
Indiana: No. 11 seed
ESPN's Heather Dinich
Oregon: No. 1 (1 seed)
Ohio State: No. 2 (5 seed)
Penn State: No. 7 (7 seed)
Indiana: No. 11 (11 seed)
ESPN Staff
ESPN's experts unanimously have Oregon as No. 1 in the College Football Playoffs, and four of them have Indiana at No. 5. Eight have Ohio State at No. 5. Penn State is in across the board despite Saturday's loss. Click through to see how they picked.
How to watch CFP rankings show
Date: Tuesday, Nov. 5
Time: 7 p.m. ET
TV channel: ESPN
Streaming option: ESPN app | Fubo (free trial)
The first College Football Playoff rankings show will be broadcast nationally on ESPN. You can also stream Tuesday's show on the ESPN app (by logging in with your TV provider credentials) or on Fubo, which carries the ESPN family of networks and offers a free trial to new subscribers.
How many teams in CFP 2024?
For the first time in the College Football Playoff era, the CFP will be more than just four teams, expanding to 12 total: five automatic qualifiers and seven at-larges.
The previous model, in use from 2014 through 2023, allowed for only four teams to make the playoff. Its predecessor, the BCS, allowed for a two-team, single-game playoff that decided the national championship.
How does College Football Playoff format work?
The CFP takes on a vastly different format this year, not only expanding from four teams to 12, but also introducing first-round byes, automatic bids and home games.
The five highest-ranked conference champions, ostensibly the Power Four champions and one Group of Five champion, will each receive an automatic bid. The four highest-ranked of these teams will be seeded 1-4 and given a first-round bye. If the Group of Five champion is not among the top 12 teams in the final poll, it will be slotted in at the No. 12 spot.
From there, seven at-large teams will make up the remainder of the field, beginning with No. 5 and concluding with, presumably, the No. 11 team. Seeds 5-12 will play in first-round games either at the home of the higher-ranked team or at another location of their choice.
No. 5 will host No. 12; No. 6 will host No. 11; No. 7 will host No. 10; and No. 8 will host No. 9. From there, winners of the first-round games will advance to the quarterfinals to take on the top four seeds.
Of note: Once the final bracket has been revealed, there will be no "re-seeding" to ensure the highest-ranked team faces the lowest-ranked remaining team. That means No. 1 will play the winner of the No. 8/9 game; No. 2 will play No. 7/10; No. 3 will play No. 6/11 and No. 4 will play No. 5/12.
The CFP committee also will not make special arrangements to ensure teams that met in the regular season will avoid playing in the postseason.
The quarterfinal games this year will take place in the Fiesta, Peach, Rose and Sugar bowls, with preferential bowls given to the highest-ranked teams. For example, No. 1 Oregon would likely prefer the Rose Bowl, leaving either the Sugar or Peach Bowls to No. 2 Georgia, and so on.
The semifinal games will take place in the Orange Bowl and Cotton Bowl, and the 2025 College Football Playoff championship game will take place in Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

title: College football rankings: Big Ten teams in updated Coaches Poll, AP Top 25 after Week 10
author: John Leuzzi
description: Here's a look at where Big Ten teams appear in the Coaches Poll and AP Top 25 after Week 10 of the college football season:
content:
Show Caption
The Big Ten was at the center of the college football world in Week 10, and the conference's biggest games didn't disappoint.
No. 4 Ohio State traveled out to No. 3 Penn State — a game that had a significant impact on the national rankings and College Football Playoff — and walked out of hostile Beaver Stadium with a 20-13 win. With that, Ryan Day and the Buckeyes (7-1, 4-1 Big Ten) redeemed themselves of an earlier season loss in a top-five matchup to then-No. 3 Oregon.
Conversely, the loss extends Penn State's (7-1, 4-1 Big Ten) losing skid to Ohio State to eight straight, and puts James Franklin's record vs. ranked teams in the spot light yet again. That said, the Nittany Lions ' hopes of making the CFP aren't completely diminished in the 12-team era.
Behind big days from Dillon Gabriel and Jordan James, Oregon (9-0, 6-0) defended its No. 1 ranking in both polls by taking down Michigan (5-4, 3-3) by a score of 38-17 at The Big House. No. 13 Indiana (9-0) also kept its undefeated season alive by winning at Michigan State / Curt Cignetti's Hoosiers could be a top-10-ranked team heading into next week's game vs. the Wolverines.

title: These Peoria-area cross country runners are heading to the 2024 IHSA state meet
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Here are the Peoria-area runners who advanced from sectionals to the 2024 IHSA cross country state finals next weekend at Detweiller Park in Peoria.
content:
The Illinois High School Association state cross country meet is less than a week away after sectionals took place Saturday across the state.
In Class 1A meets, the top six placing teams along with the first 10 individual runners not on an advancing team moved on to state. In the Class 2A and 3A races, the first seven placing teams as well as the top-10 individuals not on a state-qualifier also head to state. The finals are set for Saturday, Nov. 9 at Detweiller Park in Peoria.
Here is how the Peoria-area runners fared at sectionals:
CLASS 1A
At Elmwood
Where: Maple Lane Country Club, Elmwood
Sectional champions: Boys — Elmwood/Brimfield. Girls — Williamsville.
