title: Presidential debate live updates: What time will Kamala Harris, Donald Trump face off?
author: Marina Pitofsky
description: Debate day is here. Keep up with the USA TODAY Network's coverage of former President Donald Trump and Vice President Kamala Harris' showdown.
content:
Debate day is here.
Former President Donald Trump and Vice President Kamala Harris will face off in Philadelphia on Tuesday. The Republican and Democratic nominees are set to lay out their vision for the country – and knock their opponent on issues ranging from inflation and the economy to abortion rights and the southern border.
The debate marks one of the first major hurdles for Harris in her 2024 bid for the White House. The vice president ascended to the top of the Democratic ticket earlier this year after President Joe Biden's disastrous debate performance sparked weeks of concerns that ultimately led to the end of his reelection campaign.
On Tuesday, Sept. 10, at 9 p.m. EDT, USA TODAY Network will stream The ABC News Presidential Debate Simulcast on the USA TODAY channel, available on most smart televisions and devices.
Keep up with the USA TODAY Network's live coverage all day.
How to stream the debate, watch the debate without cable
On Tuesday, Sept. 10, at 9 p.m. EDT, USA TODAY Network will stream The ABC News Presidential Debate Simulcast on the USA TODAY channel, available on most smart televisions and devices.
– USA TODAY Staff
Former Trump official Olivia Troye senses 'sea change' against ex-president
Olivia Troye, who worked as a national security adviser to former Vice President Mike Pence, said she's hearing from other Republicans who believe Donald Trump is too extreme and don't want him to return to the White House.
Troye, who quit her job in the administration after the Jan. 6 attack on the Capitol, is serving as a surrogate for Kamala Harris and is attending the debate as Harris' guest.
'I think I'm seeing a sea change,' Troye told reporters ahead of the debate. 'I'm hearing from Republicans across the country. I'm traveling to the swing states. I'm talking to them directly, and they're saying, 'I don't identify with that.''
Troye said her values haven't changed and that she doesn't agree with everything Harris and her running mate, Tim Walz, support. But, 'I believe there is a better future for our country getting away from the extremism that Donald Trump and MAGA represent,' she said.
– Michael Collins
Melania Trump raises questions about attempted assassination of her husband
Donald Trump hasn't complained much about his security before the July 13 attempt on his life, but some of his allies have including former first lady Melania Trump. In a video promoting her upcoming memoir, Melania Trump called the assassination attempt "a horrible, distressing experience," and said "the silence around it feels heavy."
"I can't help but wonder, why didn't law enforcement officials arrest the shooter before the speech," the former first lady said.
She added: "There is definitely more to this story, and we need to uncover the truth," she said.
Donald Trump's son, Eric Trump, added on X: "I want answers as well. Something is being hidden."
– David Jackson
Presidential debate bingo: Play USA TODAY's free game during the Harris-Trump showdown
It's time for another round of the presidential debate bingo! The game where you play along as Kamala Harris and Donald Trump share the stage for the first time as they compete for the White House this November. Grab a few friends and choose your bingo cards here.
– Saman Shafiq
Foo Fighters will donate to Kamala Harris after Trump used their song 'My Hero'
The Foo Fighters are fighting back.
A representative for the rock band told USA TODAY that the Donald Trump campaign did not ask them for permission to use the group's song "My Hero" at the former president's rally last month with Robert F. Kennedy Jr. in Glendale, Arizona, "and if they were, they would not have granted it."
The representative added that "any royalties received as a result of this use will be donated" to Vice President Kamala Harris ' presidential campaign.
Trump calls for government shutdown without voting legislation
While preparing for the debate, Trump took time Tuesday to urge Republican lawmakers to shut down the government if Congress does not approve voting policies he wants. Trump wants to bar migrants who are in the country illegally from voting – but that is already illegal. His proposal would require new voters to submit more documentary proof of citizenship.
Still, in a Truth Social post, Trump said Republicans in Congress should not approve a new spending plan without his voting plan. Congress' deadline to keep the government's doors open is Sept. 30.
"If Republicans in the House, and Senate, don't get absolute assurances on Election Security, THEY SHOULD, IN NO WAY, SHAPE, OR FORM, GO FORWARD WITH A CONTINUING RESOLUTION ON THE BUDGET," he said.
– David Jackson
T wo former Trump officials, Anthony Scaramucci and Olivia Troye, will be guests of Harris campaign
Two former officials in Donald Trump's administration will be at the presidential debate for the Harris campaign on Thursday.
Anthony Scaramucci, a former Trump White House communications director, and Olivia Troye, Homeland Security advisor to Vice President Mike Pence, will serve as surrogates for the campaign and warn what a second Trump presidency would look like.
'Listen, don't take it from us: Take it from the ones who know Donald Trump the best and who are telling the American people exactly how unfit Trump is to serve as president,' said Harris communications director Michael Tyler.
Trump will knock Harris on immigration at debate
One of the top issues Trump will hammer Harris on is immigration. Trump and his allies have labeled Harris as a 'border czar,' claiming that she was put in charge of the border and millions have crossed the border under her watch. Immigration experts previously debunked the claim, saying that Joe Biden tasked Harris with leading the administration's diplomatic efforts addressing the "root causes" of migration in El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras.
Trump will likely compare his immigration record with that of the Biden-Harris administration's at the debate.
Along the U.S.-Mexico border, migrant apprehensions plunged in July from a year ago, to the lowest level of the Biden era, according to U.S. Customs and Border Protection statistics provided to USA TODAY.
Trump: 'You don't know what to expect' ahead of debate
Expect Donald Trump to harp on Kamala Harris' change of position on various issues – an allegation she's repeatedly rejected.
"You don't know what to expect - she's changed all of her policies over the years," Trump told NBC News in a phone interview on Tuesday. Harris and aides, meanwhile, plan to stress Trump's personal attacks on the vice president and other prominent Democrats.
– David Jackson
Where do Trump and Harris stand on the wars in Israel, Ukraine?
Both Trump and Harris view Israel as a pivotal U.S. ally and have supported the country in the wake of Hamas' devastating attack on Oct. 7.
Still, both nominees have split from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at times. Trump earlier this year earlier this year called on Israel to 'finish up your war.' Harris has said Israeli leaders "must do more to protect civilian life" in Gaza.
Trump has said without evidence that, if elected, Russia's invasion of Ukraine would be settled within 24 hours, though it's not clear how he would negotiate with the countries. Harris has widely criticized Russia's invasion. In a major shift, the Biden administration earlier this year authorized Ukraine to use U.S. weapons to strike targets inside Russia.
– Marina Pitofsky
Bottoms up: Drinking games for tonight's debate
Tonight's debate is high stakes for both candidates, and millions of Americans are expected to tune in. For any viewers in need of entertainment with their politics, here are just a few drinking game ideas.
Spicy USA TODAY presidential debate bingo: Players will follow along with bingo cards, and each person to subsequently call bingo takes their numerically assigned shot (of alcohol, if of age and appropriate).
Debate foul, party foul: Essentially, if the candidates fail to follow the rules, viewers take a drink.
Line by line, sip by sip: Players should pick their political cliche of choice (think "my fellow Americans" or "We the People") and sip every time that line is said.
For more game details and specifics, read here.
– Savannah Kuchar and James Powel
Where do Harris and Trump stand on the border?
Trump has made immigration and southern border policy a cornerstone of his political career. He has long attacked undocumented immigrants, promising wide-reaching deportations if he's elected to a second term. The Trump administration also faced major criticism over immigration officials separating children and parents or other family at the border with Mexico.
Harris opposed the construction of a wall at the U.S.-Mexico border as a 2020 presidential candidate, but she backed bipartisan border legislation pushed by the Biden administration that would have allocated unspent dollars to continue the construction of a border wall, among a host of other measures.
– Marina Pitofsky and Joey Garrison
When is the vice presidential debate? Will Tim Walz and JD Vance debate?
Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz and Ohio Sen. JD Vance are gearing up to take the stage for a vice presidential debate after both accepted an Oct. 1 invitation from CBS News.
The outlet also offered the candidates the chance to debate on Sept. 17, Sept. 24, and Oct. 8, but neither accepted those invitations. Vance suggested they also debate Sept. 18, but Walz has not agreed to that date.
– Rachel Barber
Harris, Trump to meet – for the first time
Harris and Trump have had much to say about one another while campaigning for president. But tonight's debate marks the first time that the pair will actually meet face-to-face.
While both have been in politics and the public eye for decades now, the candidates have yet to cross paths.
Harris was present as a senator for Trump's State of the Union addresses, but the two did not interact then. And Trump did not attend her vice presidential inauguration after refusing to accept the 2020 election results.
– Savannah Kuchar and Phillip Bailey
Advocates urge prioritizing abortion discussion
Abortion rights activists are calling for tonight's debate moderators to prioritize the issue in their questions to candidates.
A petition by the progressive advocacy group MoveOn has garnered over 40,000 signatures, including support from actress Busy Philipps, and activists Amanda Zurwaski and Kaitlyn Joshua, who shared their personal abortion stories on stage at the Democratic National Convention last month.
Abortion is likely to come up tonight as a top concern in this year's election. Harris, who has long been a leading voice in the Biden administration on the issue, has made reproductive rights a cornerstone of her presidential campaign.
What is the typical length of a debate?
Presidential debates are typically 90 minutes long, including the one tonight.
The Biden-Trump debate in June hosted by CNN went from 9 p.m. to about 10:30 p.m.
In 2020, the first presidential debate between Biden and Trump was also about 90 minutes. It was moderated by former Fox News journalist Chris Wallace.
– Sudiksha Kochi
How old are the candidates?
Age was at the center of discussion about the 2024 election after the June debate between Biden and Trump.
Biden, 81, had a stumbling debate performance that night that ultimately led to him stepping aside and endorsing Harris to become the Democratic nominee.
Members of Congress, voters, and pundits wrung their hands publicly about it in the month after the debate while Trump sought to capitalize on Biden's poor performance. He mocked the president at a rally in Virginia the day after the debate and accused Biden of being a "part-time president" at a rally in Miami in July after Biden struggled to articulate his pitch to Americans on the debate stage.
So, how old is Trump, and how old is Harris?
Trump turned 78 years old in June and would be 82 by the end of his term if he were to win in November.
Harris will turn 60 in October and would be 64 years old by the end of her term if she were to win in November.
– Elizabeth Beyer, David Jackson and Charles Trepany
Are there more presidential debates?
Tonight's debate is currently the only face-off between Harris and Trump scheduled.
Trump had proposed two other dates in September for additional debates, while the Harris campaign said in a statement the vice president would agree to another meeting between the candidates in October.
Harris, Trump polling neck-and-neck in swing states
Harris and Trump head into debate night Tuesday essentially neck-and-neck in the 2024 swing states.
Trump had enjoyed a lead in these seven battlegrounds earlier this year when Biden was still in the race.
Shortly after taking over the ticket, though, Harris gained a slight advantage in Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Michigan, North Carolina and Arizona, and tied Trump in Georgia, according to a Cook Political Report survey last month. Trump continued to lead in Nevada by 5 points.
And a Detroit Free Press survey late last month found Trump ahead again by one point in Michigan.
Essentially, the race could not be tighter, and both candidates will be vying tonight for support from voters in these key states.
What are the debate rules and who are the moderators?
The debate will be 90 minutes long with two commercial breaks. There will be no props or pre-written notes allowed onstage, and candidates will be given a pen, pad of paper and a water bottle. Candidates' microphones will be live only for the candidate whose turn it is to speak and muted when the time belongs to another candidate.
The two moderators for the debate are ABC journalists Linsey Davis and David Muir. Muir is a broadcast journalist who is the host and managing editor of "ABC World News Tonight with David Muir." Muir interviewed Biden earlier this year as a part of D-Day coverage and was Trump's first White House interview as president in 2017.
Davis hosts "ABC News Live Prime," ABC News' streaming evening newscast, and weekend "World News Tonight" on Sundays. She is also a correspondent for "World News Tonight," "Good Morning America," "20/20" and "Nightline."
– Saman Shafiq, Gabe Hauari, and Sudiksha Kochi
Who won which states in 2020?
In the 2020 presidential race, Biden won 306 electoral votes to Trump's 232. Of the 538 votes in the Electoral College up for grabs, a candidate must receive 270 of those votes to win.
In 2020, Biden won six of the seven states deemed battlegrounds in this year's election: Arizona, Wisconsin, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Georgia and Nevada. Trump won one of this year's battleground states in 2020: North Carolina.
Battleground, or swing states, are those that flipped parties in the presidential election between 2016 and 2020.
As Vice President Kamala Harris and Trump prepare to face off on the debate stage in Philadelphia later this evening, take a look at how the 2020 race shook out along with some background on the Electoral College.
– Elizabeth Beyer
Where is the debate?
The debate between Donald Trump and Kamala Harris will take place in Philadelphia at the National Constitution Center.
Pennsylvania is one of a handful of battleground states that could be key in deciding the outcome of this year's presidential election.
How candidates are approaching the debate
Catch up on the dynamics going into the debate tonight with these USA TODAY stories:
Trump's debate plan? Attack, attack, attack
With a lot on the line, will Harris the prosecutor show up on the debate stage?
7 things to watch in the Trump, Harris debate
– USA TODAY Staff
How to watch Trump, Harris debate
ABC News will host the debate between Kamala Harris and Donald Trump Tuesday. However, multiple channels, including NBC and CNN, will broadcast the event as well.
– Savannah Kuchar
Tuesday's debate is set to begin at 9 p.m. ET.

title: How big plays fueled Washington's big victory at Pekin
author: Dave Eminian
description: With a big-play receiver, a tough defense and solid kicker, Washington escaped Pekin with a big Mid-Illini football victory.
content:
(This story was updated to add photos.)
PEKIN — A.J. Jones delivered a knockout shot with one hand tied behind his back Friday in a heavyweight battle between two Mid-Illini Conference teams trying to establish themselves as elite contenders.
Washington got off the ropes from a halftime deficit and ground out a 19-9 comeback victory over Pekin at Memorial Stadium in a game of big plays, big mistakes and big numbers of penalties.
The Panthers put it away with a 25-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Humphrey to receiver Jones with 4:43 left in the fourth quarter.
The third-and-11 pass arced down the middle of the field off play action, and Jones made a spectacular catch. His right arm pinned by a defender draped on his back, he reached up with his left arm and made-a one-handed grab just inside the goal line as he hit the turf.
"They put all their trust in me," Jones said of his teammates. "He said, 'I'm going to throw it up to you and let you make a play, be the player you are. The ball came in … I went up … but the DB actually took my right arm behind my back, and I went up with one and made a helluva catch.
"I'm just so proud of us right now."
Washington climbed out of an 0-2 start to its season and leveled off at 2-2 overall and 2-0 in Mid-Illini Conference play. Pekin, a week after a big road upset of Dunlap, is 2-2 overall and 1-1 in Mid-Illini Conference play.
Big plays and flag football
The game saw 18 penalties called, including 11 against Pekin, which also managed to get two sideline warnings in the game's first 22 minutes. At one point in the first half, the Dragons had players standing so far back from the sideline they were on the track.
Emerging Dragons star Dylan Anderson — who scored three touchdowns and had a game-saving INT on a two-point try in Pekin's upset win at Dunlap last week — got right back to his big-play business when he intercepted Humphrey's 28-yard pass at the Pekin 1 on the game's opening drive.
"I just wish we could have finished this game," the sophomore said. "I'm really disappointed, feel like I let us down."
Anderson caught a strike from quarterback Brogan Benassi and flashed his 4.4/40 speed to race 73 yards for a touchdown and 6-6 tie with 11:06 left in the second quarter. He also recovered a teammate's fumble later in the game.
Washington built a 6-0 lead on a pair of first-quarter field goals — 26 yards and 41 yards — from junior Devin Miller.
The Panthers were driving early in the second quarter, reaching the Pekin 32 before running back Hunter Reed's fumble was recovered by Pekin senior Landon Erxleben at 7:54.
Pekin took over and scratched on top with a 22-yard field goal from junior Logan McCann with 71 seconds left in the first half. That capped a 14-play, 63-yard drive that ate up 6:43, and sent the Dragons to halftime in control.
Perhaps the pivotal series of the game arrived as the third quarter opened, and saw Pekin launch a 13-play, 75-yard drive that consumed the first 6:05 of the quarter.
Running back Ty Jackson recovered his own fumble to start that series. It ended with McCann initially booting a 26-yard field goal. But it was wiped out on a false start penalty, and the re-kick from 31 yards was blocked by Washington junior Parker Westerfield and Pekin came away without points.
The Panthers then rode Reed for six carries and 64 yards to take the lead, 13-9, on his 22-yard TD run around the left edge, during which he broke three tackles.
Pekin never recovered, and Washington put it out of reach with 4:34 left on Jones' one-handed TD catch.
A view from up front
Washington got 26 carries for 164 yards and a TD from Reed. Jones added two catches for 40 yards and a TD. Miller booted field goals of 26 and 41.
Pekin got 22 carries for 112 yards from Jackson. Benassi was 9 of 17 passing for 147 yds and one TD. Anderson had three catches for 86 yds, 1 TD, plus two carries for 18 yds, an interception and a fumble recovery.
The game produced 18 penalties (11 Pekin), 2 sideline warnings (Pekin). Washington threw an INT and fumbled 3 times (lost 1). Pekin fumbled 3 times (lost 1) and had a FG blocked.
Yet up front where the big and bravest battled, it was fun to watch.
"The trenches lived up to its name tonight," said Washington 6-foot-3, 260-pound senior guard Cash Wisher. "We were in a battle there for sure, and in between plays there was maybe a little talking, you know boys being boys.
"We wanted to come out and punch those guys in the face from the start, and I think we did."
Dave Eminian is the Journal Star sports columnist, and covers Bradley men's basketball, the Rivermen and Chiefs. He writes the Cleve In The Eve sports column for pjstar.com. He can be reached at 686-3206 or deminian@pjstar.com. Follow him on X.com @icetimecleve.

title: Peoria Planned Parenthood location will now perform procedural abortions
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: The clinic reopened in May after a firebombing in January 2023.
content:
Peoria's Planned Parenthood location will now offer procedural abortions after a firebombing attack on the building last year shuttered its operations.
The clinic reopened in May after undergoing extensive renovations after the January 2023 attack that caused over $1 million in damages.
Planned Parenthood said Monday that patients will now have access to a "full range of abortion options" at the Peoria Health Center at 2709 W. Knoxville Ave.
"When we renovated Peoria after it was attacked, we purposefully designed it with flexibility in mind so we can expand our care options as needed. Since PPIL continues to see a flood of patients needing care in central Illinois we are proud to now offer the full spectrum of abortion care in Peoria,' Chief Medical Officer Amy Whitaker said in a news release.
Chillicothe man Tyler Massengill was sentenced to 10 years in prison and ordered to pay $1.4 million in damages for the attack on the Planned Parenthood building.
Massengill was angry that his girlfriend and received an abortion and tossed a Molotov cocktail into the building on Jan. 15, 2023.

title: Penn State vs Illinois 2021: Revisiting 9-overtime game, the longest in college football history
author: Ehsan Kassim
description: Penn State football hosts Illinois on Saturday for the first time since 2021. Here's a look back at at the nine-overtime game in 2021:
content:
Show Caption
The last time Penn State football hosted Big Ten rival Illinois at Beaver Stadium, the longest game in college football history broke out.
On Oct. 23, 2021, the Fighting Illini outlasted the Nittany Lions 20-18 in nine overtimes in a game that lasted four hours and 10 minutes. The game kicked off at 12:06 p.m., lasted until 4:17 p.m. and featured five scoreless overtime periods with the teams.
Interestingly, Penn State entered the 2021 contest as the No. 7 team in the country. This season, the Nittany Lions are No. 8 in the US LBM Coaches Poll. The Fighting Illini are off to a 4-0 start, which is the best start for the program since 2011 when they started 6-0 to start the regular season under Ron Zook.
The nine overtimes beat the previous record of seven overtimes, though the 20-18 game was by far the lowest scoring output of any of the games that lasted at least seven overtimes. In the ninth overtime, Brandon Peters completed a two-point try to Casey Washington clinched the upset road victory for the Fighting Illini.
Here's a look back at the nine-overtime game between Penn State football and Illinois:
Penn State-Illinois football play nine overtimes
Penn State entered the game ranked No. 7 in the country, sitting at 5-1. Its lone loss came by a field goal on the road to No. 3 Iowa. The Nittany Lions looked well on the way to a bounce-back victory over the 2-5 Fightining Illini when they took a 10-0 lead with 11:12 left in the first half on a field goal by Jordan Stout. It proved to be the final score of regulation for Penn State.
Illinois running back Chase Brown scored a 1-yard touchdown late in the first half. Kicker James McCourt tied the game with 11:27 left in the fourth quarter, eventually sending it to overtime. Each team hit a field goal in the first two overtime periods to send the game to a third overtime, in which the teams traded only 2-point conversion attempts.
Prior to 2021, dueling 2-point conversions didn't occur until the fifth overtime. This rule was introduced for the 2019 season in response to the November 2018 game between Texas A&M and LSU, which went seven overtimes.
Penn State attempted the 'Philly Special' play the Philadelphia Eagles used to win Super Bowl LII, but tight end Tyler Warren missed the mark on a throw to quarterback Sean Clifford to potentially win the game in the third overtime. Neither team could score on dueling goal-line attempts from the 2-yard line from periods three through seven.
Finally, Isaiah Williams ran in for a score in the eighth overtime for Illinois, but Penn State running back Noah Cain ran in from 2 yards to tie the game at 18. In the ninth overtime, linebacker Khalan Tolson broke up Clifford's pass to Parker Washington, giving Illinois a chance to win. Peters, who entered the game after start Artur Sitkowski exited with an energy, hit Washington for the game-winning touchdown.
Notably, Brown ― who now plays for the NFL's Cincinnati Bengals ― finished with 33 rushes for 223 yards and a touchdown in the victory. Penn State receiver Jahan Dotson, a former first-round pick who now plays for the Eagles, had six receptions for 69 yards. Washington is a Jacksonville Jaguar. Warren is one of the few leftovers for Penn State from 2021.

title: 'Ordained by God': Supporters voice support for Donald Trump at Peoria rally
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: An estimated 150 cars participated in the car caravan and rally for Donald Trump.
content:
A few hundred people gathered at Peoria Expo Gardens on Sunday to rally for former President Donald Trump in a presidential race they characterized as "good vs. evil."
An estimated 150 cars participated in the "Trump Train Patriot Rally" in which vehicles and motorcycles decorated in pro-Trump materials paraded themselves from Detweiller Park to Expo Gardens, where a handful of food trucks, Trump merchandise vendors and a stage waited for them.
Central to the theme of the rally were typical Republican campaign ideals such as stepping up control of the southern border and repealing abortion access.
Yet, throughout the rally Sunday in Peoria, calls back to the 2020 election and repeated a false claim that Donald Trump won the election also was a frequent talking point.
The crowd in attendance cheered when the audio speakers played a song titled "Trump Won and You Know It" and signaled their approval throughout the rally when multiple speakers echoed a false claim put out by former President Trump that the 2020 election was rigged and he actually won.
Congressional candidate Jim Marter, who is running against Lauren Underwood in Illinois' 14th Congressional District, received a cheer from the crowd when he asked, "how many people here think the election was stolen?" which was doubled down with a claim that "Democrats cheat" to win elections.
Another talking point repeated by multiple speakers at the rally on Sunday was that Donald Trump was "ordained by God" to win the 2024 election.
Republican Tom Bell said in a speech that he "firmly believes Donald Trump is ordained by God" and added that the 2024 election was a choice between "good and evil" where Republicans represented good and Democrats represented evil.
Bell said Trump would "bring the country back to God" and said Democrat policies were "evil" before claiming that Democrats would offer sex-change surgeries to 5-year-olds and would use abortions as a form of birth control.
Jim Fraher, the event's organizer, also said in a speech that he believed "Trump is doing God's will."
Fraher, who works part time as both a travel agent and at a gas station, said the turnout for the event, which he spent three months organizing, was "amazing" and had exceeded his expectations.
He estimated that 150 cars had participated in the rally.

title: When do fall colors and leaf watching peak in Illinois? Here's what to know
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: AccuWeather predicts that the nation's best leaf watching will be found in much of the heartland, including Illinois.
content:
As leaves begin to change, a "vibrant" fall — among the nation's most colorful — is predicted for Illinois. Here's a look at the 2024 foliage forecast and when to expect peak viewing in the Prairie State.
What is the Illinois outlook?
AccuWeather predicts that the nation's best leaf watching will be found in much of the heartland. "I think the best places to go are parts of the Midwest. The trees should have nice reds and oranges, and that could extend all the way down to parts of the Ozarks and parts of southern Missouri," writes meteorologist Paul Pastelok. An AccuWeather map puts Illinois at the center of its "vibrant" foliage zone.
When do leaf colors change?
Leaves can change color from mid-September through early November, writes the Old Farmer's Almanac, depending on location and weather conditions. The second and third week of October are typical peak times, adds the Old Farmer.
When do colors change in Illinois?
The Prairie State's fall color season typically begins in northern Illinois by mid to late September, according to the Illinois Department of Natural Resources. The color change normally starts in the second week of October in central Illinois and by mid to late October in the southern part of the state.
When do colors peak in Illinois?
Peak colors usually occur in mid-October in northern and central Illinois, and by late October or early November in southern Illinois, adds IDNR.
Tracking the Illinois color change
The EnjoyIllinois website offers a Fall Colors Trip Planner, which tracks the foliage change from beginning to end. It predicts a full color peak by Oct. 15 for northern Illinois, by Oct. 22 for central Illinois, and by late October for southern Illinois.
Meanwhile, the ExploreFall.com Fall Foliage Map 2024 estimates peak color about a week later in each of those areas.
Where can I see peak colors in Illinois?
EnjoyIllinois.com recommends the Galena area and Starved Rock State Park in northern Illinois, among other areas, in its Fall Colors Trip Planner. In southern Illinois, it lists areas in and around Shawnee National Forest. It also suggests the Great River Road and Pere Marquette State Park.
The Old Farmer's Almanac ranks Pere Marquette as the eighth-best place to see fall foliage in the United States.
Where are prime spots in central Illinois?
Central Illinois offers a wealth of options for leaf peepers. Drives include the Illinois River Road National Scenic Byway and Grand View Drive. Hikes and walks include the Illinois River Bluff Trail connecting Detweiller Park with three other Peoria Park District properties. Tower Park

title: How Peoria and Pekin are featured in new Netflix documentary 'Will & Harper'
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: The road trip documentary filmed in central Illinois in March 2023. It is now available streaming on Netflix.
content:
Peoria plays a small but important role in the documentary film 'Will & Harper,' released recently on Netflix.
The road trip doc features comedian and actor Will Ferrell and his longtime friend Harper Steele. The two met while both worked at ' Saturday Night Live,' where Steele was a writer and Ferrell a performer. Steele came out at transgender in 2022.
The duo spent 16 days crossing the country visiting sporting events, dive bars, diners and tourist traps from New York to California — places Steele once loved to frequent but now is wary to return. The trip proved not only a way for Ferrell and Steele to connect as friends, but for Steele to finally traverse America as her true self.
The 1-hour, 54-minute doc was partially filmed in Peoria and Pekin in March 2023, with the duo stopping at Maquet's Rail House in Pekin and the Basket Case in Peoria. Both locations appear in the movie.
Need a break? Play the USA TODAY Daily Crossword Puzzle.
The Peoria-area segment appears about 37 minutes into the film, with the words 'Peoria, Illinois' appearing onscreen in a graphic atop shots of Peoria streets and signs. The central Illinois visit is about Day 6 of their trip, sandwiched between stops in Indiana and Iowa. In all, the segment runs about 5 minutes — but includes one of the film's most memorable and heartbreaking moments.
Ferrell and Steele are at the Rail House, speaking with Pekin transgender woman Dana Garber, who relays stories of her childhood and her transition. Garber, a retired counselor, shared many of those stories in a Journal Star story in 2021.
During the conversation, as Ferrell and Steele look on pensively, Garber shares her mental struggles as a trans woman. At one point in her life, Garber said, she prayed to God to 'fix me or kill me — one or the other.'
The trio then move to The Basket Case in Peoria, where Steele thanks the crowd for their support and is shown singing Sonny and Cher's 'I Got You, Babe" along with Ferrell and Garber.
Central Illinois is shown on screen one last time as a map overlay displays Interstate 74 up from Peoria, through Galesburg, as the duo moves on to Steele's home state of Iowa.

title: Fundraising aims to help family of 10-year-old boy who was shot and killed in Peoria
author: Zach Roth
description: A GoFundMe has been established to help pay funeral expenses for the young boy who died "far too soon."
content:
A local banker has organized a GoFundMe for the family of a 10-year-old boy killed in a shooting Sunday west of Downtown Peoria.
Lamar T. Johnson II of Peoria died Sunday night after he was shot in the 600 block of West Romeo B. Garrett Avenue. Briggett Carter-Meachem, a senior vice president at Busey Bank, set up the fundraiser Monday, with a goal of raising $15,000 before the boy's funeral service on Oct. 11.
Carter-Meachem said in the GoFundMe post that she was calling on the Peoria community to come together to help Johnson's family as they mourn the death of a child taken "far too soon."
"No family should have to bear the unimaginable pain of losing a child, and no parent should ever have to worry about how they will give their child a proper goodbye," Carter-Meachem said. "Let us come together as a community and show his family that they are not alone. Your generosity, prayers, and support during this tragic time will mean the world to them."
Carter-Meachem also promised that a memorial account would be opened at Busey in honor of Johnson to provide even more assistance to his loved ones. The goal for each of the accounts is to raise enough for funeral expenses and to relieve the family's financial stress.
As of Tuesday afternoon, the GoFundMe had raised $760 for Johnson's family.
According to the Peoria Police Department, Johnson was found down with a gunshot wound Sunday night around 7:36 p.m. He was transported to a hospital where he was later pronounced dead.
An initial report from Peoria County Coroner Jamie Harwood indicated that Johnson had sustained a gunshot wound to the chest and likely died within seconds of the shooting. He had initially been identified as being from Springfield; however, Harwood said that his parents had residence in both Springfield and Peoria and the child was living in Peoria at the time of his death.
No suspect has been found in the shooting, according to PPD. Anyone with further information on the case is asked to contact the department at (309) 673-4521 or provide an anonymous tip through their Tip411 service. They can also contact Crime Stoppers at (309) 673-9000.

title: Pitted floors and soiled surfaces: Tazewell County's best and worst restaurant inspections
author: Mike Kramer
description: The Tazewell County Health Department's September restaurant inspections found six places with five or more demerits.
content:
The Tazewell County Health Department inspects a variety of local establishments, focusing on general cleanliness, maintenance and issues that could contribute to the spread of foodborne illness.
In September, the Journal Star examined about 60 routine inspections conducted by the health department on restaurants, mobile establishments and bars in Tazewell County.
Terminology used by the health department
Foodborne Illness Risk Factors: Risk factors are practices and procedures identified as the most prevalent contributing factors to foodborne illness.
Public Health Interventions: These are control measures meant to prevent foodborne illness or injury.
Good Retail Practices: Good Retail Practices are preventive measures to control the addition of pathogens, chemicals, and physical objects into food.
Demerits: The health department's demerits system is based on the number of violations found during a regular food establishment inspection. A total demerit score of zero indicates no critical violations were noted at the time of the inspection. The health department noted that a score of zero demerits does not mean perfect conditions exist. Scores and demerits only represent the state of the facility at the time of inspection. Several Tazewell County establishments had no demerits, and six had five or more demerits.
No demerits
American Legion Post #382 - 118 E. Third Street, Delavan
Eli's - 205 W. Jefferson Street, Morton
Grandma Nana's Kitchen Mobile Truck - 26941 Robinhood Lane, Tremont
Hilltop Grill Mobile - 100 Village Court, Creve Coeur
Monical's Pizza - 06 Cherry Tree Center, Washington
Plaza Lanes, LLC - 1500 W. Washington Road, Washington
Simply Sweet Cakes - 107 W. Pearl Street, Tremont
Tremont American Legion - 24584 Lake Windemere Road, Tremont
Five or more demerits
Bob's Dairy Dream, 108 Melville Court, East Peoria
Eight demerits: The health department identified four risk factor violations that included employees handling hamburger buns with bare hands after handling raw hamburger, improper hand-washing procedures, and food-contact surfaces that had not been properly cleaned and sanitized. All discrepancies were corrected on site.
Cranwill's Drive-in, 1713 S. Second Street, Pekin
Six demerits: Cranwill's had five risk factor violations, including four repeat infractions. The health department found two cartons of eggs being stored above cut fresh produce, a hand sink being used to dispose of sanitizer, an improperly labeled and inadequately supplied handwashing sink, and an unlabeled container of chlorine bleach sanitizer.
Emerald Tea Room & Catering, 132 McKinley Street, East Peoria
Five demerits: Nasturtium flowers found in the refrigerator were not from an approved retailer and could not be served.
Famous City Billiards, 221 N. Main Street, Creve Coeur
Five demerits: Famous City's risk factor violations included a build-up of debris on the lip of the food preparation table, stove top, and cooking utensils; a handwashing sink containing alcohol bottles, a funnel, and towels; and non-food contact surfaces that were visibly soiled and greasy to the touch. The Health Department also observed a leak in the floor, a makeshift grease trap, worn and pitted concrete flooring in the kitchen, and makeshift mat flooring in the bar area. Additionally, all food handler certificates on file with the Health Department were expired.
Water issues and many violations: Best and worst Peoria food inspections for August 2024
Monical's Pizza, 111 S. Parkway Drive, Pekin
Five demerits: The health department found a used sanitizer cloth stored on a back table rather than being properly stored in a sanitizer solution. The good retail practices violation was corrected on site.
Super Gyros, 200 Veterans Drive, East Peoria
Paper towels were not available at the front hand sink during the inspection, and the ice machine baffle was heavily soiled. The prep table on the front line was not holding at 41 degrees or below.

title: East Peoria grad has a new romance novel, soon to become a Hallmark movie
author: Mike Kramer
description: East Peoria grad's new novel "Her Knight at the Museum" is scheduled for a November release and is in development for a Hallmark movie.
content:
The newest book from author and East Peoria graduate Bryn Donovan is a "fun, feel-good escape" and next year is expected to appear on your television screen.
"Her Knight at the Museum" is a magical romantic comedy novel set to release in paperback, audiobook and e-book Nov. 12, 2024, from Berkley, Penguin Random House. The book is also available for pre-order at all bookstores and is currently in development for a Hallmark movie that is tentatively scheduled for release in 2025.
Donavan, also a graduate of Knox College, submitted her manuscript during an open submission period that allowed authors to submit novels without an agent. Her book was one of four novels chosen for publication from more than 5,000 submissions. Berkley offered Donavan a two-book contract, and she is currently working on a sequel to 'Her Knight at the Museum."
What is 'Her Knight at the Museum' about?
The book begins in the Middle Ages, when a knight Sir Griffin de Beauford defeats his best friend in a tournament. Furious at the defeat, the friend becomes a bitter enemy, studies sorcery, and turns Griffin to stone. He somehow ends up in the Art Institute of Chicago, where art conservator Emily Porter breaks the curse and brings him back to life ... only to become a prime suspect in the subsequent investigation of a missing sculpture.
"I love the Art Institute of Chicago, and one day when I was there, I imagined one of the life-sized sculptures being able to see, hear and think," Donavan said. "I've also loved King Arthur stories since I was a child."
Donavan said writing about her main character's comic sense of wonder at the modern world heightened her optimism and appreciation for everyday life. She hopes "Her Knight at the Museum," and the sequel will provide the same experience for readers.
"I think all of us get down sometimes because of the news or personal issues," she said, "and I want these books to be a fun, feel-good escape."
Donovan is also the author of several other romance novels, including " Sunrise Cabin," a bestseller with Publishers Weekly. She's also written books about the craft of writing and the story treatments for two Hallmark Channel, according to her online bio. Her work has appeared also has appeared in McSweeney's, Writer's Digest and other literary journals.

title: Skittles, PB&J and music: What is the gameday routine for high school football players?
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Food. Music. Lock in. We asked Peoria-area high school football players what they do for a pregame routine. The answers will delight you.
content:
High school football players spend countless hours practicing, conditioning and hitting the weight room.
So, how do they prepare for gameday?
That's what we asked players around the Peoria area in the fifth of a multi-part series in which the Journal Star talks with high school football coaches and players about numerous topics relating to the world of preps pigskin. So far, we've asked coaches about program mottos and asked players who should get the ball in crunch time along with what's the toughest position to play.
As we head into Week 7, here is what some of the large- and small-school football players had to say about their pregame routines.
Mentally and spiritually prepared
"To just get focused and focus on winning and doing it at 100 percent." — Cameron Clark, Richwoods

title: Why the Peoria Rivermen got a wave of talent just days before SPHL season opener
author: Dave Eminian
description: The Peoria Rivermen will likely have received 10 players down from ECHL training camps by the time Tuesday night arrives. Opening night is Friday.
content:
PEORIA — Here comes the cavalry.
The Peoria Rivermen received a wave of players from ECHL camps on Monday morning that changed the outlook for their team in the early going. The defending SPHL champions ave nine players down from Double-A training camps and could get more.
They'll have to get them into practices and sort through lineup possibilities in time for their SPHL 2024-25 season opener at Quad City on Friday.
Who did the Peoria Rivermen add?
Rivermen winger Mike Gelatt — a key producer for the team's championship last spring — and defenseman Josh Martin both arrived from ECHL Bloomington. Defenseman Nick Aromatario came down from Trois-Rivieres, while defenseman Chase Spencer was due to arrive Monday night from ECHL Tulsa and goaltender Troy Kobryn was on the way from ECHL Tulsa. Goaltender Colby Muise came in from ECHL Atlanta. Forward Jake Vaughan was expected to arrive some time Tuesday from ECHL South Carolina's camp.
In addition, key Rivermen defenseman Renat Dadadzhanov was scheduled to be in ECHL Maine's camp, but he had issues getting his border paperwork ready in time. He never skated in Maine's camp, and he's believed to be headed now to the Rivermen as a 10th player technically coming down from the ECHL.
"We're excited to have all these guys join us," Rivermen coach Jean-Guy Trudel said. "It will make our camp more competitive. There's a lot of talent, a lot of skill in this group and we have get it all put together in the next few days. So we have work to do."
A pair of newbies
Among the players coming in from ECHL camps were two new players, forward Frankie Trazzera and defenseman Brock Bartholomew, signed by the Rivermen on Monday.
Bartholomew, 23, is a 6-foot-4, 200-pound blueliner down from ECHL Wichita's camp. A project for Rivermen head coach Jean-Guy Trudel, he turned pro in 2022-23 with Alfta GIF in Sweden's tier-2 pro league. He broke out for 23 goals and 40 assists in 53 games last season for the Hull Seahawks in the National Ice Hockey League, Britain's secondary pro level.
Trazzerra, 26, is a 6-foot-4, 225-pound forward coming from ECHL Allen's camp. He played four years of junior hockey for Lone Star in the NAHL, serving as captain in his final season. He moved on to play four seasons for NCAA Div.-III Trine University, then turned pro last season with Elmira in the FPHL (7 goals, 3 assists in 16 games).
Still battling for ECHL jobs
The Rivermen could still get more players as several of their signings are still sticking with ECHL teams in camp.
Trudel's son, winger Tristan Trudel, is with Fort Wayne. Veteran winger Tyler Kobryn is with Florida, winger Cole Crowder is with Worcester and center John Kaljian is at Allen.
ECHL teams open their 2024-25 season this weekend, as does the SPHL.

title: Where Illinois football's Bret Bielema ranks in coach pay in USA TODAY annual report
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Illinois football coach Bret Bielema is in the top 30 among the highest paid coaches in college football.
content:
Illinois coach Bret Bielema is the 29th highest-paid coach in college football but trails nine other Big Ten Conference coaches, according to USA TODAY Sports' annual analysis of coaches' compensation released Wednesday.
Bielema got a small bump this season, his total pay at $6.65 million, up from his $6.5 million in 2023. He earned $4.2 million and $4.3 million his first two seasons in Champaign.
Bielema's salary ranking among the Big Ten shows how much the league's schools must pay to keep the top coaches. USC's Lincoln Riley and Ohio State's Ryan Day lead the Big Ten with total pay of just more than $10 million, both in the top five nationally.
The Southeastern Conference far and away has the highest-paid coaches, with 12 of the top 25. Georgia's Kirby Smart is the highest paid in the SEC and the country, at $13.3 million.
Here are the highest paid coaches in the Big Ten for 2024, along with national rank:
Big Ten Conference coach pay 2024
Lincoln Riley (USC): $10.04 million, 4th nationally
Ryan Day (Ohio State): $10.02 million, 5th nationally

title: Who is the Peoria Journal Star high school football MVP so far?
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Here are a few names that have pushed themselves into the MVP discussion for high school football with two weeks to go in the regular season.
content:
Show Caption
The Illinois high school football season has a couple of weeks remaining, but plenty of Peoria-area players have proven their worth on the field.
Now is your chance to let us know which player is the most valuable so far. So, who will it be?
Here are 10 Peoria-area MVP candidates so far for the 2024 high school football season. Information about each candidate is below. Vote from now until noon Thursday Oct. 24. The winner be be revealed ahead of Week 9.
Week 8 previews: Schedule | Power rankings | Playoff outlook | Predictions
Dylan Anderson, Pekin
The 5-foot-11, 168-pound sophomore wide receiver has been a touchdown-scoring machine this season. Anderson has found the end zone in all seven games this season for the Dragons (5-2). His latest score came on a 31-yard TD run in last week's 42-7 win over Canton. Anderson also has two 80-yard TD catches this season.
Austin Gerber , Eureka
The 5-foot-7, 142-pound senior quarterback is the catalyst for the undefeated and the Class 3A eighth-ranked Hornets (7-0). Gerber is throwing for 165 yards a game, totaling 1,155 yards and eight touchdowns. His legs may even have been more dangerous, rushing for 410 yards and 10 TDs in seven games.
Breon Green, Peoria High
The 5-foot-10, 165-pound junior quarterback has orchestrated the potent Peoria High offense. The Class 5A sixth-ranked Lions have accounted for 3,726 total yards (1,299 passing, 2,427 rushing) along with 48 total TDs (31 rushing, 17 passing). Green threw for 290 yards and three TDs in a 46-40 win over Peoria Notre Dame in Week 2.
Jack Hanley, Peoria Notre Dame
The 5-foot-10, 175-pound senior running back has been the featured for the Irish (4-3), who host St. Louis Christian Brothers this week. Hanley has had multiple touchdown games including three against Manual in Week 6. He also put up 227 yards on 12 carries, plus three TDs against Richwoods in Week 4.
Evan Keil, Metamora
The 5-foot-10, 190-pound senior running back is the leading rusher for a 5-2 Redbird squad that features five backs with at least 140 yards. Keil has 692 yards and 11 TDs, rushing for 7.5 yards a carry. He's rushed for 106 yards against Pekin, while gaining 121 yards on the ground against Morton.
Hunter Reed, Washington
The 5-foot-11, 180-pound senior running back has stepped in quite nicely for last season's player of the year Kainon McQueary. Reed is leading the Panthers (5-2) with 969 rushing yards and 14 TDs, while rushing for 7.4 yards a carry. He's coming off a monster game against Dunlap, rushing for 228 yards and four TDs.
Mack Sutter, Dunlap
The 6-foot-6, 225-pound junior tight end is playing at a high level as a four-star recruit. Sutter has posted a team-high 26 receptions to go with 385 yards and six TDs for the Eagles (5-2). He's also been a monster on defense, recording five sacks, three forced fumbles, an interception and a defensive TD.
Lane Wheelwright, Farmington
The 6-foot-1, 185-pound senior quarterback has led the undefeated Farmers (7-0) to a No. 2 ranking in Class 2A. He's thrown for 1,565 yards with 20 touchdowns and six interceptions including 11 scores and 792 yards to wide receiver Jack Gronewold. Wheelwright has also added 312 rushing yards and six TDs.
Jake Williams, Princeville
The 6-foot, 160-pound senior quarterback guides the Princeville offense. He's completed 62 percent of his passes (75-for-121), posting 1,381 yards and 22 TDs to go with four interceptions. Williams, who also has three rushing scores, has found receivers Hunter Johnson (639 yards, 9 TDs) and Jett Benningfield (364 yards, 8 TDs) for a combined 44 catches.
Bo Windish, Elmwood/Brimfield
The 5-foot-11, 175-pound senior running back/linebacker is the Peoria-area's small-school leading rusher. His 1,274 yards on 141 carries give him 9.0 yards a rush, while putting up 182.0 yards a game. He has 22 total TDs (19 rushing, three receiving). Windish also has 33 tackles, five tackles for a loss, an interception and a fumble recovery.

title: Bernie Sanders in Belvidere: Climate change is real. Electric vehicles can help
author: Jeff Kolkey
description: Aggressive steps are needed to save the planet, said U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders when he stopped in Belvidere last week. Here's what else he said.
content:
Before firing up the crowd at last week's "Rally with the Working Class to End Trump's NAFTA 2.0" in Belvidere, U.S. Sen Bernie Sanders, I-Vermont, sat down with Register Star reporter Jeff Kolkey to talk about his views on the auto industry, electric vehicle production, free trade and climate change.
What is your message today?
Sanders: "The message is that Stellantis should reopen the Belvedere plant. The message is that when you have a CEO who makes $39 million a year— 500 times more money than the average automobile worker. When you have a company that's given millions and millions of dollars in stock buybacks to its stockholders, you know, maybe they should start paying attention to the people who have made them that money."
Stellantis says market conditions have forced them to delay investments in electric vehicle production and in Belvidere.
Sanders: "Yeah, well, apparently the market conditions allow them to provide a significant increase in the compensation package of the CEO up to $39 million. The market conditions allow them to give millions of dollars in stock buybacks. So look, it's a question of priorities. Do you have a company which is only interested in the well-being of its CEO and the well-being of its stockholders? Or do you have a company which gives a damn about its workers?"
Do you agree with those who view excessive government electric vehicle incentives and carbon reduction requirements as interfering with the auto market?
Sanders: "I'll tell you how I view it. I view what I saw in Florida the other day — North Carolina the week earlier. I view what every scientist who studies the issue tells us: Climate change is real, it is causing devastating harm in the United States and in countries around the world. And if we are concerned about our kids and future generations, we are going to have to move aggressively to transform our energy system and save the planet."
"Donald Trump thinks that climate change is a hoax. That's not only crazy, that is not only defying what virtually every scientist says, it is so dangerous because if we don't get a handle on climate change by transforming our energy system — and electric cars are one way we do that — the planet will be increasingly uninhabitable."
So the transition to more electric vehicles may cause some economic hardship but must be done?
Sanders: "Climate change is causing economic issues. Hurricane Milton and Helene are going to cost billions and billions of your taxpayer dollars. My state of Vermont has been hit with more natural disasters in the last couple of years that we have in the last hundred years at great expense. If we are going to in the long run save money by protecting the planet and ending these extreme weather disturbances, we're going to have to transform our energy system and electric cars are one, just one thing that we got to do."
Why have you long opposed free trade agreements like NAFTA and the successor that President Trump negotiated, the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement or USMCA?
Sanders: "Anybody who studied the issue understands that these so-called free trade agreements, both with NAFTA and permanent normal trade relations with China, they're designed for one purpose and that is to make it easier for large corporations to shut down plants in America, stop having to pay workers here, union workers or non union workers, decent wages and then move to countries like Mexico and China, where you can pay people very, very low wages. That's all. It's not complicated. Why, if I'm a CEO of a large corporation, do I want to pay you 30 bucks an hour, when I can pay her two bucks an hour?"

title: School records and state qualifiers: Vote for Journal Star athlete of the week for Oct. 7-12
author: Peoria Journal Star
description: Nominees from Washington, Dunlap and Limestone are among the choices for Journal Star high school athlete of the week. Vote in the poll now.
content:
After plenty of solid fall sports performers over the last week, here are the Journal Star high school athlete of the week nominees for Oct. 7-12.
Head to pjstar.com/sports to vote. The poll closes at noon Friday. Information about the nominees is below.
If you have a nominee for the honor, email us at sports@pjstar.com or tag us on Twitter @pjstarsports. Last week, Kaitlyn Anderson of the Henry volleyball team was named JS athlete of the week.
Devin Miller, Washington football
Miller used his leg to set a new school record in Friday's 31-10 win over Dunlap. The junior kicker hit a 52-yard field goal as the first-half ended to put the Panthers ahead 17-3 at halftime. He added a 5-for-5 effort on extra points.
Jett Benningfield, Princeville football
Benningfield scored every time he touched the ball in Friday's 33-22 win over previously unbeaten Stark County. The junior wide receiver hooked up with quarterback Jake Williams three times for 71 yards. Those trio of catches all resulted in touchdowns for the Princes (7-0).
Mia Lamberti, Limestone volleyball
Lamberti has become a staple on the ballot, especially after this past week's performances. The sophomore helped the Rockets go 5-0 at the Quincy Tournament on Saturday. She complied 63 kills on a .313 hitting percentage, while adding 64 assists and 10 aces. Her performance in Thursday's three-set win over Washington included 16 kills, after a near triple-double — nine kills, nine assists and nine aces — in last Tuesday's loss to Dunlap.
Caroline Keutzer, Princeton volleyball
The junior turned in a big Saturday to help the Tigers win their own tournament. Keutzer was named tournament MVP following Princeton's 4-0 day. She posted 19 kills, eight digs and eight aces on the day. Teammate Keighley Davis was also named all-tournament team. Keutzer also had big matches in wins over Illinois Valley Central (six kills, four digs) last Monday and Kewanee (10 kills, five digs) this past Tuesday.
Audrey Sanders, Peoria Christian volleyball
Sanders anchored the defense as PCS claimed the Inter-County Athletic Conference consolation championship on Saturday. The junior libero posted a perfect service, tallying 65 serves with no errors and nine aces. In tourney play, she had 40 total digs, including 19 in a win over ROWVA/Williamsfield. Sanders holds the PCS school record for career serves, posting a 97% mark — 833-for-857 — in three years on varsity.
Maxwell Kirby, Peoria Notre Dame boys cross country
Kirby dominated in last Monday's triangular meet with Illini Bluffs and East Peoria at The Yeti Cross Country Course at Donovan Park in Peoria. The sophomore ran the 5,000-meter route in 17:35.8, coming in 25.7 seconds ahead of runner-up and teammate Dax Duff (18:01.5). PND won the meet with 15 points.
Sophia Ramirez, Washington girls cross country
Ramirez turned in a top-10 effort in helping Washington win the Metamora Runnin' Red Invite on Saturday. She ran the 2.94-mile course at Black Partridge Park in 18:10.1. Her finish helped give the Panthers (101 points) the team title over Eureka (157 points).
Connor Watson, East Peoria boys golf
Watson is playing his best golf at the perfect time. The senior grabbed Class 2A Champaign Centennial Sectional medalist honors last Monday. He shot a 6-under 72 at the U of I Golf Course in Savoy. The reigning golfer of the year had seven birdies — 1, 4, 8, 11, 12, 13 and 17 — in advancing to this Friday's Class 2A state finals at Weibring Golf Club in Normal.
Leah Brown, Pekin girls golf
Brown advanced to the Class 2A state finals this Friday at the Hickory Point Golf Course in Decatur. The sophomore was lone Peoria-area Class 2A golfer to advance from the Normal U-High Sectional. Yingling continued her historic season this past Saturday. The junior captured the 1-meter diving title at 30th annual Panther Invitational hosted by East Moline United Township. Her score of 432.2 provided the Eagles with 16 of their 83 team points. That dive helped Yingling break her own 11-dive school record.
Dunlap girls tennis team
The Eagles capped their regular season with the Mid-Illini Conference Tournament title on Saturday. Dunlap went undefeated in the regular season, then won the Mid-Illini tourney crown for the third season in a row and fifth time in the last six seasons.

title: Illinois to honor Red Grange with uniforms vs Michigan for 100-year anniversary of legendary game
author: Ehsan Kassim
description: Illinois football will be donning a much more leathery look for its game against Michigan, as the Illini honor Red Grange's legendary game 100 years ago.
content:
Illinois football is playing well on the field, off to a 5-1 start to the 2024 college football season and a top-25 ranking. The athletics department is also doing its part to keep them looking good.
The Fighting Illini unveiled throwback uniforms for Saturday's contest at Memorial Stadium in Champaign, where they will face Big Ten foe Michigan. The throwback uniforms are being worn 100 years and one day after Red Grange 's historic six-touchdown performance against the Wolverines on Oct. 18, 1924.
On that historic day, Grange finished with 402 total yards and scored six touchdowns in a 39-14 victory over Michigan. The ranked matchup between No. 21 Illinois and No. 22 Michigan comes nearly 100 years to the day of the otherworldly performance for Grange. Interestingly, the Wolverines and Fighting Illini shared the national championship in 1923. Michigan will also serve as the defending champions this time around.
Here's what you need to know about Grange and the Illinois football throwback uniforms for its matchup against Michigan on Saturday:
What do the Illinois throwback jerseys look like?
According to the school's news release, the jerseys feature a blue base with tannish gold stripes, which form a pyramid shape and run from the bottom of the shirt to the top of the numbers. The jerseys also feature white numbers and blue outlines. The only orange features on them will be from the Memorial Stadium 100th Anniversary patch, which the Illini have worn all season.
The custom pants will also feature stripes with a tannish-gold hue. To complete the throwback uniforms, they will be paired with blue socks.
'The jerseys are pretty simplistic,' Jake Rosch, director of football equipment operations, said in a news release from the university. 'It was designed 100 years ago, so they were limited in their manufacturing capabilities at that time. We were able to match the jersey design, which is really cool because we wanted to be as historically accurate from 100 years ago as we could possibly make it.'
Who was Red Grange?
Harold "Red" Grange was born on Jun. 13, 1903, in Forksville, Pennsylvania. He attended the University of Illinois from 1923-25. Grange is enshrined in the College Football Football Hall of Fame and the Pro Football Hall of Fame for his outstanding career. He was on the 1923 national champion Illinois team and also won Super Bowl rings with the Bears in 1932 and 1933.
He was nicknamed "Red" due to his red hair and was also called the "Galloping Ghost." Notably, despite playing running back, quarterback, wide receiver and defensive back, Grange wore No. 77 during his career.
Grange was listed at 5-foot-11, 175 pounds by the College Football Hall of Fame. In his first collegiate game against Nebraska, Grange scored three touchdowns, setting the tone for his career. He played only 20 collegiate games but had impressive stats with 388 rushes for 2,071 yards (5.3 yards per rush), 14 catches for 253 yards, and completed 40 of 82 passes for 575 yards. He had 31 career touchdowns, with 16 being from at least 20 yards out and nine from 50 or more yards.
Following Illinois' season finale on Nov. 21, 1925, against Ohio State in Columbus, Ohio, Grange announced he was going pro. As there was no NFL draft at the time, Grange was able to negotiate a deal with Bears owner and coach George Halas. Grange was paid a reported $3,000 per game and a varying percentage of the gate revenue, per ESPN.
In the NFL, Grange had two stints with the Chicago Bears (1925 and 1929-34) and played for the New York Yankees (1926-27). Due to his excitement when he played, Grange is known for "putting pro football on the map." For his first game, the Bears sold out Cubs Field (renamed Wrigley Field later) for 36,000 fans.
Grange played in the NFL for nine seasons and appeared in 96 games. He missed the 1928 season before returning to the Bears, where he continued to play both sides of the ball. He had a touchdown-saving tackle in the fourth quarter of a 23-21 in the 1933 NFL Championship Game at Wrigley Field.
Grange was included in the 2002 NCAA's "Football's Finest" publication, which put together the stats for 3,000 of college football's "finest players and coaches associated with college football." He died at the age of 87 of pneumonia on Jan. 28, 1991, in Lakes Wales, Florida.
Red Grange's stats vs Michigan 1924
Michigan entered the matchup against the Fighting Illini not having suffered a loss in 20 straight games (18-0-2) and had outscored its opponents 443-32 in that span. That did not faze Grange. He returned the opening kickoff from the 5-yard line and scored on the 95-yard touchdown kickoff off return.
On the next drive, he returned the ball to the 33 before scoring a 67-yard touchdown on the first play from scrimmage. He added a 44-yard touchdown run after a Michigan fumble on the next possession. He added touchdown runs of 95, 67, 56, and 44 yards in the first half. Grange scored another rushing touchdown in the third quarter and added a passing touchdown before being taken out of the game.
The 402 all-purpose yards ― 212 rushing yards, 64 passing and 126 kickoff returns ― still rank third all-time in a single game in the Big Ten.

title: Grading College Football Playoff sleepers ... from Indiana to Illinois to Army
author: Blake Toppmeyer
description: Indiana Hoosiers are a College Football Playoff contender, and that's no joke. Go ahead, Google it. And there are several others worth watching.
content:
Show Caption
Indiana Hoosiers are a College Football Playoff contender, and that's no joke. Go ahead, Google it.
In the floplympics, Mike Norvell leads Lincoln Riley and Hugh Freeze.
When evaluating playoff sleepers, Indiana and SMU stand out a bit ahead of the rest.
Coach ' Google Me ' saw a spike in search traffic Saturday afternoon.
Indiana's 56-7 destruction of Nebraska sparked more college football observers to familiarize themselves with Curt Cignetti, the first-year coach of the Hoosiers who's full of bravado, with the résumé to back it up.
'There was a national perception that Nebraska had a pretty legit defense on a national scale,' Cignetti said after the romp. 'So, that will open eyes, OK?'
Consider me wide-eyed.
The Hoosiers are among seven undefeated Power Four teams, and although their 7-0 record comes as a surprise to many, it doesn't to Cignetti, who boldly declared this after Indiana hired him: 'It's pretty simple. I win. Google me.'
More than halfway through Cignetti's first season in Bloomington, the prospect of his Hoosiers qualifying for the College Football Playoff generates some Google buzz.
Indiana's playoff hopes are real, for three reasons:
1. The schedule breaks nicely. The Hoosiers won't play fellow the Big Ten's other undefeated teams, Oregon and Penn State, during the regular season. Just one ranked opponent, Ohio State, lurks on Indiana's schedule. The Hoosiers represents the Big Ten's best chance at a fourth playoff qualifier, and an 11-1 record might entice the CFP committee, as long as Indiana doesn't get demolished by the Buckeyes.
2. The Hoosiers aren't just winning. They're blowing out their competition. So, true, this win against No. 25 Nebraska registers as their best win, but the selection committee shouldn't ignore an average margin of victory of 35 points.
3. No obvious weakness cripples Indiana, and veteran quarterback Kurtis Rourke registers as a trump card.
Cignetti disproved the notion that fans must wait patiently for years while a program turnaround creeps forward. In this microwave era, Cignetti flipped the roster by adding 31 transfers, third-most in the nation. Rourke, an Ohio transfer, ranked as a premier prize, though he is expected to miss next week's game against Washington due to a hand injury.
Cignetti's transfer haul included several quality players who followed him off James Madison's team that finished 11-2 last season.
If you haven't by now, go ahead and Google Cignetti. You'll see he's never had a losing record in 14 seasons as a coach, across Division II, FCS and FBS. He's coached three programs into their respective division's playoff. His career winning percentage checks in at .783, and he's not content with Indiana being a cute October story before fading into basketball season.
'I'm not going to let (players) get complacent, or the coaches either,' Cignetti said. 'I was a maniac in the fourth quarter of this game, a maniac.'
In this case, I think being a maniac is a good thing. I'll Google it, to be sure.
What's the status of Indiana and some playoff sleepers? Here's the 'Topp Rope' view:
Evaluating College Football Playoff sleeper teams
Indiana (7-0): Indiana's schedule could backfire if the bubble overcrowds. The Hoosiers didn't play a Power Four nonconference opponent. Games against Western Illinois, Charlotte and Florida International anchor their strength of schedule. Nonetheless, when evaluating sleeper teams for the playoff, Indiana's offensive and defense balance and litany of blowout victories make the Hoosiers a … Real contender.
Southern Methodist (6-1): The Mustangs lost by three points to Brigham Young, but that's not a dealbreaker considering the Cougars are undefeated and might win the Big 12. SMU should be favored its remaining games, opening a pathway to the ACC championship game. Real contender.
Pittsburgh (6-0): Like Indiana, Pitt is made vulnerable to snub because of a soft strength of schedule. Unlike Indiana, the Panthers win in white-knuckle fashion. Three wins came by four points or fewer. Credit the grit, but brace for the second-half wobble against a stiffening schedule that includes SMU and Clemson. Longshot contender.
Army (7-0): Army's option offense is a beautiful sight. To have hope of a playoff bid, Army needs to beat Notre Dame, win out, and a two-loss team winning the Mountain West would assist the cause. Of note, the Army-Navy game on Dec. 14 won't count toward playoff determination. That presents as a sticky wicket for the playoff committee. Would it risk placing Army or Navy into the playoff, knowing that either could lose the following week and soil the committee's selection? Longshot contender.
Navy (6-0): Sound fundamentals, roster retention and player development still resonate. Behold Army and Navy. Everything I wrote about Army is also true of Navy. The Midshipmen need to beat Notre Dame, run the table, and root for a two-loss Mountain West champion. Longshot contender.
Illinois (6-1): Bret Bielema's return to the Big Ten has been ' borderline erotic,' as he would say. The formula Bielema used to success at Wisconsin also resonates at Illinois. The Illini join Indiana as basketball schools with a playoff prayer. The trouble for Illinois is it drew a tougher schedule than Indiana, and the Illini are a 21½-point Saturday underdog at Oregon. And a loss effectively eliminates Illinois, making the Illini … The ultimate longshot.
Battle for the bottom
Alabama fans ready to punt Kalen DeBoer back to Washington, take solace: At least the Tide didn't hire Mike Norvell. And at least you're not Auburn.
With five games to go, Norvell's Florida State Seminoles (1-6) already wrapped up the gold for biggest flop. Fresh off a 13-1 season, the 'Noles checked out of the penthouse and into the outhouse.
In the stall next to them is Southern California (3-4). That the Trojans lost to Penn State was no disaster, but they also own losses to Michigan, Maryland and Minnesota. M-M-Mercy.
Lincoln Riley avoided the SEC by jettisoning Oklahoma for USC, but he's found the Big Ten to be too tough. Perhaps he should relegate back to the Big 12. If you can't cut it L.A., try Waco, Texas.
Monstrous, cost-prohibitive buyouts protect Norvell and Riley.
That's not true of Hugh Freeze, who eyes the bronze in bust battle royale.
Auburn (2-5) keeps finding ways to lose. The latest: Missouri marched 95 yards to steal a 21-17 victory. Freeze's $20-plus million buyout is a fraction what it would cost either Florida State or USC to make a coaching change, and Auburn has a firm stomach for buyouts.
A 2025 recruiting class that ranks No. 5 nationally by 247sports gives Freeze the thinnest layer of cover. In a time when boosters influence recruiting as much as the coach, are some pledged blue-chippers enough to save a beleaguered coach?
Ask me again next month when we what Auburn's record is and whether that recruiting class slipped.
Three and out
1. Georgia's 30-15 upset of Texas boosted the SEC's quest to horde the most playoff bids. Texas had been the conference's last remaining undefeated team, and even after defeat, the Longhorns enjoy a navigable path to the playoff, while Georgia solidified its footing. Unless the bubble clears significantly, five bids for any conference feels almost out of reach, but the result in Austin increased the SEC's chance for four bids.
2. Coaches will do almost anything to gain an advantage, so how long until a coach reflects on Saturday's situation at Missouri and begins campaigning for a hospital to be built next to the stadium? Missouri quarterback Brady Cook made a midgame hospital trip during the Tigers' win against Auburn for an MRI on his injured ankle. University Hospital is just across the street from Faurot Field. Cook had time to get evaluated and return to engineer a fourth-quarter comeback. 'No. 1 characteristic of an elite quarterback is toughness,' Missouri coach Eliah Drinkwitz said, 'and that guy's got it written all over him.' And a relevant characteristic of any hospital is its proximity to you.
3. My latest 'Topp Rope' playoff projection: Georgia (SEC), Ohio State (Big Ten), Clemson (ACC), Brigham Young (Big 12), Boise State (Group of Five), plus at-large selections Texas, Texas A&M, Tennessee, Oregon, Penn State, Notre Dame, Miami. Next up: Iowa State, LSU, Indiana, SMU, Kansas State.
